Changing Employer IDs on Payroll Vouchers

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Action/2020/Change-ER-ID-Payroll-Vouchers.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Action/2020/Change-ER-ID-Payroll-Vouchers.htm

Changing Employer IDs on Payroll Vouchers

You can change employer IDs on pre-existing pay vouchers with the Change Employer IDs for a Voucher form.

Important! You must rebuild the tax registers after running this process.

Note: Note: This form does not use Client Access Group Security.

To access the form and change IDs:

  1. Click Back Office [Image: screenshot] .

  2. From Employer|Action, select Change Employer IDs for a Voucher.

  3. Complete these fields as required:

Field Description
To Employer ID Enter the Employer ID to which payroll vouchers will be moved. This is a required field.
From Employer ID Enter the Employer ID from which payroll vouchers will be moved. This is a required field.
Tax Year Enter the appropriate tax year. Only vouchers processed during this tax year will be updated. This is a required field.
Rebuild Vouchers Flag If enabled, rebuilds payroll vouchers. Provides two options. You can: - Create New Vouchers. - Update Employer IDs on Existing Vouchers (default): When selecting this option, the system does not include the adjustments in the Mastertax PTS file even if you select Send Adjusting entries for the Send adjusting entries to Mastertax PTS File field.
  • Create New Vouchers.
  • Update Employer IDs on Existing Vouchers (default): When selecting this option, the system does not include the adjustments in the Mastertax PTS file even if you select Send Adjusting entries for the Send adjusting entries to Mastertax PTS File field. | Only Client ID | Enter the Client ID to which this process is limited. Employees are only reassigned if they are assigned to the employer specified in the From Employer ID field for this client. | | Only States | Updates the payroll vouchers of employees working for clients in the specified state. This is the state that appears on the Client Master. | | Only Employee ID | Updates the specified employee IDs. | | Except Client ID | Skips the specified client IDs. | | Except States | Skips employees working for clients in the specified state (based on the main address of the client). | | Except Employee ID | Skips the specified employee IDs. | | Employee Work State or Client Address State | Evaluated by an employee’s work state or the state listed as the Client Master Address. If nothing is specified, the Client Master Address State is used. | | Update Employee Details | If enabled, this updates an employee record with the Employer ID specified in To Employer ID. | | Update Client Details | If enabled, this updates the primary PEO (Employer) on the Client Master with the Employer ID specified in To Employer ID. | | Pay Dates On or After | If used, only changes pay vouchers on or after this date. | | Pay Dates On or Before | If used, only changes pay vouchers on or before this date. | | Send adjusting entries to Mastertax PTS File | If enabled, transmits adjusting entries to the Mastertax PTS file. |
  1. Click Update.

One of the following warning messages displays after clicking Update:

  • If you enter criteria without limiting updates based on one or more state codes and select Client or Employee in the Employee Work State or Client Address State field, the following warning displays:

[Image: screenshot]

Clicking Yes proceeds with the update.

  • If you enter criteria to limit updates based on one or more state codes and select Employee in the Employee Work State or Client Address State field, the following warning displays:

[Image: screenshot]

Clicking Yes proceeds with the update.

  1. Rebuild the tax registers in the following order:

  • Company Tax Register

  • SBEA (if applicable)

  • 941 Register

Obtaining Employee Deductions for Insurance Carriers

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Action/2020/New_Essential_StaffCARE_Custom_Download_Form.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Action/2020/New_Essential_StaffCARE_Custom_Download_Form.htm

Obtaining Employee Deductions for Insurance Carriers

You can download an insurance deduction file for the Essential Staff Care or BIC vendors (insurance carriers) that contains a list of deductions for each employee’s paycheck, such as Medical, Dental, Vision, Life, and STD. For example, this form displays a payroll number for the BIC vendor option:

[Image: screenshot]

To obtain a list of employee deductions, do the following:

  1. Click Back Office.

  2. Select User Roles from the System|Change menu.

  3. Add Payroll Deduction Custom Export to your user role. (See the System Administration Guide for information about defining user roles.)

  4. Click Payroll Deduction Custom Export from the Payroll|Report menu and do the following:

Field Description
Payroll Number/Enter a Pay Date Range Do one of the following: - Enter or select a Payroll Number. A list of clients displays for that payroll. (Selecting the Payroll Number only allows you to use the logged-in client.) - Select Enter a Pay Date Range, then enter or select a Start Date and an End Date. A list of clients displays for that payroll period.
  • Enter or select a Payroll Number. A list of clients displays for that payroll. (Selecting the Payroll Number only allows you to use the logged-in client.)
  • Select Enter a Pay Date Range, then enter or select a Start Date and an End Date. A list of clients displays for that payroll period. | Output Format | Select Essential Staff Care or BIC as the vendor (insurance carrier). | | Deduction Codes | Click the + icon to add a deduction code or click Deduction Codes to add additional codes to the download process. You can select a deduction code from the Deduction Codes for Report Filter list or refine the search, then click Accept. | | Save Deductions | Click Save Deductions to save all deduction codes in the form. In the confirmation prompt that displays, click OK. | | Delete All Deductions | Click Delete All Deductions to remove all deduction codes. In the confirmation prompt that displays, click Yes to delete all entries or No to cancel the deletion. | | Client | Click the + icon to add a client or click Client to add additional clients to the download process. You can select a client from the Client Master Search list or refine the search. (Clicking Client and making a selection overwrites the first item in the list.) Note: Selecting the Payroll Number only allows you to use the logged-in client. | | Save Client Entries | Click Save Client Entries to save all client entries in the form. In the confirmation prompt that displays, click OK. | | Delete All Client Entries | Click Delete All Client Entries to remove all client entries. In the confirmation prompt that displays, click Yes to delete all client entries or No to cancel the deletion. | | Benefit Deduction Codes | Click the + icon to add a benefit deduction code or click Benefit Deduction Codes to add additional codes to the download process. You can select a benefit deduction code from the Deduction Codes for Report Filter list or refine the search, then click Accept. | | Save Benefit Deductions | Click Save Benefit Deductions to save all benefit deduction codes in the form. | | Delete All Benefit Deductions | Click Delete all Benefit Deductions to remove all benefit deduction codes. In the confirmation prompt that displays, click Yes to delete all entries or No to cancel the deletion. | | Save Benefit Groups | Click Save Benefit Groups to save all benefit groups in the form. In the confirmation prompt that displays, click OK. Note: This field and its accompanying panel only display if you select Essential Staff Care in the Output Format field. | | Delete All Benefit Groups | Click Delete All Benefit Groups to remove all benefit groups. In the confirmation prompt that displays, click Yes to delete all groups or No to cancel the deletion. Note: This field and its accompanying panel only display if you select Essential Staff Care in the Output Format field. | | Only include MED, DEN, VIS Offer Types for the listed Benefit Groups | Click Only include MED, DEN, VIS Offer Types for the listed Benefit Groups to only include this type of information for the Payroll Number or the pay date range for the Benefit Groups listed in the panel. (If you do not enable this field, the system includes all offer types for the listed Benefit Groups.) Note: This field setting cannot be saved and if needed, it must be enabled each time you run the report. |

  1. Click Build. A confirmation prompt displays, “Are you sure you wish to build the Download File at this time?” Click Yes to build the file or click No to cancel this process.

  2. After the process finishes, click Close.

  3. If the process discovers data, a file opens containing the requested information. If there are multiple files, the process displays a .zip file that contains each individual file.

Processing On Demand Checks

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Action/2021/On_Demand_Check_Processing.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Action/2021/On_Demand_Check_Processing.htm

Processing On Demand Checks

You can use the On Demand Check Processing form to process and print a check, on demand, for an employee. For example, self-service payroll clients can use this process, for compliance reasons, to calculate and physically print last (final) paychecks when terminating employees.

Important! This process only creates live checks at this time.

After making the required selections and calculating the totals, the form displays as follows:

[Image: screenshot]

Important! For all new functionality, PrismHR recommends that you test this feature in your demo environment to validate expected behavior before processing in your production environment.

To print an on demand check, do the following:

  1. Go to the On Demand Check Processing form on the Payroll|Action menu.

  2. Complete the following fields in the On Demand Check Processing panel:

Field Description
Employee ID Enter or select the Employee ID. If you select this field, the Select Employee window displays, so you can search for an employee ID or name.
Check Date Enter the Check Date. The default is the current date.
Voucher The system populates the Voucher number.
Voucher Type Select the Voucher Type that was issued to the employee: Regular (default) or Supplemental.
Bank Account The system populates the Bank Account defined in the Account tab for On Demand Checks on the Client Details form. > Note: Note the following: - If you do not define an on demand bank account on the Client Details form, an error message displays, “The On Demand Checks account has not been set up in client details. This needs to be completed before On Demand Checks can be created.” - Only service providers can view the bank account ID that displays in the Bank Account field. (This field is hidden for worksite managers and worksite trusted advisors.)
  • If you do not define an on demand bank account on the Client Details form, an error message displays, “The On Demand Checks account has not been set up in client details. This needs to be completed before On Demand Checks can be created.”
  • Only service providers can view the bank account ID that displays in the Bank Account field. (This field is hidden for worksite managers and worksite trusted advisors.) | Tip Gross Receipts | Enter the amount of Tip Gross Receipts to record, if you require allocated tip calculations. | | Pay Period | Select a Pay Period to use in calculating taxes for the pay amount: Weekly, Biweekly, Semi-monthly, Monthly, Quarterly, or Annually. The system uses the default value of the employee’s pay group. | | Deduction Period | Select the Deduction Period for which the system calculates standard deductions and benefits. If you do not select a deduction period, the system does not include any standard deductions. Note: If you select None, the Deductions panel displays. If you select any of the other options, this panel only displays after you calculate the totals, then click Accept in the Tax Calculation Overrides window that displays. | | Work Shift | Enter the Work Shift applicable to the payroll voucher, if any. | | Period Start Date | Enter the Period Start Date. | | Period End Date | Enter the Period End Date. |
  1. Enter the pay in the Gross Pay panel:
  1. — Enter or select the Pay Code. The Pay Description displays. (Note: If you include a blank row between pay codes, an error message displays when you select Calculate Totals, “Please remove any blank rows that exist in the pay or deduction details.”)
b. Enter the Hours/Units Paid.

  1. — The Hours Worked defaults to either the same as the hours paid or zero, depending on whether the pay code is used to pay productive work. You can edit the Hours Worked as needed.

  2. — The system calculates the default Pay Amount based on the employee’s rate of pay and the calculation rules for the pay code. You can override it as necessary.

  1. Enter any voluntary deductions taken from the check, in addition to those for the Deduction Period:
  1. — Enter or select the Deduction Code. The Description displays. (Note: If you include a blank row between deduction codes, an error message displays when you select Calculate Totals, “Please remove any blank rows that exist in the pay or deduction details.”)
b. Enter the Deduction Amount.
  1. Select Calculate Totals to display the calculation totals for this paycheck. The Tax Calculation form displays, where you can view the taxes. (You cannot edit an employee’s taxes in the Tax Calculation form.)

Note: If you did not complete all the required fields and enter at least one pay code, an error message displays, “Please fill in the required fields and at least one Pay Code to calculate totals.”

  1. Click Accept after reviewing the totals.

  2. The Calculate Totals panel displays the Gross Pay, Deductions, Taxes, and Net Pay amounts.

  3. Click Print Check. The check printing process automatically starts. During this process, the system processes and posts the payroll for the calculated amount.

Note: If you did not complete all the required fields, enter at least one pay code, entered a blank line between codes, and you did not select Calculate Totals, an error message displays, “Before printing the check, you must fill in the required fields, at least one Pay Code and calculate totals. Please remove any blank rows that exist in the pay or deduction details.”

  1. After posting, an On Demand Payroll Post confirmation message displays. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

You can access the Payroll Summary form to print the payroll. If you select Yes, the Payroll Summary form opens. (Selecting No clears the form.)

Processing Multistep Payroll Approval

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Action/2021/Processing_Multistep_Payroll_Approval.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Action/2021/Processing_Multistep_Payroll_Approval.htm

Processing Multistep Payroll Approval

Using the Multistep payroll approval process, you must setup a minimum of two payroll approval steps before the payroll is finalized (that is, after calculation). For example, you can use this process so an assistant manager can perform the initial payroll approval, and then a general manager can perform the final review and complete the approval.

Note: As done in the original payroll approval method, service providers can still approve payrolls and override the approval steps.

This payroll approval process consists of the following procedures:

  1. Setting up multistep payroll approval. (Note: Only service providers can setup a multistep payroll approval process.)

  2. Processing the payroll.

  3. Finalizing multistep payroll approval.

Note: Note the following about processing multistep payroll approvals:

  • Approvers who are waiting for their step to become available can still review the payroll approval reports on the Payroll Approval form, but they cannot approve or deny the approval until it’s their turn. (The buttons remain inactive until their turn is available.)

  • Multistep payroll approval is not available for self-service payroll. If you select Self-Service Payroll on the Payroll tab in the Client Details form, an error message displays, “Multistep Worksite Payroll Approval is not supported with Self-Service Payroll. You must choose another Worksite Payroll Approval Type to continue.”

Overview of the Multistep Payroll Approval Process

Once the payroll processor calculates the payroll, PrismHR sends a message to the first payroll approver that the payroll is ready for review and approval. Using the Payroll Approval form, the approver reviews the payroll and can either approve or deny it. If the payroll approval is denied, the approver must provide a reason. (You can view the Worksite Payroll Approval comment when the Worksite Manager or Worksite Trusted Advisor denies a payroll.) For example:

[Image: screenshot]

After the next approver submits approval (and is the final approver), you can proceed to the next step of the payroll process.

Note: For information about how to setup and process a standard payroll approval process, see Processing Standard Payroll Approval.

Setting Up Multistep Payroll Approval

Before calculating a payroll that should have multistep payroll approval, ensure you have setup at least two or more payroll approval steps.

Service providers can setup multistep payroll approval by doing the following:

  1. Enable the Multistep option in the Worksite Payroll Approval field on the Control tab in the Client Details form. After selecting this option, an informational message displays, “Approval Steps must be defined under Approval Policies to fully activate Multistep Approvals. If steps are not defined, this setting will work the same as Standard worksite payroll approval.” Click OK.

  2. Click Save. An informational message displays, “Approval Steps must be defined under Approval Policies to fully activate Multistep Approvals. Would you like to define them now?” Click Yes. (Note: If two or more approval steps are not defined under Approval Policies, the setting works the same as Standard worksite payroll approval.)

  3. The system redirects you to the Approval Policies form, which displays on the HR|Change menu. Now that you have set up the client, the Payroll Approval (Multistep) option displays in the Approval Type field. (Note: Prior to setting up the client, the Payroll Approval (Multistep) option is not available on this form.)

  4. Select the Payroll Approval (Multistep) option, then setup at least two payroll approval steps in the Step panel and click Save. (Note: If you only setup one step and click Save, a message displays, “A minimum of two steps are required for Payroll Approval (Multistep).” Click OK and setup the second step.)

Note: You must setup at least one user with the HR Role (worksite manager/worksite trusted advisor) or A/M Role (service provider) that was selected on the Approval Policies form, so the system generates the approval to a user.

Processing the Payroll

After setting up payroll approval and before finalizing payroll approval, there are two methods you can use to process the payroll:

  • SuperBatch calculation: When you calculate a payroll with worksite approval setup using the SuperBatch form on the Operations|Action menu, the approval is generated after you select Reviewed OK during the Review step. Selecting this button triggers the approval and updates the payroll status to Client approval pending. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

  • Process Payroll calculation: When you calculate a payroll using the Process Payroll form on the Payroll|Action menu for a client with worksite payroll approval, the following message displays, “Do you wish to notify the client that this batch is ready to approve?” If you select Yes, the system starts step one in the approval process and updates the payroll status to Client approval pending. If you select No, the system bypasses the approval process and moves the payroll forward to the next status. You must recalculate the payroll, if you need to begin the approval process.

Note: If the client is set to Wire Transfer for payroll processing, this choice is not available and instead, the payroll advances immediately to Client approval pending status if worksite approval is established.

Finalizing Multistep Payroll Approval

This part of the payroll approval process is usually performed by the worksite manager or the worksite trusted advisor. Although a service provider can also perform the payroll approval, usually that only happens when the worksite manager or the worksite trusted advisor is not part of the approval process or has made a verbal approval.

To complete the multistep payroll approval process, do the following:

  1. The Payroll Approval form displays the information for review.

  2. Review the reports for the payroll by selecting them from the View Report/Analytic drop-down:

  • Employees in Payroll: Lists the employees in the payroll batch. Click the employee ID to view the Employee Details. see Maintaining Employee Details.

  • Payroll Summary: Summarizes the vouchers in the payroll batch. Click the voucher number to view the voucher details. see Listing Details Associated with a Selected Employee Voucher.

  • Payroll Detail: Displays the Payroll Summary form. see Listing Payments in a Payroll.

  • Invoice: Displays the billing invoice for the payroll batch. See Viewing Invoice Details.

  • Gross-to-Net Report: Allows you to run the Gross-to-Net (Register) Report. This report provides a summary of the employee voucher, including all pay and deductions. See Gross-To-Net Register Report.

  • Payroll Register Report: Displays the Payroll Register Report. This report displays information for each employee on the report, as well as the current, month-to-date, quarter-to-date, and year-to-date values for pay, deductions, taxes, and paid time off. See Payroll Register Report.

  • Check Journal Report: Allows you to run the Payroll Check Journal Report. This report provides employee payroll check details. See Payroll Check Journal Report.

  • Batch Register Report: Displays the Batch Register Report. This report displays detailed information per employee for a payroll. See Batch Register Report.

  • Deduction Code Summary Report: Displays the Deduction Code Summary Report. This report displays a list of deductions for a client along with the deduction taken for a single payroll or date range. See Deduction Code Summary Report.

  • Client Allocation Report: Displays the Client Allocation Report for service providers. This report provides a listing of client allocations based on the allocation format selected.See Client Allocation Report.

  • Cost Allocation Report: Displays the Payroll Allocation Report for work sites. This report displays payroll costs that are distributed across multiple cost centers such as departments, divisions, or locations. See Payroll Allocation Report.

  • Unpaid Employees Report: Allows you to run the Unpaid Employees Report after receiving notification that a payroll is waiting for your approval. This report displays payroll information for employees who received no earnings in a specific payroll or during a payroll period. See Unpaid Employees Report.

  1. The first approver reviews the payroll (the Approve field is checked on Payroll Approval form) and can either Approve or Deny approval. (Note: If the first approver does not approve the payroll, the approver must provide a reason, then the process stops.)

  2. If the first approver submits approval and clicks Submit, PrismHR then sends a message to the next payroll approver. (Note: If the next approver does not approve the payroll, the approver must provide a reason, then the process stops.)

  3. In the Payroll Approval form, the next payroll approver reviews the payroll (the Approve field is checked on this form) and can either Approve or Deny approval. (Note: If the next approver does not approve the payroll, the approver must provide a reason, then the process stops.)

  4. If the next approver submits approval (and is the final approver) and clicks Submit, the system proceeds to the next step of the payroll process.

Regenerating and Reposting Multiple Payrolls and Invoices

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Action/2021/Regenerate_Client_Accounting.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Action/2021/Regenerate_Client_Accounting.htm

Regenerating and Reposting Multiple Payrolls and Invoices

Use the Regenerate Client Accounting form to regenerate more than one payroll or invoice at a time for the ASO and PEO client types, respectively, and then repost the regenerated accounting. (Note: You can repost up to 10 payrolls or invoices at once.)

Note: Regenerating PEO client accounting is only available for service providers. Also, the system does not currently support reversals in Regenerate PEO Client Accounting.

When you open this form, the system detects which client type, ASO or PEO, is already set up for the client. For example:

  • If the client type is set to ASO, the form displays as follows:

[Image: screenshot]

  • If the client type is set to PEO, the form displays as follows:

[Image: screenshot]

Important! For all new functionality, PrismHR recommends that you test these processes in your demo environment to validate that your specific accounting configuration achieves the desired result before processing in your production environment.

Note: Note the following pre-conditions that must exist before you can regenerate client accounting:

  • You must set up an existing ASO or PEO client type that has an ASO or PEO Client Accounting setup.

  • Client Accounting setup must have a selected output type.

  • Payrolls must be posted with an existing account setup.

  • You have the ability to make changes to an ASO or PEO accounting configuration.

  • You must run the regenerate process to update existing billing vouchers and invoices with new accounting information.

To regenerate and repost multiple payrolls, do the following:

  1. On the Payroll|Action menu, select Regenerate Client Accounting.

  2. Do the following based on the selected client type:

Client Type Action
ASO 1. Select Payroll Number. The Select Payroll Batches list displays. 2. Enter a payroll number or select up to 10 payroll numbers from the list that displays. The multi-value selector moves the selection to the Selected Payroll Batches list. (Note: After you select a payroll number, the system dims it.) In addition, you can do the following: - To add all the displayed payroll numbers, click Add All. - To remove all the payroll numbers that display in the Selected Payroll Batches list, click Remove All. Note: If you select more than 10 payrolls, a message displays: “<number> payrolls selected only 10 payrolls can be reposted at once.”
  1. Select Payroll Number. The Select Payroll Batches list displays.
  2. Enter a payroll number or select up to 10 payroll numbers from the list that displays. The multi-value selector moves the selection to the Selected Payroll Batches list. (Note: After you select a payroll number, the system dims it.) In addition, you can do the following:
  • To add all the displayed payroll numbers, click Add All.
  • To remove all the payroll numbers that display in the Selected Payroll Batches list, click Remove All. | PEO | 1. Select Invoice Number. The Select Client Invoices list displays. 2. Enter an invoice number or select up to 10 invoice numbers from the list that displays. The multi-value selector moves the selection to the Selected Client Invoices list. (Note: After you select an invoice number, the system dims it.) In addition, you can do the following: - To add all the displayed invoice numbers, click Add All. - To remove all the invoice numbers that display in the Selected Client Invoices list, click Remove All. Note: If you select more than 10 invoices, a message displays: “You can only regenerate accounting for up to 10 invoices at a time.” |
  1. Select Invoice Number. The Select Client Invoices list displays.
  2. Enter an invoice number or select up to 10 invoice numbers from the list that displays. The multi-value selector moves the selection to the Selected Client Invoices list. (Note: After you select an invoice number, the system dims it.) In addition, you can do the following:
  • To add all the displayed invoice numbers, click Add All.
  • To remove all the invoice numbers that display in the Selected Client Invoices list, click Remove All.

  1. Click Done.

  2. Click Regenerate & Repost Accounting. A confirmation message displays: “This will regenerate the client accounting for <client>. Are you sure you want to proceed?” Click Yes to proceed. The process begins and displays each payroll or invoice number as they are regenerated and reposted. “Complete” displays when the process finishes.

Note: The regenerate process runs for each payroll or invoice number you selected in the Select Invoices to Regenerate panel (see step 2).

  1. The client accounting download process runs automatically after the regenerate process finishes. A window with the client accounting file displays. Click the client accounting download file that displays on the bottom-left side of the window and note the following:

  • If you ran the regenerate and recalculate process for a single payroll or invoice, a single file opens in Excel.

  • If you ran the regenerate and recalculate process for multiple payrolls or invoices, a zip file displays in Excel that contains compressed individual files for each payroll or invoice.

  • After regenerating client accounting, the system adds a copy of the regenerated client accounting download file into the payroll history/payroll reports process. Note the following:

  • When regenerating accounting for a client using PEO accounting when the Name of Output File field contains an entry in the PEO Client Accounting form, the new accounting download displays in the Payroll Reports form for the payroll that you regenerate. (The system does not send a file to Payroll Reports if there is no entry in the Name of Output File field.)

  • When regenerating accounting for a client using ASO accounting when the Name of Output File field contains an entry in the ASO Global G/L Account Setup form, the new accounting download displays in the Payroll Reports form for the payroll that you regenerate. (The system does not send a file to Payroll Reports if there is no entry in the Name of Output File field.)

  • The file name of the regenerated file in the Payroll Reports form begins with “Regen -” and is followed by the client’s naming convention.

  • The system adds the new version of the file with an increasing number at the end of the file name for any subsequent regenerations.

As a result of this process, the updated regenerated accounting values for each select payroll or invoice number display in the Accounting tab on the Employee Voucher form in the employee’s payroll voucher or invoice in the Company Accounting panel.

Viewing Payroll Reports and Downloadable Output Files

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Action/Approval_Payroll_Reports.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Action/Approval_Payroll_Reports.htm

Viewing Payroll Reports and Downloadable Output Files

Selecting Approval Payroll Reports from the View Report/Analytic drop-down on the Payroll Approvals form opens the Approval Payroll Reports form, which lists all the available payroll approval reports and downloadable files for completed payrolls. Click the Open File icon (

[Image: screenshot]

) in the Job column to view the report or downloadable file listed in the Report Title column. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Moving your cursor over the Open File icon displays “Open File.”

For example, clicking the Open File icon in the Gross-To-Net Report row opens that report:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Note the following:

  • You can only access the Approval Payroll Reports form from the Payroll Approval form. (You cannot use the Search menu to access this form.)

  • Reports only display for completed payrolls:

  • If a payroll is in Pending (AP.PEND) status, no reports display in the Payroll Reports form when you select the Reports icon ( [Image: screenshot] ) in the Payroll Summary form.

  • If a payroll is in Completed (INIT.COMP) status, the reports display in the Payroll Reports form when you select the Reports icon ( [Image: screenshot] ) in the Payroll Summary form.

Approvals Pending

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Action/Approvals_Pending_Payroll.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Action/Approvals_Pending_Payroll.htm

Approvals Pending

The Approvals Pending form lists any pending approvals that are assigned or available to you.

  • An approval that is assigned to a particular user can only be acted upon by that user.

  • Approvals are available to a user if one of the user’s roles matches the role applicable to the current approval step.

Approvals Pending (Assigned to You)

You can act on approvals listed in the Approvals Pending (Available to You) panel.

  • Standard Approvals: see Reviewing Standard Approvals

  • Payroll Approvals: see Processing Standard Payroll Approval

Approvals Pending (Available to You)

To act on an approval that is available to you, “grab” the approval. The system assigns the approval to you.

  1. Within the Approvals Pending (Available to You) panel, click the desired Approval Type. The Approval form opens.

You can click Show Audit History to display the history of users involved in processing the action.

  1. Click Grab. The selected approval type now appears in the Approvals Pending (Assigned to You) panel.

There are two methods available to process an approval:

  • Click the Approve icon (blue checkmark) for the Approval Type you want to approve. Click Yes in the confirmation message that displays to continue with the approval. An approval confirmation displays at the top of the form.

  • “Grab” the approval:

  1. Within the Approvals Pending (Available to You) panel, click the desired Approval Type. The Approval form opens.

You can click Show Audit History to display the history of users involved in processing the action.

  1. Click Grab. The selected approval type now appears in the Approvals Pending (Assigned to You) panel.

Note: Note: You can open the pending approval in Approvals Pending (Assigned to You) panel and click Return to Queue. The approval pending item is then returned to the Available to You queue for you or another user to access later.

Reversing a Batch

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Action/Batch_Reversal.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Action/Batch_Reversal.htm

Reversing a Payroll

You can reverse all the vouchers in a payroll batch at once using the Payroll Reversal form.

This is a full batch reversal:

  • All vouchers, including direct deposit, will be voided. Any garnishments will also be reversed. This occurs because any garnishments sent using ACH/EFT are not voided in the system. (Adjusting the garnishment record is a manual process for these items.)

  • The credit will be exactly the reverse of the original invoice; there are no calculations.

  • Any Client Bill Pending transactions will not be reinstated; be sure to confirm them when you complete the reversal.

  • Any manual checks posted during the batch will not be reinstated as open. The will be voided with the rest of the batch.

  • You cannot reverse payrolls that contain HSA ACH transactions. In this case, a warning message displays, “This payroll contains an HSA ACH transaction which will not be reversed with this process. If you have questions regarding this transaction you should cancel the reversal and check with your manager.”

To reverse a payroll:

  1. Select Payroll Reversal from the Payroll|Action menu.

  2. In the Select a Payroll field, enter the payroll batch you need to void. The form populates and also displays notices.

  3. Enter the Void Date (the default is today’s date).

  4. Enter the Void reason. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

  1. If you need to exclude any miscellaneous vouchers from the batch reversal, remove the checkmark from the Include in Reversal checkbox. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

  1. Click Refine/Review Voucher Selection Before Reversal to review the vouchers in the payroll batch. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

If you want to exclude some pay vouchers from the batch reversal, remove the checkmark from the Include in Reversal checkbox. Excluded vouchers move from the list on the left to the list on the right.

  1. When you are ready, click Void Batch.

  2. The system displays the Processing Voucher Reversal form while it processes the reversal.

  3. Respond to any messages that display.

  4. When the Close button is enabled, the reversal is complete. You can close the form and return to the Batch Reversal form.

Note: Note: All dates and times in PrismHR are Central Time.

[Image: screenshot]

Confirming Payroll Voucher Reversals

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Action/Confirm_Pending_Reversal.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Action/Confirm_Pending_Reversal.htm

Confirming Payroll Voucher Reversals

When it is evident that the financial institution is able to honor the ACH debit, you can confirm the reversal of a payroll voucher that includes ACH direct deposit distributions. This feature is available on the Confirm Pending Reversals form on the Payroll|Action menu.

[Image: screenshot]

To confirm payroll voucher reversals:

  1. Select Payroll.

  2. From Payroll|Action, select Confirm Pending Reversals.

  3. Click the Process Item link.

  4. Select the pending check reversal. The system populates the information for the process item.

Note: If the system displays a message that informs you that the maximum days for an ACH Reversal for the checking account is exceeded, then you can choose to either continue or stop the reversal. Click Yes to continue processing the reversal or click No to stop the reversal process and clear the form.

  1. Click Save. The Employee Payroll Voucher Reversal form displays with a prompt to confirm that you want to complete processing the reversal.

  2. Click Yes.

  3. Click Save again. A prompt displays to confirm you want to void the voucher.

  4. Click Yes to confirm that you want to continue. The system displays the Voucher Reversal Parameters form where you can enter the reason.

  5. Enter the reason for the void. The reason you enter, as well as your user information, display on the permanent void record.

  6. Click Accept.

  7. The system displays the processing steps as it voids the voucher.

  8. If the client changes their ACH from Active to ACH by Division and then voids a voucher that does not contain a division, the following informational message displays: “The client is set up for ACH by Division, but this record does not have a valid division code. Manual adjustments to return the credit to the client may be required after this reversal is completed.”

  9. Click Close to return to the cleared Employee Payroll Voucher Reversal form.

Employee Payroll Voucher Reversal

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Action/Employee_Payroll_Voucher_Reversal.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Action/Employee_Payroll_Voucher_Reversal.htm

Reversing an Employee Payroll Voucher

Use the Employee Payroll Voucher Reversal form to reverse an employee’s payroll voucher. You can reverse a payroll voucher if it was issued in error and it has not yet been cashed or deposited.

Important! The system prevents you from reversing an adjustment voucher that was created by reclassifying a direct deposit. (Reversing these adjustment vouchers could create a check for a negative amount.)

In addition, you cannot reverse payroll vouchers when a direct deposit is sent to a check using the Reclassify Direct Deposit form. In this scenario, you cannot reverse these types of adjustment vouchers using the Employee Payroll Voucher Reversal form. If you try to perform this function a message displays, “You may not reverse this adjustment voucher.”

When you void the original voucher in this scenario, the following happens:

  • The system also voids the adjustment voucher created by sending a deposit to a check. A warning message displays to alert you while the system validates the voucher number, “This voucher had an adjustment voucher created by sending direct deposits to a check. If you void this voucher then the other voucher will be voided also.”

  • If all the ACH deposits were sent to a check, then the system does not prompt you to draft from the employee’s account. However, if only some of the ACH deposits were sent to a check, then the system prompts you about reversing the remaining deposits, “This voucher contains ACH items, some of which were converted to a check. Reverse the remaining ACH amounts (drafted from the employee’s account)?” If you select Yes, the system creates an ACH journal after the voucher is voided to recover the amount of the deposit that was not sent to a check.

  • If you choose to draft the remaining deposits from the employee, the system prompts whether you want to put the reversal on hold pending recovery of the ACH. If you select Yes, the system does not post the reversal for the original voucher and does not create the reversals for the adjustment voucher until later when you confirm the pending reversal.

Note: The process to reverse a payroll uses the same method described above, but the system does not provide any prompting.

[Image: screenshot]

To reverse an employee’s payroll voucher, do the following:

  1. Go to the Payroll|Action menu and select Employee Payroll Voucher Reversal.

  2. Enter a voucher number from any year or select the Voucher Number. Note the following:

  • Vouchers from the current year display in the Search list when you select Voucher Number. To display vouchers from a previous year, select a year in the Pay Period field and then click Search.

  • To reverse a voucher for a previous year, you must manually enter the Voucher Number.

  • If the system displays a message that informs you that the date was changed to today, click OK.

  • If you select a voucher from a different quarter, the system warns you when it changes the void date to today. This is because there can be tax implications. Click OK, then proceed.

  • If you selected a voucher than includes ACH direct deposit, the system asks you for additional information; see Reversing a Voucher that Includes ACH.

  • If the system displays a message that informs you that the maximum days for an ACH Reversal for the checking account is exceeded, then you can choose to either continue or stop the reversal. Click Yes to continue processing the reversal or click No to stop the reversal process and clear the form.

  • If you are in different time zones when processing voids, you can enable the system-level custom feature code, UNRESTRICT-VOID-DATE, to edit the Reversal/Void Date. (See Using Custom Feature Codes.)

Important! This is a global setting, so if you enable the UNRESTRICT-VOID-DATE custom feature code it impacts the Reversal/Void Date field for all users who have access to process voids.

Note: Note the following if you enable the UNRESTRICT-VOID-DATE custom feature code:

  • After you either dismiss or accept any prompts that are part of the standard voucher reversal, the Reversal/Void Date is available for editing.

  • If you select a voucher with a current or future pay date, the Reversal/Void Date is available for editing.

  1. If today’s date is not the same as the voucher pay date, the Voucher Reversal Parameters form opens where you confirm the reversal date.

[Image: screenshot]

  1. Indicate whether the system should use Today or the Pay Date as the date for the reversal.

  2. Click Accept.

  3. Click Save. The system prompts you to confirm that you want to void the voucher.

  4. Click Yes to confirm that you want to continue. The system displays the Voucher Reversal Parameters form where you can enter the reason.

  5. Enter the reason for the void. The reason you enter, as well as your user information, display on the permanent void record.

  6. Click Accept.

  7. The system displays the processing steps as it voids the voucher.

  8. If the client changes their ACH from Active to ACH by Division and then voids a voucher that does not contain a division, the following informational message displays: “The client is set up for ACH by Division, but this record does not have a valid division code. Manual adjustments to return the credit to the client may be required after this reversal is completed.”

  9. Click Close to return to the cleared Employee Payroll Voucher Reversal form.

Receiving an Employee Payroll Voucher Reversal Notification

After an Employee Payroll Voucher Reversal is complete and the Client Control for Payroll Finalization Notification is set to Email, the system notifies the user at the email address indicated in the Payroll Finalization email and for worksite managers/worksite trusted advisors with the Payroll Approver H/R Role that the reversal is complete and displays the invoice from the reversal.

Note: The system sends the Payroll Finalization email to worksite managers and worksite trusted advisors designated with the Payroll Approver Human Resource Role on the Users form, including any email addresses listed in the Additional Notification Emails panel on the Control tab in the Client Details form (the Additional Notification Emails panel displays when you select the Email option).

Reversing a Voucher that Includes ACH

  1. The system displays a message that reads: “This voucher contains ACH items. Reverse the ACH amounts (drafted from the employee’s account)?”

  • Click Yes. Proceed to step 2.

  • Click No to return to the Reverse Employee Voucher form.

  1. The system displays a message that reads: “Do you want to HOLD completion of this reversal until the ACH clears?”

  • Click Yes if you do not want the system to process the ACH reversal until someone confirms it.

  • Click No if the system should go ahead and create the ACH debit. The system will issue it during the next electronic transfer.

  1. Click Save in the Reverse Employee Voucher form. Continue with the normal procedure for entering a payroll voucher reversal:

  2. Click Yes to confirm that you want to continue. The system displays the Voucher Reversal Parameters form where you can enter the reason.

  4. Click Accept.

  5. The system displays the processing steps as it voids the voucher.

  6. If the client changes their ACH from Active to ACH by Division and then voids a voucher that does not contain a division, the following informational message displays: “The client is set up for ACH by Division, but this record does not have a valid division code. Tracking Payments to Employees

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Action/Manual_Check_Entry.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Action/Manual_Check_Entry.htm

Tracking Payments to Employees

Use the Manual Check Entry form to track a payment made manually by the client to an employee.

The manual check process generates a voucher that the system includes in the client’s next payroll batch, then updates the payroll registers when the payroll processor posts the batch.

After completing a manual check entry, you can create a zero-dollar, non-negotiable pay stub by accessing the voucher from either the Process Payroll form or the Employee Voucher form. (This feature is only available for new payrolls, not previously processed payrolls.)

[Image: Manual Check Entry form]

Note: Note: Only service providers are allowed to select a bank account number in the Bank Account field, so this field does not display for Worksite Managers and Worksite Trusted Advisors. Instead, the bank account number defaults to 999 in the background when WSMs and WTAs are processing this form.

To track payments to employees, do the following:

  1. Click New to create a new manual check entry, or enter or select the Reference number to view an existing entry. This is a unique internal identifier, and not the same as the check number.

Note: Note the following:

  • If you edit an existing manual check entry, you can click the Show Details button to see the voucher information, which consists of the pay summary, deductions summary, and tax summary, along with the gross pay, deductions, taxes, and net pay.

  • If you enter or select an existing manual check entry that was created by processing a backdated leave request, the Backdated Leave Request attribute displays in the upper-right corner. (This is helpful in determining whether a manual check entry is for a backdated leave request.)

  1. Enter the Employee by either entering the name, Social Security Number, or ID to display a pop-up list of matching employee records. You can also click the field label or press Ctrl+Enter with your cursor in this field to open the search window.

  2. Enter the Check Date. The default is the current date.

When your organization processes the payroll that includes this check, the pay date on the manual check voucher will be set to the date as the payroll batch for tax liability purposes. The period start and end dates remain the same.

  1. The system populates the Voucher number.

  2. Select the Voucher Type that was issued to the employee: Regular, VOID, or Supplemental.

  3. Enter the Bank Account from which the check was drawn. If you select an account that will not credit the client back for the amount of the net check, the system warns you and gives you the opportunity to change or confirm the account.

  4. Enter the Check Number that the client issued to the employee.

Note: When working with existing manual check entries, you can update the check number if it is still in Pending status. (This option is not available if the entry is in Initialized or Posted status.)

  1. Enter the amount of Tip Gross Receipts to record if you require allocated tip calculations.

  2. Select a Pay Period to use in calculating taxes for the pay amount: Weekly, Biweekly, Semi-monthly, Monthly, Quarterly, or Annually. The system uses the default value of the employee’s pay group.

  3. Select the Deduction Period for which the system should calculate standard deductions and benefits. If you do not select a deduction period, the system does not include any standard deductions.

  4. Enter the Work Shift applicable to the payroll voucher, if any.

  5. Enter the Period Start Date.

  6. Enter the Period End Date.

  7. Enter the pay in the Gross Pay panel:

  • Enter the Pay Code. The Pay Description displays.

  • To allocate wages, enter or select the Location, Department, Division, or Position.

Note: The system only displays the fields as defined in the user’s access record.

If you select a field, a list of available selections displays. You can refine this list to search for a particular item.

Note: If there is an existing home assignment for the employee recorded on the Employee Details form’s Work tab, the system automatically pulls it into these fields. You can change these settings by making new selections in these fields.

  • Enter the Hours/Units Paid.

  • The Hours Worked defaults to either the same as the hours paid or zero, depending on whether the pay code is used to pay productive work. You can edit the Hours Worked as needed.

  • The system calculates the default Pay Amount based on the calculation rules for the pay code. You can override it as necessary.

  1. In the Deductions panel, enter any voluntary deductions that should be removed from the check in addition to those for the Deduction Period.

Note: You can add voluntary deductions to the manual check entry if those voluntary deductions are listed on the employee’s recurring deductions or when the deduction period is blank. (This allows you to enter voluntary deductions directly in the Manual Check Entry form. However, the system does not pull recurring deductions into the manual check.)

  • Enter the Deduction Code. The Description displays.

  • Enter the Deduction Amount.

  1. Click Calculate Totals. The system calculates the taxes for this check, then displays the amounts in the Calculation Results form. For example:

[Image: Tax Calculation Overrides]

  1. Review the results. If the taxes are not correct, edit the amounts in the Tax Wthld Amt column.

Note: You can enable the DISABLE-MANUALCHK-TAX-EDIT-WSM custom feature code to prevent worksite managers and worksite trusted advisors from editing taxes in the Tax Wthld Amt column on the Tax Calculation Overrides form, which is accessible after calculating the totals in a manual check entry. (Service providers can continue to edit taxes in the Tax Wthld Amt column even if this custom feature code is applied.) See Specifying Client Custom Feature Codes.

  1. Click Accept to return to the Manual Check Entry form.

WARNING: Once you save the check, you cannot recalculate it. Be sure it is correct before saving. If the check was not correct, delete it and enter a new check.

  1. When you are satisfied that the manual check entry is correct, click Save.

The system posts the information on this voucher to the registers when your organization posts the next payroll batch for the client.

Moving Employees from One Pay Group to Another

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Action/Mass_Change_Pay_Group.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Action/Mass_Change_Pay_Group.htm

Moving Employees from One Pay Group to Another

Use this feature to change the pay group for the client’s employees at one time and update their standard default hours. For example, you can use this feature if the client changes from a semi-monthly pay period with 86.67 standard hours to a bi-weekly pay period with 80 hours. This feature also allows you to add employees to a payroll in progress for the To Pay Group.

Before you begin, make sure the new pay group is set up for the client and that a payroll batch exists. see Establishing Pay Groups.

[Image: screenshot]

To move the client’s employees from one pay group to another, do the following:

  1. Enter the From Pay Group ID that you need to change. One of two messages displays:

  • The system notifies you that employees will not be removed from an active payroll, and states that you will need to delete and recreate the batch in progress; you will do this in step 11.

  • The system notifies you that the employees are not in an active payroll and alerts you that they will not be added to a payroll automatically. You need to do this manually in step 12.

  1. Enter the To Pay Group ID that you need to apply. The New Pay Period displays.

  2. Make note of the payroll batch IDs for each Payroll in Progress (From Pay Group and To Pay Group). You will use these after you run the Mass Change Pay Group utility (step 11 and step 12).

  3. The system displays the New Standard Hours for the employees who will be changed to the new pay group. Edit the hours if needed.

  4. If necessary, enter the New Default T/S Hours for employees.

Note: The system automatically updates these hours in the Default T/S Hours field on the Pay tab in the Employee Details form. (This occurs even if the Auto Accept T/S field is not enabled.)

  1. If you need to filter employees by status, select any combination of Active Status, Terminated Status, and On Leave Status. Otherwise, leave All Statuses selected.

  2. Click Find Employees. The system retrieves the employees who are assigned to the From Pay Group and displays their information.

[Image: screenshot]

  1. Select the employees whose pay group should change, or click Select All to select all the employees in the list.

  2. When you are finished selecting employees, click Save.

  3. Click Yes to confirm that you want to change the pay groups.

The system updates the employee records, including the default time sheet hours, and it displays the total number of employees who were updated. It displays additional information that also applies (for example, the system will not add new hires whose start date is after the pay period end date of the new payroll).

Once the process is complete, there are additional updates that you need to make.

  1. Delete the From Pay Group’s old payroll batch that you noted in step 3:
a. Open Payroll Control (found in the Payroll menu under Payroll\ Change).
b. Enter the Payroll Number.
— — —
c. Click Delete.
— — —
d. Click Yes to confirm that you want to delete the payroll.
— — —
  1. — In the message that asks whether you want to create a new batch for the pay group, click the appropriate button:

Click No if there are no employees assigned to the From Pay Group and you do not create a replacement payroll for the old pay group.

Click Yes if there are still some employees assigned to the From Pay Group.

  1. Add any employees who were not added to the To Pay Group’s payroll batch that you noted in step 3:
a. Open Payroll Control.
b. Enter the Payroll Number.
— —
  1. — Open the Actions menu [Image: screenshot] and then select Add Employees to Payroll.
d. Add each employee who was not added to the new payroll batch.
e. Click Accept.
— —
f. Click Save.
— —

You can now process the payrolls.

Creating and Deleting Invoices for Miscellaneous Charges

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Action/Miscellaneous_Invoice.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Action/Miscellaneous_Invoice.htm

Creating and Deleting Invoices for Miscellaneous Charges

Use the Miscellaneous Invoice form to create an invoice for stand-alone, miscellaneous charges. You can also delete pending records (those records that have not been processed) and process locks using this form.

[Image: Miscellaneous invoice form]

To create an invoice for miscellaneous charges, do the following:

  1. Enter the Bill Date for this invoice.

  2. Select Suppress ACH if this invoice should not follow ACH rules established for this client.

  3. For each event code:

  • Select the Event Code to bill. The Description displays.

  • Enter the units and rate to bill, or the total amount:

Enter the Billing Units and Bill Rate. The Amount To Bill populates automatically.

Enter the Amount To Bill. Typically, you would enter Billing Units of 1, and then the Bill Rate populates with the same value as the Amount To Bill.

  • Enter the Location code. This is required for sales tax calculations. (Note: If the client is set to ACH by Location, you must enter a Location code.)

  • Enter the Division, Department, Shift, or Project information, as appropriate. (Note: If the client is set to ACH by Division, you must enter a Division code.)

  • Enter the Cost.

  • Enter a Comment that explains the invoicing of the event code.

  1. Click Save.

Note: Note: If the client is set to ACH by Location or ACH by Division and has missing or incomplete banking information, an error message displays and will not allow you to save the invoice. (You must review the client’s ACH setup and make the appropriate updates.)

Importing Miscellaneous Invoices Data

You can access the Miscellaneous Invoices import template in the Data Import Tool from this form to import stand-alone, miscellaneous charges data by clicking Import

[Image: screenshot]

. The Miscellaneous Invoices import template option and its tabs/fields automatically display.

Note: Note: You can also navigate directly to the Data Import Tool by clicking

[Image: screenshot]

(Back Office), then select Data Import Tool on the Operations|Import Processing menu. In the Data Import Tool form, select the Miscellaneous Invoices import template option.

Note: Note the following when importing Miscellaneous Invoices data:

  • Users whose user role is set to DENY for the Miscellaneous Invoice form cannot import data using the Miscellaneous Invoices import template and subsequently, the Data Import Tool icon will not display on this form.

  • Users whose user role is set to FULL or INQUIRY for the Miscellaneous Invoice form, but whose user role is also set to DENY for the Data Import Tool cannot view the Import icon on the Miscellaneous Invoice form.

  • Users whose user role is set to INQUIRY for the Miscellaneous Invoice form can view the Miscellaneous Invoices import template for Miscellaneous Invoice, but cannot import data.

  • Users whose user role is set to INQUIRY for the Data Import Tool can view the form and import template options, but cannot import data.

  • Users who do not have access to a particular company through client access groups are unable to import data into that company.

  • You can group the lines into one invoice if they are for the same client and date and are in consecutive lines in the file. However, if there are records for the same client and date that are not next to each other in the input file, the system does not group them in the same invoice because the program processes the lines one at a time.

Deleting Pending Records

To delete pending records (those records that have not been processed) and process locks, do the following:

  1. With a pending record displaying in the Miscellaneous Invoice form, click Delete.

  2. A prompt displays asking you to confirm the deletion: “Are you sure you want to delete this record?” Do one of the following:

  • Click Yes to delete the pending record. (The record no longer displays on the form.)

  • Click No to cancel the deletion. (The delete process cancels and the pending record displays.)

Receiving a Miscellaneous Invoice Notification

After a Miscellaneous Invoice is complete and the Client Control for Payroll Finalization Notification is set to Email, the system notifies the user at the email address indicated in the Payroll Finalization email that the invoice is complete and displays the invoice.

Note: The system sends the Payroll Finalization email to worksite managers and worksite trusted advisors designated with the Payroll Approver Human Resource Role on the Users form, including any email addresses listed in the Additional Notification Emails panel on the Control tab in the Client Details form (the Additional Notification Emails panel displays when you select the Email option).

Net-to-Gross Calculator

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Action/Net_to_Gross_Calculator.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Action/Net_to_Gross_Calculator.htm

Net-to-Gross Calculator

The Net-to-Gross Calculator is helpful when you are calculating special bonus checks or duplicating a check that has been issued manually by the client. The calculator computes the gross amount that, after taxes and deductions, results in the amount of the check.

For example, without the calculator, you might issue a check for a net amount of $100.00 and then guess at the gross amount, estimate the appropriate taxes, and then continue to recalculate and rerun the numbers until the guessed gross amount is accurate (or close enough). Using the Net-to-Gross Calculator, you enter the amount of the check that the employee will receive or has received and select the deduction period that should be included in the calculation, if any. The system performs a reverse calculation to determine the exact gross amount that, with taxes and deductions, ends up with the net payment of the target amount.

[Image: Net to Gross calculator form]

To use the net-to-gross calculator:

  1. Enter the Employee by either entering the name, Social Security Number, or ID to display a pop-up list of matching employee records. You can also click the field label or press Ctrl+Enter with your cursor in this field to open the search window. This is the person receiving the check.

  2. Enter the Pay Date for the check issue date. This must be after the last processed payroll batch pay date. If this payment should be attached to a batch (such as an Other Payments Batch), enter the pay date of the batch.

  3. Select the Voucher Type: Regular, Vacation, or Supplemental.

  4. Select the correct Pay Period that applies to the payment. The system calculates taxes based on the pay period. If you select a different pay period than should apply, the calculated taxes will not match the taxes on the initialized voucher, which results in a voucher without an even net payment amount.

  5. If appropriate, use the Deduction Period to indicate the deduction period that the system should use for calculating standard deductions, benefits, and garnishments. Do not select a period if you do not want to include those in the calculation. (The deduction period does not apply to the supplemental voucher type.)

  6. The Estimated Periods Remaining is important for calculating amounts such as FSA or HSA contributions. It is the number of benefits deduction periods remaining, and the system calculates the default value based on the next scheduled regular batch. Edit the value only as needed.

  7. If appropriate, select the employee’s Work Shift. If the work shift code has a differential that is included in the pay code, the calculator uses the differential in the gross pay calculation. If not, you do not need to select anything.

  8. Enter the appropriate Pay Code. The pay code must apply to the selected voucher type. If you want to add this payment to an Other Payments Batch, you must enter a pay code with a fixed pay calculation.

  9. The Payroll Number defaults to the next regularly scheduled payroll batch for the selected employee. If you want to use a special batch, such as one for bonuses, you would first create one in Payroll Control and then enter that batch number in this field. Note that the system only adds the voucher to the specified payroll batch if you select the Write Batch checkbox after getting the calculation results.

  10. Enter the Target Net Pay amount, which is the final net payment amount of the check.

  11. Press Tab. The system runs the calculations and displays the results.

[Image: Calculation details]

  1. Review the gross pay amount, deductions, tax withholding amounts, and so on.

  • If you want to use the Net-to-Gross Calculator to make a payment to the employee within a regularly scheduled payroll batch, select Write Batch and then click Save. The system tells you the number of the batch where the payment is included. This option does not add the payment to a manual or special batch.

  • If the regular payroll batch that you want to include the payment in is still in time sheet entry status, the system adds it to the payroll.

  • If the regular payroll batch that you want to include it in has been initialized (calculated), then the payroll processor needs to recalculate the payroll to include the payment.

  • Because other changes could occur to the employee’s record that would affect the results of this payment (for example, changes to deduction amounts or tax withholding information), the payroll processor should review the results of the payment amount to ensure that the results are the same.

  • If you used the calculator only for estimation purposes, click Clear.

To remove an item in the Net-to-Gross Calculator, go to Payroll|Change|Batch Payments. Find the item that you want and click Delete.

Processing Standard Payroll Approval

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Action/Payroll_Approval.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Action/Payroll_Approval.htm

Processing Standard Payroll Approval

Once the payroll processor calculates the payroll, PrismHR sends a message to the payroll approver that the payroll is ready for review and approval. Using the Payroll Approval form, the approver reviews the payroll and can either approve or deny it. If the payroll is denied, the approver must provide a reason. (You can view the Worksite Payroll Approval comment when the Worksite Manager or Worksite Trusted Advisor denies a payroll.) For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: For information about how to setup and process a multistep payroll approval process, which involves setting up a minimum of two payroll approvers, see Processing Multistep Payroll Approval.

Setting Up Standard Payroll Approval

Before calculating a payroll for standard payroll approval, ensure you have setup payroll approval.

Setup standard payroll approval by doing the following:

  1. Enable the Standard option in the Worksite Payroll Approval field on the Control tab in the Client Details form.

  2. Click Save.

  3. Setup at least one worksite manager or worksite trusted advisor who has Payroll Approver as their HR Role on their user record.

Processing the Payroll

After setting up payroll approval and before finalizing payroll approval, there are two methods you can use to process the payroll:

  • SuperBatch calculation: When you calculate a payroll with worksite approval setup using the SuperBatch form on the Operations|Action menu, the approval is generated after you select Reviewed OK during the Review step. Selecting this button triggers the approval and updates the payroll status to Client approval pending.

  • Process Payroll calculation: When you calculate a payroll using the Process Payroll form on the Payroll|Action menu for a client with worksite payroll approval, the following message displays, “Do you wish to notify the client that this batch is ready to approve?” If you select Yes, the system starts the approval process and updates the payroll status to Client approval pending. If you select No, the system bypasses the approval process and moves the payroll forward to the next status. You must recalculate the payroll, if you need to begin the approval process.

Note: If the client is set to Wire Transfer for payroll processing, this choice is not available and instead, the payroll advances immediately to Client approval pending status if worksite approval is established.

Finalizing Standard Payroll Approval

This part of the payroll approval process is usually performed by the worksite manager or the worksite trusted advisor. Although a service provider can also perform the payroll approval, usually that only happens when the worksite manager or the worksite trusted advisor is not part of the approval process or has made a verbal approval.

To complete the payroll approval process, do the following:

  1. The Payroll Approval form displays the information for review.

  2. Review the reports for the payroll by selecting them from the View Report/Analytic drop-down:

  • Approval Payroll Reports: Opens the Approval Payroll Reports form, which lists all the available payroll approval reports. Click the Open File icon in the Job column to view the report listed in the Report Title column. (See Viewing Payroll Reports and Downloadable Output Files.)

  • Employees in Payroll: Lists the employees in the payroll batch. Click the employee ID to view the Employee Details. see Maintaining Employee Details.

  • Payroll Summary: Summarizes the vouchers in the payroll batch. Click the voucher number to view the voucher details. see Listing Details Associated with a Selected Employee Voucher.

  • Payroll Detail: Displays the Payroll Summary form. see Listing Payments in a Payroll.

  • Invoice: Displays the billing invoice for the payroll batch. See Viewing Invoice Details.

  • Gross-to-Net Report: Allows you to run the Gross-to-Net (Register) Report. This report provides a summary of the employee voucher, including all pay and deductions. See Gross-To-Net Register Report.

  • Payroll Register Report: Displays the Payroll Register Report. This report displays information for each employee on the report, as well as the current, month-to-date, quarter-to-date, and year-to-date values for pay, deductions, taxes, and paid time off. See Payroll Register Report.

  • Check Journal Report: Allows you to run the Payroll Check Journal Report. This report provides employee payroll check details. See Payroll Check Journal Report.

  • Deduction Register Report: Lists all payroll deductions and the amount the employer contributes. See Deduction Register Report.

  • Deduction Code Summary Report: Displays the Deduction Code Summary Report. This report displays a list of deductions for a client along with the deduction taken for a single payroll or date range. See Deduction Code Summary Report.

  • Client Allocation Report: Displays the Client Allocation Report for service providers. This report provides a listing of client allocations based on the allocation format selected. See Client Allocation Report.

  • Unpaid Employees Report: Allows you to run the Unpaid Employees Report after receiving notification that a payroll is waiting for your approval. This report displays payroll information for employees who received no earnings in a specific payroll or during a payroll period. See Unpaid Employees Report.

  1. After reviewing the payroll, select the appropriate option:

  • Approve: The payroll is approved and will be sent to the payroll processor for completion.

  • Deny: The payroll will be returned to the payroll processor for correction. You must enter Comments, explaining why you did not approve the payroll.

  1. Click Submit.

Calculating Payroll Vouchers

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Action/PP_Calculate_Payroll_Vouchers.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Action/PP_Calculate_Payroll_Vouchers.htm

Calculating Payroll Vouchers

To begin the payroll calculation process, click the Calculate icon (

[Image: screenshot]

) for the payroll. (Note: The time sheet entry must be complete to enable payroll calculation.)

Note: Note: The Security Notification dialog displays if you have made changes to sensitive employee information prior to calculating payroll.

During the payroll calculation process, PrismHR creates a payroll voucher for each employee to be paid in the current payroll as follows:

  • Calculates full gross-to-net earnings

  • Posts any other earnings combined with selected time sheet earnings to one of up to twelve payroll vouchers that could be created for an individual employee

  • Calculates and processes scheduled deductions

  • Calculates and takes payroll taxes

  • Processes any active tax calculation overrides or deduction overrides

  • Creates billing vouchers

  • Calculates accounting

  • Calculates benefits and benefit deductions

  • Accrues paid time off registers, if any

  • Applies FLSA ruleset, if applicable

Note: Note: If the pay date is on or before today’s date, you might be prompted to enter an authorization code; see Authorization Code for Backdated Payroll.

When the calculation begins, the Calculating Payroll form opens. When the Close button is enabled, the calculation is complete. You can close the form and return to the Process Payroll form.

Note: Note: All dates and times in PrismHR are Central Time.

[Image: screenshot]

Note: When your client is set up for Worksite Payroll Approval and Self Service, the Self Service Restrictions are set to either Print or Select/Null, and the ACH status on the Billing tab on the Client Details form is not set to Wire Transfer Client, the following message displays for worksite managers and worksite trusted advisors who are calculating payroll:

To move into the payroll approval status and generate the approval email, click Yes.

To bypass the payroll approval step and move the payroll to the next step, click No.

In addition, this message displays for all users calculating payroll when the client has enabled payroll approval and the ACH status is not set to Wire Transfer Client.

If there were any errors, they display at the bottom of the Process Payroll form in the Errors and Warnings panel. You must resolve these errors before you can proceed to the next step.

If warning messages display, payroll calculation does not fail but not resolving them could cause accounting issues. For example, if the employee’s recorded timesheet hours are incorrect, warning messages similar to the following would display:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: If you enabled the Enable payroll live check calculation warning field on the System Parameters form and the system will create live checks during payroll processing, a warning message displays during payroll calculation, “Warning: there are <X> live checks.”

In addition, helpful messages display in this panel that clearly define what needs to be fixed to successfully process a payroll. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: You can download the errors, warnings, and messages that display in this panel to an Excel spreadsheet by clicking the Errors and Warnings Download icon (

[Image: screenshot]

).

After calculating a payroll, the following dialog displays: “Do you want to send the payroll approval to the client?” Click one of the following options:

  • Click Yes to send the approval notification email to the client.

  • Click No to disregard sending the approval notification, which closes the dialog.

The payroll’s batch status then updates to Calculation Complete and allows users to post the payroll or recalculate and submit it for approval.
