Finalizing the Payroll

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Action/PP_Finalize_Payroll.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Action/PP_Finalize_Payroll.htm

Finalizing the Payroll

When you are sure all the information for the payroll batch is complete and accurate, finalize the payroll by clicking the Finalize icon (

[Image: screenshot]

).

During the Finalization process, PrismHR gathers the data from the vouchers created during the calculation of the payroll and finalizes each item to the appropriate register. The system creates a permanent record of the payroll within its files.

Once the payroll is finalized, PrismHR considers it to be complete and creates another payroll for this client and pay group. The system cannot calculate or finalize more than one payroll for the same client at the same time.

Reports and invoices designated to be printed at the completion of the payroll print immediately to your designated printer. The system sends checks and direct deposit advices, as well as any garnishment checks, to a print file.

Note: Note the following:

  • If you pass the ACH threshold limit during payroll processing a message displays in the job progress window on the Process Payroll form. In addition, the following warning displays in the Errors and Warnings panel after payroll calculation finishes, “The payroll is over the ACH threshold limit. You must clear the ACH hold before payroll displays in the ACH file. Delaying this action could delay releasing funds to employees.” (If the ACH threshold limit is null, the message and warning do not display. However, if the ACH threshold limit is set to at least zero (0), the message and warning do display if the payroll is over the limit.)

  • If you have a payroll where all employees receive live checks but the client is paying their invoice using ACH and that invoice exceeds the ACH threshold limit, the system displays a warning during calculation and finalization. At that time, the funds for the client are put on hold if the fees to be taken from the client are over the threshold limit.

Finalizing Payroll for Self-Service Worksite Managers and Worksite Trusted Advisors

Self-service worksite managers and worksite trusted advisors who are restricted from finalizing and printing payroll can indicate that they are ready to send the payroll to a service provider for finalization when they finish reviewing the payroll.

After self-service worksite managers and worksite trusted advisors successfully calculate a payroll (the payroll must be in INITWARN or INITOK status) the following message displays, “Are you sure you want to submit the payroll for processing?” Make either of the following selections to continue:

  • Yes: The system moves the payroll to the next status and becomes visible to service providers in SuperBatch. In addition, making this selection dims/locks the Time Sheet Entry and Payroll Calculation icons and updates the Payroll Calculation icon’s text for all user types depending on the payroll status:

  • INITWARN: Payroll Calculation: Complete with Warnings, Submitted

  • INITOK: Payroll Calculation: Complete, Submitted

Note: Selecting Yes does not allow self-service worksite managers and worksite trusted advisors to edit the payroll any further without a service provider resetting it back to them to any status before payroll calculation. After a service provider changes the payroll status back to any status with “TS,” the Time Sheet Entry icon becomes available to worksite managers and worksite trusted advisors once again. In addition, if the status is set to TSOKCOMP, the Payroll Calculation icon becomes available.

  • No: The system moves the payroll to the next status and is not visible to service providers in SuperBatch. In addition, making this selection updates the Payroll Calculation icon’s text for all user types depending on the payroll status:

  • INITWARN: Payroll Calculation: Complete with Warnings, Not submitted

  • INITOK: Payroll Calculation: Complete, Not submitted

Note: Selecting No requires recalculation to submit the payroll for processing.

Once the payroll is ready for finalization after making a response from the list above, the following occurs for service providers:

  • Yes: The system automatically updates SuperBatch, so service providers can post the payroll.

  • No: The system does not update SuperBatch, so service providers cannot post the payroll.

Reviewing Payroll Reports

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Action/PP_Review_Payroll_Reports.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Action/PP_Review_Payroll_Reports.htm

Reviewing Payroll Reports

Once the payroll calculation is complete, you must review it for accuracy. You can also review any errors that occurred.

Important! If there are any changes to the payroll batch after it is calculated, you must recalculate the payroll batch to apply those changes.

You can sort the information that displays in the Payroll Overview panel by making selections from the following filters:

  • View: Select the view to display in the first menu. For example, select Employees in Payroll (default) to view the employees in the selected payroll batch. Selecting Payroll Summary displays the employee vouchers associated with the selected payroll batch.

  • Categories: In the second menu, select the category to display (default is Status/Type). For example, select Locations to filter employees by their locations.

  • Filter: In the third menu, All (default) displays all the items that pertain to the selected category. For example, if you select Locations in the category menu and All as the filter, all the employee locations display.

  • Review: Select the review type, which opens the associated form. For example, if you select Payroll Vouchers, the Payroll Summary form opens for the selected payroll batch.

  • Charts: Select a bar in the chart to display the employees in the table below that pertain to that category. (The system dims the other bars.) To remove a bar from the chart display, select that bar in the legend. (The system dims it in the legend.) To redisplay it, simply click the dimmed item in the legend. (Note: Selecting items in the legend only affects the display in the chart and does not affect the table data.)

Reviewing for Accuracy

The payroll vouchers created in the Calculation process are the same ones from which checks will be created. Therefore, you must review these vouchers for accuracy. You can use the payroll batch reports, accessed on the right-hand side of the form, to determine the accuracy of the payroll. No matter which reports you use to review the batch, be aware that some kind of review process must be completed before finalizing and posting the payroll.

Selecting Employees in Payroll

  1. Select Employees in Payroll in the View drop-down. The employee name, employee ID, status/type, pay group, and category selections you make in the second and third drop-downs display for each employee in the payroll. In addition, you can select a bar in the chart to display the employees in the table below that pertain to that category.

  2. Click an Employee ID to view the Employee Details; see Maintaining Employee Details.

Displaying Payroll Summary

  1. Select Payroll Summary in the View drop-down. The employee name, voucher number, check/deposit type, gross pay, and category selections you make in the second and third drop-downs display for each voucher in the payroll. In addition, you can select a bar in the chart to display the employees in the table below that pertain to that category.

  2. Click a Voucher number to view the Employee Voucher; see Listing Details Associated with a Selected Employee Voucher.

Viewing the Invoice

  1. Select Invoice in the Review drop-down. The invoice generated by the payroll batch opens; see Viewing Invoice Details.

  2. Click Close when you are finished.

Displaying Payroll Vouchers

  1. Select Payroll Vouchers from the Review drop-down. The Payroll Summary opens, listing the checks paid in the payroll batch.

  2. Click a Voucher # to display the Employee Voucher; see Listing Details Associated with a Selected Employee Voucher.

  3. Click Close when you are finished.

Selecting Billing Vouchers

  1. Select Billing Vouchers in the Review drop-down. The Payroll Billing Summary opens, listing the totals of the payroll vouchers used to calculate the billing amounts in the batch.

  2. Click a Voucher # to display the Billing Voucher Detail; see Viewing Billing Voucher Details.

  3. Click Close when you are finished.

Viewing Other Reports

Other reports might be available in the Review drop-down, if your organization specified those reports in the Payroll Reports panel in the Payroll tab on the Client Details form. See Reports for information on these and other reports that your organization might use.

Reviewing for Errors

If PrismHR encountered errors during the payroll Calculation process, the

[Image: screenshot]

icon displays. Click this icon to review any messages from the system regarding the errors it encountered. (See Understanding Payroll Error Messages for a description of common errors and solutions.) Once you have taken the proper steps to correct the error situation, you must calculate the batch again. The batch cannot be finalized until the Calculation and Review processes have been successfully completed.

After resolving any errors, you must recalculate the batch.

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Action/Process_Payroll.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Action/Process_Payroll.htm

Processing Payroll

Use the Process Payroll form to enter time sheet information, calculate the payroll, finalize the payroll, run the Payroll Validation Report and the Payroll Audit Report, update employee and payroll records, review/download errors and warnings, and print the vouchers. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Important! The output recorded in the Payroll Audit Report is generated using artificial intelligence (AI), so please review all output for accuracy, completeness, and appropriateness before using it.

Using the Processing Payroll Panels

The Process Payroll form displays four distinct panels:

In addition, you can do the following: - Select Payroll Validation Report to generate a listing of validation errors for the selected payroll number. (See Payroll Audit Report.) - Select the Payroll Maintenance menu to access quick links to other forms, such as the Payroll Control form, for the selected payroll.   • View: Select the view to display in the first menu. For example, select Employees in Payroll (default) to view the employees in the selected payroll. Selecting Payroll Summary displays the employee vouchers associated with the selected payroll.
  • Categories: In the second menu, select the category to display (default is Status/Type for Employees in Payroll and Check/Deposit for Payroll Summary). For example, select Locations for the Employees in Payroll category to filter employees by their locations.
  • Filter: In the third menu, All (default) displays all the items that pertain to the selected category. For example, if you select Locations in the category menu and All as the filter, all the employee locations display.
  • Review: Select the review type, which opens the associated form. For example, if you select Payroll Vouchers, the Payroll Summary form opens for the selected payroll.
  • Charts: Select a bar in the chart to display the employees in the table below that pertain to that category. (The system dims the other bars.) To remove a bar from the chart display, select that bar in the legend. (The system dims it in the legend.) To redisplay it, simply click the dimmed item in the legend. (Note: Selecting items in the legend only affects the display in the chart and does not affect the table data.)
  • Employee search box: To perform a search, enter the employee name or ID, then press Enter or Tab, or click the search icon ( [Image: screenshot] ). The results display in the table below the search box, including the employee name and ID, status/type, and pay group.
  • Actions: Select an option to update employee records, which opens the associated form. The Actions menu displays while Employees in Payroll is selected in the Payroll Overview panel. For example, if you select Pay Rate Change, the Pay Rate Change form opens for the selected employee.
  • If a user’s role is set to Deny for both the Pay Rate Change form and the Employee Termination form, when they click the Actions menu a message displays, “No actions available. Contact your administrator.”
  • If a user’s role is set to Deny for either form, then that option does not display on the Actions menu. | Errors and Warnings | Displays errors and warnings, which helps you address issues that prevent payroll processing from completing. Click the download icon ( [Image: screenshot] ) to download these messages to a .CSV file. For example, a warning message displays when calculating payroll if an employee has a gross pay greater than zero but has zero net pay, “Warning: Employee <Employee ID> Voucher <number> has gross pay with zero net pay.” > Note: Note the following: - All errors and warnings that occur during and after payroll process calculation display the employee’s last name, preferred name instead of their last name, first name, if applicable. (If the employee does not have a preferred name, then their last name, first name displays.) - You cannot process a payroll that contains a deidentified employee. An error message displays, “Employee: <employee ID> can not be paid as they are de-identified.” Remove the deidentified employee and process the payroll again. |
  • All errors and warnings that occur during and after payroll process calculation display the employee’s last name, preferred name instead of their last name, first name, if applicable. (If the employee does not have a preferred name, then their last name, first name displays.)
  • You cannot process a payroll that contains a deidentified employee. An error message displays, “Employee: <employee ID> can not be paid as they are de-identified.” Remove the deidentified employee and process the payroll again. ## Processing a Payroll

The steps involved in processing a payroll are:

  1. Entering Time Sheets2. Calculating Payroll Vouchers

  2. Reviewing Payroll Reports

  3. Finalizing the Payroll

  4. Generating Payroll Reports

Payroll Calculation Logic

The payroll calculation process includes the gross wages and calculates the employee contribution based on the Benefit Rules and value assigned to the Benefit Plan for Gross % of Wages.

On the Benefit Rules form, if a benefit plan uses the Percent of Gross Wages value, then while calculating the contribution towards the Employee portion of premium, if Max Contribution has been defined for any Benefit Rule, then it will ignore the Max Contribution value. You must also set The Contribution rule amounts made by Company or Employee field to Employee for the payroll process to include gross wages.

The logic to determine the Percent of Gross Wages being used is as follows:

  • If the Employee Benefit Rule Overrides form uses the Percent of Gross Wages value, then:

  • the value in the Percent of Gross Wages field on the Employee Benefit Rule Overrides form will be used to calculate the Percent of Gross Wages or else it will use the value assigned on the Group Benefit Plans form to calculate Percent of Gross Wages.

  • If the Employee Benefit Rule Overrides form does not use the Percent of Gross Wages value, then:

  • the value in the Percent of Gross Wages field on the Benefit Rules form will be used to calculate the Percent of Gross Wages or else it will use the value assigned on the Group Benefit Plans form to calculate Percent of Gross Wages.

The payroll calculation is as below:

  • Once the Percent of Gross Wages value has been determined, this value is used to calculate the Contribution Amount for the Employee portion of the premium.

  • If the Percent of Gross Wages value is not being considered, then the Contribution Amount is calculated for the Employee portion of the premium based on the Benefit Rule grid.

  • If the Percent of Gross Wages value is less than the Calculated Contribution from the Benefit Rule grid, then the Percent of Gross Wages is used as the contribution towards the Employee portion of premium. The dependent premium is calculated in full by the benefit rule.

  • If the Percent of Gross Wages value is greater than the Calculated Contribution from the Benefit Rule grid, then the Calculated Contribution is used from the Benefit Rule grid as the contribution towards the Employee portion of premium.

Understanding the Security Dialog

The Security Notification dialog warns clients of changes made to sensitive employee information prior to calculating payroll. This dialog displays when you:

  1. Edit employee information, such as:

  • Email address

  • Direct deposit

  • Mobile phone

  • Employee name

Note: Note: This dialog displays updates made to an employee’s mobile phone number as listed on the HR|Change|Employee Details form’s Address tab.

  1. Navigate to Payroll|Action|Process Payroll. Click the Calculate icon ( [Image: screenshot] ). The Security Notification dialog displays.

[Image: screenshot]

  1. Click View Report. The Security Changes Report displays, which provides a listing of changes to employees’ employment status and includes changes made to any new or existing employee records.

Note: To ensure “self-service payroll” Worksite Managers and Worksite Trusted Advisors have access to the Security Notification dialog, set up the following qualifications on these forms:

  • Client|Change|Client Payroll form: Enable the Self-Service Payroll field on this form’s Payroll tab to set the client to self-service mode

  • System|Change|Users form: Enable the user as a Payroll Processor in the Human Resource Roles panel, in addition to having access to process payroll in self-service mode

Payroll Warning for Flat Amount Creditor Garnishment

When you process a manual or a special payroll where any employee has a flat amount as a garnishment which is not for child support, a warning indicating the Employee ID and the docket number displays, so you can review and make adjustments as needed. For example:

[Image: Payroll Warning for flat amount creditor garnishment]

Note: Note: This will work only if the Enhanced Garnishment Capping field in the System Parameters form is checked.

Payroll Warning for Pay Code Included in Timesheet Entry with Zero Dollar Rate

When you process a payroll where a timesheet entry contains hours greater than zero (0) and a 0.0000 unit rate, which results in $0.00 being paid for the time sheet entry, a calculation warning displays in the Process Payroll and SuperBatch forms. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Note the following:

  • This warning does not stop the payroll from processing.

  • This warning is visible to all user types using either the Restartable Payroll feature or the Legacy Payroll feature.

Payroll Warning for Retirement Plan that has one or more Deduction Types flagged as Prohibited

When an employee is enrolled in a Retirement Plan that has one or more Deduction Types flagged as Prohibited on the Retirement Plans form and an employee’s existing elections in that plan reflect a deferral of the prohibited Deduction Type, then while initializing a payroll for that employee, a warning message, “ has retirement elections in prohibited by the plan setup. Deductions will not be taken.” displays. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Note: On the System Parameters form, under the Global Codes Setup section, if the Employer Match Billing Code is configured and at the same time a Retirement Plan is configured for the Employer Match Bill Code with the Prohibit Billing checkbox selected, then the payroll process ignores the global bill code and does not produce any employer match billing for the plan in the payroll.

Processing Approvals

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Action/Processing_Approvals.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Action/Processing_Approvals.htm

Processing Approvals

When events take place that could potentially require an approval, such as a new hire or a payroll, PrismHR determines if there is a policy in place for the particular approval type.

  • If there is no policy definition, then the system immediately updates the database with the new hire or other information.

  • If there is an approval policy, then the system generates an approval event. If the first step for the approval is assigned to a particular user, then an e-mail is sent to that user. In addition, when the user logs in, the dashboard alerts the user of any pending approvals.

Recalculating Alabama Income Tax Exempt Wages

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Action/Recalculate%20Alabama%20Income%20Tax%20Exempt%20Wages.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Action/Recalculate Alabama Income Tax Exempt Wages.htm

Recalculating Alabama Income Tax Exempt Wages

Use the Recalculate Alabama Income Tax Exempt Wages form to recalculate the overtime payroll wages that are exempt from income tax for employees in the state of Alabama for a client. This process will not modify any existing payroll voucher data including exempt earnings, taxable earnings, and tax withheld for AL Income Tax 01-20. This recalculation will provide a report of the recalculation results. The recalculated values will be applied to MasterTax reporting, W-2 reporting, and Report Center reporting of actual exempt hours and wages for AL Overtime Income tax exemption. Tax adjustments will be required if the recalculated values do not align with the payroll data when it was processed.

The Alabama income tax exemption applicable to overtime wages ended on June 30, 2025. For any wages earned in June 2025 but paid in July 2025, the Alabama Overtime exemption will be honored. Exempt overtime wages earned on or before June 30 but not paid until July 2025 may be reported on the July 2025 Form A-6 or the September Form A-1 if quarterly filing.

When recalculating the exempt overtime amounts for Alabama wages earned in June but paid in July, you may also need to process corresponding tax adjustments. The Recalculate AL Overtime utility will be applied to the employees W2 and quarterly tax reports. The Recalculate utility will not adjust an employee’s taxable wages or tax amounts. After running the Recalculate AL Overtime utility, you can leverage Report Center to review the employees taxable wages with the exempt overtime amounts. This report can be created using the Employee Payroll Voucher data set with the field exempt_ot.

[Image: screenshot]

[Image: screenshot]

Important! Before using the Recalculate Alabama Income Tax Exempt Wages form, you must enable the system level custom feature code OVERTIME.EXCEPTION.PAY and disable the client level custom feature code DISABLE.OVERTIME.EXCEPTION.PAY for this form to work correctly for the client, else you will get an error message stating Overtime Exemption Pay is not enabled or is disabled for this client. Click OK to acknowledge the message.

Note: Note: Client Access Group security is enabled on this form.

To access the form, click Payroll. Under Payroll|Action, click Recalculate Alabama Income Tax Exempt Wages.

To recalculate Alabama income tax exempt wages:

  1. Complete the following fields:

Field — Description

Start PAY Date — Enter the starting check date for the pay period. The starting pay date cannot be prior to 1/1/2024.

End PAY Date — Enter the ending check date for the pay period. the ending pay date cannot be a date prior to the starting check date for the pay period.

  1. Click Preview. A list of payroll vouchers displays that require adjustments for the selected pay period.

If no adjustment is required a message displays, “No Vouchers found eligible for Alabama OT Exempt Pay adjustment.” Click OK to confirm the message.

Note: If you did not enable the OVERTIME.EXCEPTION.PAY system-level custom feature code or if the DISABLE.OVERTIME.EXCEPTION.PAYclient-level custom feature code is still enabled, when you click Preview an error message displays, Overtime Exemption Pay is not enabled or is disabled for this <client>.” Click OK to confirm the message.

  1. Click Download to download the list to your system in .txt format.

  2. Click Update to recalculate the listed payroll vouchers. A message displays, “Records updated successfully.” Click OK to confirm the message.

Note: Click Cancel at any time to clear the form. (No changes will be made.)

Recalculate Global PTO Vouchers

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Action/Recalculate%20Global%20PTO%20Vouchers.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Action/Recalculate Global PTO Vouchers.htm

Recalculate Global PTO Vouchers

Use this form to update any existing vouchers that need to be included in the Flat Amount by Hours Worked Global PTO accrual calculations when enabling Global PTO functionality mid-year for a client. This process will not calculate accruals or create PTO registers. You should use this process when you enable Global PTO mid-year and need to account for accruals in the past. So, when you enable Global PTO mid-year, this process allows the look-back calculation method the ability to pick up the vouchers in the past to accurately represent the YTD accrued balances for Global PTO.

Note: Note: Client Access Group Security is enabled on this form.

To access this form, click the Payroll menu. Under Action, click Recalculate Global PTO Vouchers.

To recalculate Global PTO vouchers in PrismHR:

  1. Complete the following field:

Field Name — Description

Start PAY Date — Enter the starting date of the pay date range from when you want recalculate to Global PTO for payroll vouchers.

  1. Click Preview. A job progress window opens and shows the total number of records to be updated. Click Close. You will see a preview consisting of the following columns:

  • VOUCHER : Payroll number

  • EMPLOYEE ID : The employee id

  • EMPLOYEE NAME : The employee name

  • ORIG PTO PLANS : The original Global PTO Plans assigned to the employee

  • NEW PTO PLANS : The new/changed Global PTO Plans assigned to the employee

  • ORIG PTO TYPES : The original Global PTO Plan types assigned to the employee

  • NEW PTO TYPES : The new/updated Global PTO Plan types assigned to the employee

  • MESSAGE : Any message provided

  1. Click the Download hyperlink to download the above information in a .CSV format.

  2. Click Update to update the Global PTO information on the required payroll vouchers. You will receive a warning message stating You are going to apply these changes to these vouchers. Do you wish to proceed?

  • Click Yes to update the selected payroll vouchers. A job progress window will appear showing the progress. Once completed, you will be returned to the main screen

  • Click No to go back without making any changes.

  • Yes - When set to Yes, the recalculation utility will include the successor wage and tax amounts in the results of the voucher recalculation utility. If successor earnings were entered for FUTA, and you are adjusting FUTA rates, the state will be determined based on the current home work location for the employee in the recalculation process. For example, if an employee has FUTA successor earnings and works in NY which has a FUTA rate increase, those wages would be included in the rate adjustment. If that employee has a home location of FL, the wages would not be included.
  1. Select Update existing vouchers if you do not want to create new adjustment vouchers.

Recalculate Taxes on Vouchers

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Action/Recalculate-Taxes-on-Vouchers.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Action/Recalculate-Taxes-on-Vouchers.htm

Recalculate Taxes on Vouchers

Use the Recalculate Taxes on Vouchers form to recalculate taxes on prior payroll vouchers for tax codes. if

  • it was calculated incorrectly earlier OR

  • there has been a change in the minimum wage levels, which affects all hourly employees whose current wage matches an amount you designate OR

  • there has been a change in the wage level of the individual employee, for example getting a raise or a promotion etc.

To access the form, click Payroll. Under Payroll|Action, select Recalculate Taxes on Vouchers.

Note: Note: You can access historical reports by selecting Recalculate Taxes on Vouchers Report History.

  • This only displays historical previews of reports where Update Tax was enabled.

  • It will also show if any warnings were generated on the Job Control while processing. The Include SUTA/FUTA Successor Wages field should be Yes for this to work.

To recalculate taxes on vouchers:

  1. Select a Tax Type and complete the applicable sections for each from the following options:

  • See Recalculate Taxes on Vouchers - Unemployment

  • See Recalculate Taxes on Vouchers - Miscellaneous

  • See Recalculate Taxes on Vouchers - Medicare

  • See Recalculate Taxes on Vouchers - OASDI

  1. Click Preview Changes - a job progress window opens. If there are any errors, make the required changes and redo the process.

  2. Click Close to close the job progress window, and see the changes in the tax amounts to be made for each employee in the preview pane. Only the first 100 records show up in the preview pane. Click the Download Report link to download this report.

  3. Click Cancel if you do not want to recalculate the tax code on the vouchers.

  4. Click Update Tax to update the changes to tax calculations on vouchers.

Note: Note: When the Recalculate Taxes on Vouchers process is run, and an employee has taxable wages with overlimit wages to the SUTA state being processed that have been backed out via tax adjustment before running the utility, the adjustment will continue to occur. Each occurrence will be reported in the processing reports, on-screen process log report, and the Job Control Status report, including the PDF and XLS versions, with the following message stating

Employee XXXXXX in company XXXXX has 0.00 Gross Taxable with an Overlimit amount >0.00, resulting in a negative tax amount. Additional adjustment may be required.

Recalculating Workers Compensation for a Payroll

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Action/Recalculate-Work-Comp-Payroll.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Action/Recalculate-Work-Comp-Payroll.htm

Recalculating Workers Compensation for a Payroll

Recalculate Workers Compensation (WC) with the Recalculate Work Comp for Payroll form when changes have occurred to a client’s WC carrier, or when accrual rates were not updated before payroll was posted. This process recalculates WC accrual for a single payroll and updates payroll vouchers and employee WC registers. PrismHR includes a process to recalculate WC taxes in payroll vouchers. Taxable and tax amounts are recalculated, and other WC parameters on pay vouchers are updated, such as WC policy and rate.

All the steps originally used to assign values for WC are employed when a voucher is initialized, but current settings are used. This provides a way to correct values that were set up incorrectly for WC when a payroll batch was originally posted. Registers do not need to be rebuilt after running this process, because they are automatically updated when the vouchers are processed.

This process recalculates WC accrual (cost) values and does not impact billing. The rates in effect on the voucher pay date are used. This utility will not change employee information set up in Employee Details, but will only change WC cost numbers on reports run from Operations Management. This data will not flow through to the profit report.

Note: Note: This form does not use Client Access Group Security.

To recalculate workers compensation for a payroll:

  1. Click Payroll.
  2. From Payroll|Action, select Recalculate Work Comp for Payroll.
  3. Choose a payroll from Select a Payroll.
  4. Click Recalculate. The system asks you to confirm this step.
  5. Click Yes. Workers Compensation is then recalculated using the current values of these parameters:
  • JOB.CODES (Job Master Classification)
  • JOB.CODE.MASTER (Work Comp Class)
  • EARNING.CODES (Factor, WC Taxable, Pay Class, Rate Class, Comp State)
  • CLIENT.MASTER (W/C Policy, Work Location based W/C Clac?, Service Type)
  • WC.RATES (Gross Rate)
  • WC.POLICIES (Suppress G/L Accrual, Suppress Tria Premium, Rate Template)
  • WC.MODS (Use override rates)
  • STATE.CODES (W/C Wage Basis, W/C Wages Sheltered, Week ends on Day, Rate/Hundred)
  • LOCATION.CODES (W/C Policy, Work Comp State)

Regenerate ASO Client Accounting

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Action/Regenerate_ASO_Client_Accounting.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Action/Regenerate_ASO_Client_Accounting.htm

Regenerating ASO Client Accounting

You can regenerate an ASO client’s accounting for a payroll batch. You would do this if you need the file for any reason. Typically, this would be after someone edits the ASO client’s G/L setup and you need to update the allocations of the previously posted payroll data with the new G/L data.

[Image: Regenerate ASO Client Accounting]

  1. Enter the Payroll Number.

  2. Click Run.

A message displays when the file generation is complete.

Report and Download

  • To print the accounting report, click the Reports menu and select Payroll|Reports > ASO Client Payroll Accounting Journal Detail Report.

  • To create the download file, click the Reports menu and select Payroll|Reports > Create Client Accounting Download.

Reprint Garnishment Checks

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Action/Reprint_Garnishment_Checks.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Action/Reprint_Garnishment_Checks.htm

Reprint Garnishment Checks

Use Reprint Garnishment Checks when you need to reprint a garnishment check.

While the form allows you to include multiple checks (one per line), each of those must be in the same batch (payroll control number). If you need to reprint garnishment checks in different payroll batches, you must process them separately.

[Image: Reprint Garnishment checks]

  1. Enter each Garnishment Check# you need to print:

  • If you know the check number, you can enter it in the table.

  • If you do not know the check number, click the Garnishment Check# column label to open the search window; see Search for Garnishment Checks by Date Range.

  • You can also select all garnishment checks for a specific payroll batch by clicking the Reprint Payroll Control# button; see Search for Garnishment Checks by Payroll Batch.

  1. Once you have entered all of the garnishment check numbers you need to reprint, click Process.

The system displays the Reprinting Garnishment Checks form. When the process is complete, the Close button enables.

[Image: Processing steps for reprinting garnishment checks]

  1. Click Close.

Search for Garnishment Checks by Date Range

If you clicked the Garnishment Check# link to search for the checks that you need to reprint, the Select Garnishment Checks search opens.

[Image: Selecting garnishment checks]

  1. If you want, you can limit the search to a particular employee. Enter the Employee ID by either typing the name or ID to display a pop-up list of matching employee records, or by clicking the field label to open the search window.

  2. Enter the Starting Check Date and Ending Check Date.

  3. Click Run.

Any checks that match the criteria display in the Select Garnishment Checks list. (If no checks match your search criteria, a message informs you that no items were selected. Return to step 1 of the reprint garnishment checks procedure.)

[Image: List of garnishment checks, with one selected]

  1. Choose the garnishment check that you want to print by selecting the checkbox. You can select only one check.

  2. Click Accept. Continue with step 2, above.

Search for Garnishment Checks by Payroll Batch

If you clicked the Reprint Payroll Control# button to search for the checks that you need to reprint, the Batch Number Entry search opens.

[Image: Batch Number Entry]

  1. Enter the Payroll Number and then press Enter.

  2. If there are garnishment checks in the payroll batch, the Pay Date and Processor display. (A message displays if there are no garnishment checks in the payroll batch you entered. You can enter another payroll number.)

  3. Click Accept. Continue with step 2 of the reprint garnishment checks procedure.

Automating Calculation of Employee Retroactive Pay

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Action/Retroactive_Time_Sheet_Entry_Form.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Action/Retroactive_Time_Sheet_Entry_Form.htm

Automating Calculation of Employee Retroactive Pay

You can use this form to automate the calculation of an employee’s retroactive pay after making a back-dated pay rate change.

To submit an employee’s retroactive time sheet entry, do the following:

  1. Select the employee from the list in the Time Sheet Entry form.

  2. The Detail Time Sheet Entry form displays. Click the New Retro Pay Entry option from the Entry field.

  3. A confirmation dialog displays asking if you want to roll in the previous pay lines, and only paid payrolls will be picked up. Click Yes to confirm or No to cancel.

  4. After clicking Yes, the Retroactive Time Sheet Entry form displays.

  5. Click Retro Pay Code and select the pay code, then click Apply Retro Calc.

  6. The retro pay entry processes, then returns to the Detail Time Sheet Entry form and displays the employee’s retroactive pay entry.

  7. Click Save.

Note: Note: You are only allowed to submit one Retro Pay Detail line, per Employee, per Batch.

Changing the Payroll Processor

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Action/SB_Change_Processor.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Action/SB_Change_Processor.htm

Changing the Payroll Processor

Payroll manager users can use the Change Processor form to change the processor for one or more payrolls.

[Image: screenshot]

To change the processor for one or more payrolls, do the following:

  1. Enter the Company to Move to move all payrolls for one client.

  2. Enter the Processor to Move to move all payrolls assigned to one processor.

  3. Select the Move Type:

  • Today Only: The payroll is reassigned for the current day. After that, it reverts to the original processor.

  • Until Payroll is Complete: The processor is assigned to the current payrolls.

  • Permanent: The processor is assigned to current and future payrolls.

  1. Enter the Move to Processor.

  2. Click Submit. The payrolls are assigned to the processor.

Calculating Payroll Vouchers

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Action/SB_Next_Gen_Calculate_Payroll_Vouchers.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Action/SB_Next_Gen_Calculate_Payroll_Vouchers.htm

Calculating Payroll Vouchers

To begin the payroll calculation process, click the Ready for Calculation icon

[Image: screenshot]

on the ribbon. All payrolls ready for calculation display.

Note: Time sheet entry must be complete to enable payroll calculation.

The SuperBatch form allows you to calculate more than one payroll at a time. Also, the calculation takes place in the background, so you can work on other payrolls while the system calculates the payroll batch.

While PrismHR calculates the payroll, the

[Image: screenshot]

icon displays.

During the payroll calculation process, PrismHR creates a payroll voucher for each employee to be paid in the current payroll as follows:

  • Calculates full gross-to-net earnings

  • Posts any other earnings combined with selected time sheet earnings to one of up to twelve payroll vouchers that could be created for an individual employee

  • Calculates and processes scheduled deductions

  • Calculates and takes payroll taxes

  • Processes any active tax calculation overrides or deduction overrides

  • Creates billing vouchers

  • Calculates accounting

  • Calculates benefits and benefit deductions

  • Accrues paid time off registers, if any

  • Applies FLSA ruleset, if applicable

After the payroll calculation process, the relevant icon displays:

[Image: screenshot]

Payroll calculation completed successfully and is ready for client approval. You can proceed to the next step. (See Using SuperBatch.)

[Image: screenshot]

Payroll calculation completed with errors. The errors need to be resolved and the payroll recalculated before you can proceed.

If warning messages display, payroll calculation does not fail but not resolving them could cause accounting issues. For example, if there are obsolete Position, Department, Division, or Project codes associated with an employee’s timesheet details, warning messages display.

Calculating Payrolls

After payrolls are enabled, click Ready for Calculation in the ribbon, which displays all payrolls ready for calculation (identified by

[Image: screenshot]

icon). For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Do the following:

  • To calculate a single payroll, select the checkbox for the payroll you want to calculate, then click Calculate Selected.

  • To calculate multiple payrolls, either select the checkbox for each payroll you want to calculate or click Calculate All to calculate all payrolls listed.

After clicking a calculation button, the system opens the Calculate All Payrolls form, which displays all payrolls eligible for calculation.

Click Continue to proceed. The system makes the calculations. You can proceed to the next step of the payroll process.

Note: Note: If there are pre-validation errors for a payroll, then the system will not calculate it. You will need to resolve any issues with the payroll to proceed.

Finalizing Payroll

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Action/SB_Next_Gen_Finalize.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Action/SB_Next_Gen_Finalize.htm

Finalizing Payroll

When you are sure all the information for the payroll is complete and accurate, finalize the payroll by clicking the Payroll is ready to finalize icon (

[Image: screenshot]

). The SuperBatch form allows you to finalize more than one payroll at a time. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

During the Finalization process, PrismHR gathers the data from the vouchers created during the calculation of the payroll and finalizes each item to the appropriate register. The system creates a permanent record of the payroll within its files.

Once the payroll is finalized, PrismHR considers it to be complete and creates another payroll for the client and pay group. The system cannot calculate or finalize more than one payroll for the same client at the same time.

Reports and invoices designated to print at the completion of the payroll print immediately to your designated printer. The system sends checks and direct deposit advices, as well as any garnishment checks, to a print file.

Finalizing a Single Payroll

Once it is enabled, click the Payroll is ready to finalize icon (

[Image: screenshot]

) for the payroll.

Finalizing Multiple Payrolls

In the SuperBatch form, some users can select and finalize multiple payrolls. See Defining Users to learn about the settings required to access this feature.

To finalize multiple payrolls, do the following:

  1. Click Finalize All at the bottom of the SuperBatch form. The system opens the Finalize All Payrolls form, which displays all payrolls eligible for finalization.

[Image: screenshot]

  1. To remove a payroll from the list, click the x at the far left of the line. This allows you to finalize only the payrolls that you are ready to process.

  2. Click Continue to proceed. The system finalizes the payrolls. You can proceed to the next step of the payroll process.

Note: Note: If there are errors for a payroll, then the system will not finalize it. You need to resolve any issues with the payroll to proceed.

Viewing Payroll Batches in SuperBatch

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Action/SB_Next_Gen_Open_SuperBatch.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Action/SB_Next_Gen_Open_SuperBatch.htm

Viewing Payroll Batches in SuperBatch

To view the payroll batches in SuperBatch, enter the Pay Date Up To and specify a Payroll Processor. The SuperBatch form displays the incomplete batches that are assigned to the payroll processor. A payroll batch is considered to be incomplete until it has been successfully posted.

To view the payroll batches:

  1. Enter a check Pay Date Up To to include all incomplete payroll batches that require payroll processing and are due on or before that date. The default is one week from the current date.

  2. If you are a payroll manager, select the Payroll Processor. The incomplete payroll batches assigned to that payroll processor display.

  3. To further filter the payrolls that display:

  • If you want to view only self-service payrolls, select the Self Service Only option in the Self Service filter. To view payrolls that are not self-service, select Not Self Service.

  • If you want to view specific payroll types, select an option in the Payroll Type filter.

  1. The icons in the top-right corner of the SuperBatch form help you perform the following actions:

Icon — Description

Payroll Transfer [Image: screenshot] — Displays the SuperBatch Payroll Transfer form, where you can transfer all currently viewed payrolls or selected payrolls to another payroll processor. (Select the payroll processor and click Update.) Note: If you select multiple payrolls and then click this icon to change to a new payroll processor, only the payrolls you selected are updated, not those in the entire view.

Filter Selection [Image: screenshot] — Displays a search form, where you can enter information to narrow the payroll assignments that display. (Enter the search information and click Apply.)

Refresh Existing Filter [Image: screenshot] — Refreshes payrolls that display based on the existing user and selected filters/settings. Note: This filter can also act as a “reset” for payrolls.

Reset Filters [Image: screenshot] — If you filtered the payrolls to only display payrolls associated with a particular step, select this icon to refresh the display so all payrolls associated with the selected filters redisplay.

  1. Click [Image: screenshot] to enter or adjust time sheet information. See Entering Time Sheets for more information.)

Working with the Ribbon

After filtering the payrolls using the options above, a ribbon displays the steps for the payrolls in-progress. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Each step displays the number of payrolls associated with it.

To further filter the payroll display, click a step in the ribbon to display all the payrolls in that step. (Some of these filters can include several statuses, which you can select as a group or individually.) For example, clicking Ready for Time Entry in the example above displays the payrolls matching that criteria:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: A blue selection bar and chevron down arrow display within a step when you click it, so you can easily determine which step is selected in the ribbon.

Note: Note the following when viewing payrolls:

  • If your organization separates the print/ship function, then the service provider with the payroll processor (Print/Mail) role will see the Delivery Date instead of the Cutoff Date.

  • Service providers who have worksite managers and worksite trusted advisors processing payroll using Self Service can view a payroll when the client is set up with a wire payment, so they can quickly monitor when to mark a payment as received so the client can continue processing.

Important! This feature is only available when Self-Service Payroll is enabled and the Self-Service Restrictions field is set to Print or Select (Null) on the Payroll tab on the Client Details form for the client and that client has wire set up for ACH status. When the payroll moves to WT.PEND status in these scenarios, you can view it as a service provider in the SuperBatch.

Performing Payroll Batch Approval

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Action/SB_Next_Gen_Payroll_Batch_Approval.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Action/SB_Next_Gen_Payroll_Batch_Approval.htm

Performing Payroll Batch Approval

Payroll approval is an option available anywhere payroll is processed, such as during SuperBatch calculation and Process Payroll calculation, that allows the payroll processor and client to communicate electronically regarding the approval of a calculated payroll. Once the payroll processor has calculated the payroll, PrismHR automatically sends an e-mail notifying the client that the payroll is ready for their review and approval.

There are two payroll approval processes you can use:

  • Standard payroll approval process: Once the payroll processor calculates the payroll, PrismHR sends a message to the payroll approver that the payroll is ready for review and approval. Using the Payroll Approval form, the approver reviews the payroll and can either approve or deny it. If the payroll is denied, the approver must provide a reason. (See Processing Standard Payroll Approval.)

  • Multistep payroll approval process: You must setup a minimum of two payroll approval steps before the payroll is finalized (that is, after calculation). For example, you can use this process so an assistant manager can perform the initial payroll approval, and then a general manager can perform the final review and complete the approval. (Note: Only service providers can setup a multistep payroll approval process.) (See Processing Multistep Payroll Approval.)

Note: Note the following:

  • Only specified approvers can approve/deny a payroll and view reports. During a SuperBatch payroll calculation, approvals are generated after the approver selects Reviewed OK during that process.

  • You cannot bypass payroll approval if the client is set up for wire transfer on the Client Details > Billing tab. Instead, the system automatically sends the approval notification email after you calculate the payroll.

  • If the client is not set up for wire transfer, service providers can bypass payroll approval from the Process Payroll form.

  • When processing payrolls where the Maximum ACH Amount is set on the Control tab in the Client Details form, the Restartable Payroll and Legacy Payroll features prevent submitted payrolls (those whose status is set to INITPEND), that exceed a set ACH amount, from processing until they are approved by a Billing Representative.

Note: To use the Legacy Payroll feature, you must enable the LEGACY-PAYROLL-GLOBAL custom feature code.

Once notified, the client can log in and review the payroll using the Payroll Approval form, then either accept the payroll or explain what changes are required. (See Processing Standard Payroll ApprovalSee Processing Standard Payroll ApprovalSee Processing Standard Payroll Approval or Processing Multistep Payroll Approval.)

After the client approves the payroll, you can proceed to the next step of the payroll process.

Handling a Denied Payroll

If the client requires additional changes, the client approval icon displays as

[Image: screenshot]

“Payroll has been denied approval by client.”

  1. Click the icon to review the client’s explanation in the Payroll Message. (You can review the worksite manager’s or worksite trusted advisor’s detailed comment on why the payroll was denied. In addition, click Print to view the comment in report format, where it can then display as a PDF or you can export it to XLS format.)

  2. After reviewing the explanation:

  • Click Close. You can return to handle the issue at a later time.

  • Click Reset Payroll. The payroll returns to the Ready to Calculate status, so that you can make any changes that are required.

  1. After you reset the payroll, make the required changes and run the calculation again.

  2. Review the payroll reports.

  3. The client will review the payroll again.

  • If the client rejects the changed payroll, return to step 1.

  • If the client approves the payroll, you can proceed to the next step of the payroll process.

Printing and Mailing Payroll Batches

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Action/SB_Next_Gen_Print_Mail.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Action/SB_Next_Gen_Print_Mail.htm

Printing and Mailing Payroll Batches

The final payroll batch steps are to print and mail the batch documents, including the billing invoice, reports, direct deposit advices, and paychecks. The Print/Mail feature provides a method of tracking the payroll batch through the actual mailing of the batch documents. The handling of these documents depends on your organization’s procedures.

The documents for payroll batches that have been posted and have the Status MAIL are ready to be bundled and processed for mailing. Checks can be “set aside” indefinitely until you are ready to print them if your organization prints the checks.

Note: Note: Users can specify what prints for a client during the payroll process on the Client Details Payroll tab.

Setting Up the Payroll Batch Shipping Mode

Setting the shipping mode for the payroll batch allows you to click the Print icon during the printing and mailing process (known as the Autocomplete feature), so you can select when and how to ship the payroll batch.

To set up the payroll batch shipping mode, do the following:

  1. Click Back Office.

  2. From System|Change select System Parameters.

  3. Enter ALL as the Automatic Mail Code. (Note: An Automatic Mail Code is an existing delivery code to set automatic mailing capability when shipping items in a payroll batch.)

[Image: screenshot]

When a delivery method code is entered in this field, the system sets all payrolls that use the same delivery method to Mailed. Payrolls with different delivery methods must have their status manually set to Mailed. For example, if USPS is entered as a code, the system sets all payrolls sent by US mail to Mailed. Payrolls sent by FedEx must have their status manually set, which logs the tracking number or other information.

Enter ALL to set all payrolls to Mailed status, regardless of the delivery method.

  1. After clicking the Payroll is ready to finalize icon ( [Image: screenshot] ) in the SuperBatch form, the payroll automatically completes.

Printing a Single Payroll

Once it is enabled, click the Print icon (

[Image: screenshot]

) for the payroll.

Printing Multiple Payrolls

In the SuperBatch form, you can select and print multiple payrolls.

To print multiple payrolls, do the following:

  1. Click the Print All button at the bottom of the SuperBatch form. The system opens the Print All Payrolls form, which displays all payrolls eligible for printing.

[Image: screenshot]

  1. To remove a payroll from the list, click the x at the far left of the line. This allows you to print only the payrolls that you are ready to process.

  2. Click Continue to proceed. The system prints the output to the designated printer.

Reviewing a Payroll

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Action/SB_Next_Gen_Review_Payroll_Batch.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Action/SB_Next_Gen_Review_Payroll_Batch.htm

Reviewing a Payroll

Once the payroll calculation is complete, you must review it for accuracy. You can also review any errors that occurred.

Reviewing Vouchers for Accuracy

The payroll vouchers created in the Calculation process are the same ones from which checks will be created. Therefore, you must review these vouchers for accuracy and correctness. You can use payroll batch reports to determine the accuracy of a batch prior to posting. No matter which reports you use to review the batch, be aware that some kind of review process must be completed before posting the payroll.

To access the reports for a payroll, click

[Image: screenshot]

in the batch row. The payroll review menu opens. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

  • If you are not finished with the review, click Close.

  • Once the review is complete, click Reviewed OK.

Review the reports, which are described below.

Generating the Payroll Audit Report

  1. In the payroll review menu, select Payroll Audit. The Payroll Audit Report opens, which compares the current payroll against the prior payroll and displays changes, outliers, and potential issues that warrant review. See Payroll Audit Report.

  2. Click Close when you are finished.

Displaying the Payroll Summary

  1. In the payroll review menu, select Display Payroll Summary. The Payroll Summary report opens, listing the checks paid in the payroll. See Listing Payments in a Payroll.

  2. Click on a Voucher # to display the Employee Voucher; see Listing Details Associated with a Selected Employee Voucher.

  3. Click Close when you are finished.

Displaying the Payroll Billing Summary

  1. In the payroll review menu, select Display Billing Summary. The Payroll Billing Summary report opens, listing the totals of the payroll vouchers used to calculate the billing amounts in the batch.

[Image: screenshot]

  1. Click a Voucher # to display the Billing Voucher Detail; see Viewing Billing Voucher Details.

  2. Click Close when you are finished.

Displaying the Invoice

  1. In the payroll review menu, select Display Invoice. The invoice generated by the payroll batch opens; see Viewing Invoice Details.

  2. Click Close when you are finished.

WARNING: If a change is made to the payroll batch after it has been calculated, the payroll batch must be calculated again in order for the changes to take effect within the payroll batch.

Generating the Payroll Register Report

  1. In the payroll review menu, select Payroll Register Report. The report parameters display.

  2. Choose the Selection Parameters, Display Columns, Sort Parameters, and Other Options.

  3. Click Run. The report displays, using the parameters you specified.

  4. When you are finished with the report, close the report and then close the report parameters.

Generating the Bill Rate Report

  1. In the payroll review menu, select Bill Rate Report. The report displays.

  2. When you are finished with the report, close it.

Generating the Payroll Check Journal Report

  1. In the payroll review menu, select Check Journal Report. The report parameters display.

  2. Choose the Selection Parameters, Sort Parameters, and any other options.

  3. Click Run. The report displays, using the parameters you specified.

  4. When you are finished with the report, close the report and then close the report parameters.

Generating the Gross-to-Net Register

  1. In the payroll review menu, select Gross-to-Net Register. The report parameters display.

  2. Choose the Selection Parameters and the value to Sort By.

  3. Click Run. The report displays, using the parameters you specified.

  4. When you are finished with the report, close the report and then close the report parameters.

Generating the Client Allocation Report

  1. In the payroll review menu, select Client Allocation Report. The report parameters display.

  2. Choose the Selection Parameters.

  3. Click Run. The report displays, using the parameters you specified.

  4. When you are finished with the report, close the report and then close the report parameters.

Generating the Invoice Variance Report

  1. In the payroll review menu, select Invoice Variance Report. The report parameters display.

  2. Choose the Report Parameters.

  3. Select Invoice Two’s Payroll Number.

  4. Click Run. The report displays, using the parameters you specified.

  5. When you are finished with the report, close the report and then close the report parameters.

Generating the Employee Time Off Accruals Report

  1. In the payroll review menu, select Employee Time Off Accruals Report. The selected payroll number displays.

  2. Select whether you want to Sort By employee name or voucher.

  3. Click Run. The report displays, using the parameters you specified.

  4. When you are finished with the report, close the report and then close the report parameters.

Generating the Deduction Code Summary Report

  1. In the payroll review menu, select Deduction Code Summary Report. The selected payroll number displays.

  2. If you want to run this report for a payroll batch in a specific Pay Date Range, select this option.

  3. Select the Sort By option and the Deduction Code, if appropriate.

  4. Click Run. The report displays, using the parameters you specified.

  5. When you are finished with the report, close the report and then close the report parameters.

Generating the Payroll Variance Reports

  1. In the payroll review menu, select Payroll Variance Reports. The report parameters display.

  2. Choose the Report Parameters.

  3. Click Generate Report. The report displays, using the parameters you specified.

  4. When you are finished with the report, close the report and then close the report parameters.

Generating the Unpaid Employees Report

  1. In the payroll review menu, select Unpaid Employees Report. The report parameters display.

  2. Choose the Report Parameters.

  3. Click Run. The report displays, using the parameters you specified.

  4. When you are finished with the report, close the report and then close the report parameters.

Displaying Warning Messages

If there are warnings in the payroll batch, you can review them. These are items that do not prevent the posting of the batch; for example, an employee in the batch who has no hours in the time sheet.

Performing Error Review

If PrismHR encountered errors during the payroll Calculation process, the

[Image: screenshot]

icon displays. Click this icon to review any messages from the system regarding the errors it encountered. (See Understanding Payroll Error Messages for a description of common errors and solutions.) Once you have taken the proper steps to correct the error situation, you must calculate the batch again. The batch cannot be finalized until the Calculation and Review processes have been successfully completed.

After resolving any errors, you must recalculate the batch.

Adding Employee to Payroll

You can add an employee to a payroll by opening the Actions menu in Summary Time Sheet Entry and then selecting Add Employee to Payroll.

Examples of when you would use this feature:

  • An employee was recently moved to the pay group in the payroll and is not currently included.

  • An employee is in a different pay group but works for the same company.

To add an employee to a payroll:

  1. Enter or select the Employee ID.

Note: You can search for an employee by entering the employee’s preferred, first, or last name.

  1. Click Add.

Making Detail Time Sheet Entries

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Action/SB_PP_Detail_TimeSheet_Entry_Form.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Action/SB_PP_Detail_TimeSheet_Entry_Form.htm

Making Detail Time Sheet Entries

You can enter more information in the Detail Time Sheet Entry form than in the Summary Time Sheet Entry, such as changing position codes or selecting pay codes, which do not display in the summary form.

There are three ways to access the Detail Time Sheet Entry form from the Summary Time Sheet Entry form:

  • Click the name of the employee. The Detail Time Sheet Entry form opens, allowing you to create a new entry or edit any existing entries for that employee.

  • While the cursor is in the row of an employee, click a pay code column heading. The Detail Time Sheet Entry form opens for that employee and pay code, where you can enter or edit the time sheet entry.

  • While the cursor is in one of the pay code fields, press Ctrl+Enter. The Detail Time Sheet Entry form opens for that employee and pay code, where you can enter or edit the time sheet entry.

You can tab through the fields, and press Ctrl+Enter to search for or clear values.

Note: Note: Time sheet entries display on the right side of the form. If the pay code is one of the standard ones displayed in Summary Time Sheet Entry, the date is shown in white. If it is not one of those standard pay codes, it is shown in pale yellow. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Follow these instructions when working in detail time sheets:

  1. Use [Image: screenshot] and [Image: screenshot] to “pivot” to move to the previous or next employee time sheet. From the Pivot By drop-down, select how you want to pivot; the options vary by client.

  2. Make the appropriate entries for the employee.

Note: Note: Not all fields display for every client; the fields that display are determined in the Client Details Time Sheet tab.

  1. — Select the Entry type as either New Entry or New Retro Pay Entry. If you select New Retro Pay Entry, the Retroactive Time Sheet Entry form displays (see description below).

  2. — Enter the Charge Date when the employee should receive credit for the hours worked or units produced.

c. Enter the Pay Code applicable to this line amount.
d. Based on the pay code, the next field is Hours Paid or Amount Paid.
— —

  • Hours Paid: Enter the number of hours for which to pay the employee.

  • Amount Paid: Enter the total amount to pay the employee.

  1. — Enter the Position Code for the position the employee performed; the default comes from Employee Details, but you can change it.
f. Enter the number of productive Hours Worked.
g. Enter the applicable Division code.
— —
h. Enter the Department code in which the employee worked; you can change the default.
— —
  1. — Enter the applicable work Location code; the default is the employee’s worksite location in Employee Details.
j. Enter the Shift or Mileage code.
  1. — Enter the Project or work order code to which to distribute the hours/units and amount earned.
l. For an entry based on Hours Paid, enter the Pay Rate.
m. If appropriate, enter the FMLA Event for the employee.
— —

  1. — Select Suppress Labor Alloc. if the system should not allocate according to the allocation rules; the line item will go strictly to the employee’s “home”. If you do not select this option, the system will allocate the line item according to the rules set for the employee in the Employee Details Pay tab.

  2. — If you enabled the SHOWGLALLOCOVR custom feature code, you can initiate a payment override in the G/L Alloc. Override field by entering the G/L account to charge this payment during pay voucher creation.

  1. Press Enter or click Save to save the entry. The system clears the fields so you can make another entry for the current employee, or pivot to the next one.

  2. If you need to delete an entry, click on it in the right side of the form and then click the [Image: screenshot] icon.

  3. When you are finished, press Page Up or click Return to close Detail Time Sheet Entry and return to the Summary Time Sheet Entry form, where you can proceed with the payroll process.

Note: Note: Any pay rate changes you make here will not be overwritten for this payroll if there are any changes outside of the time sheet.

Retroactive Time Sheet Entry Form

You can use this form to automate the calculation of an employee’s retroactive pay after making a back-dated pay rate change.

[Image: screenshot]

To submit an employee’s retroactive time sheet entry, do the following:

  1. Select the Payroll # in the Time Sheet Entry form.

  2. Select the Employee from the list in the Time Sheet Entry form.

  3. The Detail Time Sheet Entry form displays. Click the New Retro Pay Entry option from the Entry field.

  4. A confirmation dialog displays asking if you want to roll in the previous pay lines, and only paid payrolls will be picked up. Click Yes to confirm or No to cancel.

  5. After clicking Yes, the Retroactive Time Sheet Entry form displays.

  6. Click Retro Pay Code and select the pay code, then click Apply Retro Calc.

  7. The retro pay entry processes, then returns to the Detail Time Sheet Entry form and displays the employee’s retroactive pay entry.

  8. Click Save.

Note: Note: You can only submit one retroactive pay detail form, per employee, per batch. Note that this process is designed to take the employee’s standard pay rate into consideration when applying the calculation. If Shift Codes were applied, resulting in a higher pay rate on the original vouchers, the calculations will notbe accurate and should be handled manually.

After calculating an employee’s retroactive pay, you can view the Retro Pay calculation details from the Pay tab of the initialized (calculated) and finalized (posted) voucher by clicking the Retro Pay Calculation link in the Employee Voucher form. (These details display the same information that displays in the Retroactive Time Sheet Entry form.)

[Image: screenshot]

Show and Hide Time Sheet Columns

Making Summary Timesheet Entries

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Action/SB_PP_Summary_TimeSheet_Entry_Form.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Action/SB_PP_Summary_TimeSheet_Entry_Form.htm

Making Summary Timesheet Entries

The columns in the Summary Time Sheet Entry form display the employees and pay codes for the payroll. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Note the following:

  • The gray columns are standard.

  • The white pay and deduction columns that display are set in the Client Details Time Sheet tab.

  • If you import the client’s payroll information, see Importing the Data File.

  • You can use the Tab and arrow keys or the mouse to navigate the Summary Time Sheet Entry form. See Making Detail Time Sheet Entries if you need to make detailed entries.

Follow these instructions when working in summary timesheets:

  1. In the appropriate pay code columns, enter timesheet information for each employee.

If you enter paid time off hours for an employee with default timesheet hours whose position is FLSA exempt, the system warns you and prompts you to determine how to proceed. Click Yes to subtract the PTO hours from the regular pay hours. Click No to add the PTO hours to the employee. (This does not apply to FLSA exempt employees without any default timesheet hours.)

Note: Employees assigned the Variable Salary option as their Pay Method in the Employee Details form display as “salaried” employees in timesheets. This assignment is indicated by displaying a green dot in the Salary column in timesheets. However, the Variable Salary option only displays if the VARSALMETHOD custom feature code is enabled on the System Parameters form.

  1. In any deduction code columns, you can enter deduction data for each employee.

  2. Use the scroll bar at the bottom of the page to scroll over to display the rest of the columns in this form.

  3. If there is more than one page of employees, press Page Up and Page Down, or click the [Image: screenshot] and [Image: screenshot] buttons near the bottom of the form, to navigate to the previous or next pages.

  4. At any point, you can save your work by clicking Return. The Summary Time Sheet Entry form saves and closes, and you return to the previous form.

  5. Finalize the entry using one of these methods:

Method Description
Checkbox next to employee Select the checkbox for each employee whose information is complete, and click Return when you are finished. The next time you open Summary Time Sheet Entry, those employees do not display until the entire payroll is finalized. > Note: Note the following for worksite managers and worksite trusted advisors: - The system displays a confirmation message only when you check the box for the last employee of the payroll to be finalized and behaves as indicated in the Finalize Page button description (see below). - If the worksite manager or worksite trusted advisor has restricted access to timesheets, they can still use the checkboxes to finalize the employees and the full payroll.
  • The system displays a confirmation message only when you check the box for the last employee of the payroll to be finalized and behaves as indicated in the Finalize Page button description (see below).
  • If the worksite manager or worksite trusted advisor has restricted access to timesheets, they can still use the checkboxes to finalize the employees and the full payroll. | Finalize button | Click Finalize to finalize all employees in the payroll. A confirmation message displays for worksite managers and worksite trusted advisors, “Are you sure you want to finalize and submit this payroll for processing?” If you select Yes, all timesheets finalize. (Selecting No ensures that the system will not finalize the timesheet.) The Summary Time Sheet Entry form saves and closes, and you return to the previous form. Note: A worksite manager or worksite trusted advisor that is set up for self-service payroll processing will not see the message when they click the Finalize button. | | Finalize Page | Click Finalize Page to mark all employees on the page as complete. Clicking this button on the last page of a timesheet that has not been finalized displays a message for worksite managers and worksite trusted advisors, “All employees for this payroll have been finalized. Do you want to finalize and submit this payroll for processing?” If you select Yes, the system finalizes the timesheet and all employees and the payroll moves into TSOKCOMP status. (Selecting No does not finalize the timesheet and employees, and you return to the Summary Time Sheet Entry form.) Note: If you click the Finalize Page button and there is still another page that needs to be finalized, no message displays. | Note: Not all users have access to the Finalize or Finalize Page buttons. Worksite managers who have permission to view only some of the employees in the payroll cannot use those buttons.
  1. Once the batch is finalized, you can proceed to the next step in the payroll process.

Receiving Email Notifications After Finalizing Payrolls

After a worksite manager or worksite trusted advisor in a client that is not set up as self-service payroll finalizes a payroll, the system sends an email notification to the payroll processor for that payroll who is listed on the Payroll Control form, even if the user ID is different from the user ID listed on the Account tab in the Client Details form.

Note: Note the following conditions that must exist for the system to create the message for payroll submission notifications:

  • If the system-level setting to enable payroll submission notifications is checked and the client-level setting is set to Select or Enable

  • If the client-level setting for payroll submission notifications is set to Enable when the system-level setting is not checked

The email message displays as follows:

  • Subject line: “Payroll <number> submitted for client <Client’s DBA name> (<Client ID>).” For example, “Payroll 202206 submitted for Client JMF Photography (1211).”

  • Email body: “Payroll <number> has been submitted for processing.” For example, “Payroll 202206 has been submitted for processing.”

Unfinalizing Entries

If you need to unfinalize entries:

  1. Deselect the checkbox for each employee whose information you need to change.

  2. Select the checkbox at the top of the Employee column to deselect all employees on the page.

  3. Click Unfinalize All to deselect all finalized employees in the payroll.
