Using SuperBatch

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Action/SuperBatch_Next_Generation.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Action/SuperBatch_Next_Generation.htm

Using SuperBatch

SuperBatch, a payroll processing hub, helps payroll processors oversee each payroll assignment without adding extra work or time. Using a streamlined workflow, you can accomplish all your payroll tasks—entering time data, checking for errors, finalizing and printing—directly from the SuperBatch. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: When there is a long list of payrolls the automatic refresh causes the screen to “bounce” and does not return you to the payroll where you were working. To stop this automatic refresh, click the Stop Timer (

[Image: screenshot]

) icon at the top of the form. Clicking this “hourglass” icon stops the timer until you click the icon again. (The icon changes to indicate a start/stop status.)

Working with SuperBatch

SuperBatch allows you to quickly process a large volume of payrolls accurately. In addition, you can view and download any warnings (yellow triangle) or errors (red triangle) in the payroll by clicking the icon. A Payroll Warning or Payroll Errors message displays where you can click Reset Payroll to restart the payroll or click Print to open a report in .csv format, so you can view the warnings or errors and quickly address issues that prevent payroll processing from completing.

Note: All errors and warnings that occur during and after payroll process calculation display the employee’s last name, preferred name instead of their last name, first name, if applicable. (If the employee does not have a preferred name, then their last name, first name displays.)

The contents of the SuperBatch form are specific to your user ID. Client payrolls assigned to you that remain incomplete as of the Cutoff Date Up To are the only ones that appear on your SuperBatch form. The basic flow of using SuperBatch appears below.

[Image: screenshot]

Using the Filtering Options

You can use the filtering options in the enhanced version of SuperBatch to limit the payrolls that display:

  • Cutoff Date Up To: Includes all incomplete payroll batches that require payroll processing and are due on or before that date. (The default is the Friday of the current week.)

Note: You can adjust the lookback period the system uses for the Cutoff Date Up To date by enabling the SUPERBATCHLOOKBACK custom feature code on the System Parameters form. However, note the following when using the SUPERBATCHLOOKBACK custom feature code:

  • Enabling this custom feature code displays the SuperBatch Lookback Period field on the System Parameters form, where you can adjust the date.

  • The default for the SuperBatch process is the standard 95-day lookback period.

  • If you enable this field but do not enter a numeric value, the system defaults to the standard 95-day lookback period.

  • If you remove the SUPERBATCHLOOKBACK custom feature code, the system hides the SuperBatch Lookback Period field and reverts to the standard 95-day lookback period.

Note: Note the following about the Cutoff Date Up To filtering option:

  • The system selects all payrolls by the cutoff date, not the pay date.

  • When the Cutoff Date Up To date is greater than the current date, the system selects all payrolls with a pay date greater than or equal to today’s date (minus 95 days), plus all payrolls from the current date to the entered pay date.

  • When the Cutoff Date Up To date is less than the current date, the system selects all payrolls with a pay date greater than the entered pay date (minus 95 days).

  • Payrolls will always display for the Cutoff Date Up To date minus 95 days. For example, if the date entered is 100 days in the past, the system displays payrolls 195 to 100 days in the past.

  • Payroll Processor: Payroll representative who is the current active user. In addition, this filter allows you to select all payroll processors. (The incomplete payroll batches assigned to that payroll processor display.)

Important! If you enable Manager Only Views All SuperBatch Payrolls in the Global Configuration form, Payroll Processor users are only able to view their assigned payrolls and cannot use the SuperBatch Payroll Transfer functionality.

  • Self Service: The client processes all or some steps of their own payrolls.

Note: After selecting All Payrolls, “SS” displays next to each payroll’s Employees Finalized notation in the Client Level Actions area, so you can easily find all self-service payrolls.

  • Payroll Type: The payroll batch type. For example, payrolls set to Regularly Scheduled are those payrolls automatically created by PrismHR.

  • Cost Center: Filters payrolls based on the selected cost center.

Note: Note the following:

  • The cost centers listed in the Cost Center filter option are defined on the Cost Centers form.

  • Cost centers are assigned to clients in the Cost Center field on the Client Details form.

  • After selecting a cost center, the system filters the payrolls so only clients with the selected cost center display.

The icons in the top-right corner of the SuperBatch form help you perform the following actions:

Icon — Description

Payroll Transfer [Image: screenshot] — Displays the SuperBatch Payroll Transfer form, where you can transfer all currently viewed payrolls or selected payrolls to another payroll processor. (Select the payroll processor and click Update.) Note: If you select multiple payrolls and then click this icon to change to a new payroll processor, only the payrolls you selected are updated, not those in the entire view.

Filter Selection [Image: screenshot] — Displays a search form, where you can enter information to narrow the payroll assignments that display. (Enter the search information and click Apply.)

Refresh Existing Filter [Image: screenshot] — Refreshes payrolls that display based on the existing user and selected filters/settings. Note: This filter can also act as a “reset” for payrolls.

Reset Filters [Image: screenshot] — If you filtered the payrolls to only display payrolls associated with a particular step, select this icon to refresh the display so all payrolls associated with the selected filters redisplay.

A ribbon displays the steps for the payrolls in-progress. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Each step displays the number of payrolls associated with it.

To further filter the payroll display, click a step in the ribbon to display all the payrolls in that step. (Some of these filters can include several statuses, which you can select as a group or individually.) For example, clicking Ready for Time Entry in the example above displays the payrolls matching that criteria:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: A blue selection bar and chevron down arrow display within a step when you click it, so you can easily determine which step is selected in the ribbon.

For example, click the link in the Payroll Number column to open the Payroll Control form, which displays details about that payroll. (Each form opens as a layer over SuperBatch, so that you do not lose your place and can return to SuperBatch easily.)

[Image: screenshot]

To do this: Select this:
Access additional actions for selected client or payroll Ellipsis ( [Image: screenshot] ) icon (see below)
Access Client Details form displaying selected client’s details Client name or client ID
Access Payroll Control form displaying selected payroll’s details Payroll number

Accessing Actions and Reports Menu

You can quickly access the options described below by selecting the Ellipsis icon (

[Image: screenshot]

). For example:

[Image: screenshot]

A window opens where you can select from the following options:

Option — Description

Bill Pending — Lists billing events that will occur during the next scheduled billing date (in other words, they are pending). These billing events can be created on this form or generated automatically by PrismHR. (See Working with Bill Pending Data.)

Company Details — Maintain company information and settings. (See Maintaining Client Details.)

Employee Details — Maintain employee information and settings. (See Maintaining Employee Details.)

New Hire Entry — Enter a newly hired employee’s information. (See Setting Up New Hire Information.)

Pay Rate Change — Set a new pay rate for an employee. (See Making a Pay Rate Change for an Employee.)

Payroll Control — Establish essential information for processing payroll. (See Establishing Information for Processing Payrolls.)

Payroll Approval — After payroll processor calculates the payroll, PrismHR sends a message to the payroll approver that the payroll is ready for review and approval. (See Processing Standard Payroll Approval.)

Rehire — Rehire a terminated employee. (See Rehiring a Terminated Employee.)

Payroll Validation — Generate listing of validation errors for the selected payroll number. (See Generating the Payroll Validation Report.)

Payroll Information — Displays payroll information, such as payroll approval client, assigned payroll process user, delivery method, and remote timesheet entry client.

Payroll Allocation — Determines the format for the payroll costs that are distributed across multiple cost centers such as departments, divisions or locations.

Payroll Variance Analysis — Opens the Payroll Variance Analysis dashboard, where you can review relevant payroll information and compare two payrolls on a single dashboard to simplify the review process.

Note: When you select an option, the client’s or payroll’s information automatically displays.

Note: Note the following:

  • If you do not have access or are denied access to a form that displays in the Actions list, that option does not display.

  • If you do not have access or are denied access to all of the forms, the Actions header does not display.

  • If you do not have access or are denied access to all of the Actions and Reports the following message displays, “No actions and reports available. Contact your administrator.”

  • If you have Inquiry access to a form, that option displays in the Actions list.

SuperBatch Processing Steps

The steps involved in SuperBatch processing are:

  1. Viewing Payroll Batches in SuperBatch

  2. Entering Time Sheets

  3. Calculating Payroll Vouchers

  4. Reviewing a Payroll

  5. Performing Payroll Batch Approval (if required for client)

  6. Finalizing Payroll

  7. Printing and Mailing Payroll Batches

Using the Actions Menu

You can access other information and features using the Actions menu:

  • Add Employee to Payroll: Enter or select an employee to add to a payroll. (See the Payroll Processing Guide.)

  • Change Processor: Change the processor for one or more payrolls. (See the Payroll Processing Guide.)

  • Client Bill Pending: Review the billing events that will occur during the next scheduled billing date (see the Client Administration Guide), or click New Entry to enter a billing item or view the details of an existing one (see the Client Administration Guide).

  • Employee Loans: Establish employee loan information, track the payment of the loan, or view loan payments that were deducted from employee paychecks. (See the Payroll Administration Guide.)

  • Process Payroll: Enter time sheet information, calculate the payroll, finalize the payroll, run the Payroll Validation Report and the Payroll Audit Report, update employee and payroll records, review/download errors and warnings, and print the vouchers. (See the Payroll Processing Guide.)

  • Recurring Deduction Overrides: Temporarily override one or more deductions for a specified employee’s paycheck. (See the Payroll Overrides Guide.)

  • Recurring Deductions: Enter voluntary deductions for the selected employee. (See the Payroll Administration Guide.)

  • Scheduled Deductions: Establish a one-time or temporary deduction for the employee. (See the Payroll Overrides Guide.)

  • Scheduled Payments: Establish payments for a specific date in the future or repeat them each pay period during a specified time period. (See the Payroll Overrides Guide.)

  • Tax Calculation Overrides: Temporarily override the way the system calculates taxes for an employee. (See the Payroll Overrides Guide.)

  • Vacation Pay Override: Overriding vacation voucher calculations. (See the Payroll Overrides Guide.)

Suppressing Taxes

WARNING: Do not suppress taxes unless you are trained in its use. Suppressing a tax is not the same as blocking a tax. When you suppress a tax, you also suppress taxable earnings. Contact the PrismHR Customer Support Team for assistance.

To suppress a tax in PrismHR:

  1. Enter the Tax Identifier of each tax to suppress. The Identifier displays.

  2. Enter the Tax Authority code for each suppressed tax. The Authority displays.

  3. Enter the Start Date. If you leave this field blank, the system immediately begins to suppress the tax.

  4. Enter the Stop Date. If you leave this field blank, the system suppresses the tax indefinitely.

  5. Click Close. The system saves your changes.

Tax Calculation Overrides

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Action/Tax_Calculation_Override_Entry.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Action/Tax_Calculation_Override_Entry.htm

Overriding Employee Tax Calculation

Use the Tax Calculation Overrides form to temporarily override the way the system calculates taxes for an employee.

Working with Income Tax Overrides

Using the Income Tax Overrides panel, you can:

  • Add a fixed amount to the amount already withheld.

  • Block the tax withholding altogether.

  • Indicate a new percentage rate to be used in calculating the tax.

  • Enter a new fixed amount.

To override income taxes for an employee:

  1. Enter the Employee by either entering the name, Social Security Number, or ID to display a pop-up list of matching employee records. You can also click the field label or press Ctrl+Enter with your cursor in this field to open the search window.

  2. Enter the Tax Auth ID to which this tax calculation override applies. The Authority Name displays.

  3. Select the Override Type to use in the override for this tax authority:

Override Type Description
Add to Amount Withheld Increases the employee’s income tax withholding by a fixed Amount.
Percentage Rate Withholds a percentage Amount of net taxable pay.
Fixed Amount Withholds the Amount.
Block Withholding Blocks withholding of income tax from the employee’s pay.
Supplemental Tax Rate Withholds a percentage Amount of supplemental pay.
Supplemental Tax Amount Withholds a fixed Amount of supplemental pay.
Supplemental Block Blocks withholding from supplemental pay.

  1. Enter the override Amount that corresponds with the Override Type. If you blocked withholding, leave this field blank.

  2. Enter the Starting Pay Date when this temporary tax override goes into effect. The tax override applies to payroll batches if the pay date falls within the date range. For the tax override to work, this field is mandatory.

  3. Enter the Ending Pay Date when this temporary tax override is no longer in effect. For the tax override to work, this field is mandatory.

  4. Select the Status to control how the system handles overrides during payroll processing:

  • Active (default): Processes overrides as they were originally done.

  • Inactive: Ignores overrides during payroll processing. (You can later reactivate an inactive override by changing this status.)

  • Onetime: Applies the override to one payroll processed within the entered date range.

Note: After a payroll processes with the Status set to Onetime, the override status changes to Inactive and the voucher number displays in the Voucher field. (You cannot edit or reactivate a onetime override after it is used. However, you can enter a new override for the same tax authority.)

  1. Repeat for each tax authority.

  2. Set up any miscellaneous overrides as needed. Otherwise, click Save.

Miscellaneous Overrides

Depending on the entries you make in the Miscellaneous Overrides panel, different fields display.

Note: Note: You cannot use the Weeks In Pay Period method if the employee uses the federal cumulative method.

WARNING: Do not use the Tax Options field unless advised to do so by the PrismHR Customer Support Team.

To set up miscellaneous tax overrides:

  1. First, make sure you have selected the appropriate employee on the Tax Calculation Overrides form.

  2. Enter the Weeks in Pay Period to use when calculating taxes on the selected voucher types. Enter the other values as needed:

  • Enter the From Date when the tax override goes into effect.

  • Enter the To Date through which this tax override is active.

  • In For Voucher Types, specify the voucher types to which overrides apply: Regular, Supplemental, or Vacation.

  1. Select Yes in the Suppress Local Tax field to suppress the withholding of all local taxes for this employee. Enter the other values as needed:

  • Select the Local Tax Type to suppress.

  • Enter the Thru Pay Date when the system should stop suppressing the local tax. If you leave this field blank, the tax is always suppressed.

Important! If you used the Tax Calculation Overrides form in the past for an employee it is possible that you need to delete “phantom” data. You must select Delete to remove these records. Confirmation that the system successfully deleted the record occurs when no Tax Calculation Override on File message exists. Going forward, when you create a new override record, selecting an option from the Suppress Local Tax and Courtesy Wthld PA E.I.T fields’ drop-down menus prevents the system from creating “phantom” data.

  1. Select Suppress Work State Tax to suppress state income tax withholding in the state where the employee works.

Note: Enter the Thru Pay Date to suppress state income tax withholding. If you leave this field blank, the tax suppression will not stop.

  1. Select Yes in the Courtesy Wthld PA E.I.T field to force the system to withhold local resident-based Earned Income Tax (EIT).

Note: By default, if an employee lives in but works outside of Pennsylvania, the system does not withhold local resident-based Earned Income Tax.

  1. Enter any special Tax Options, if required. Do not enter a value in this field unless specifically you are instructed to do so by PrismHR Customer Support.

  2. Click Save.

Actions Menu

You can access other information and settings using the Actions menu.

Importing Timesheet Deductions

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Action/Time_Sheet_Deduction_Import.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Action/Time_Sheet_Deduction_Import.htm

Importing Timesheet Deductions

You can use the Time Sheet Deduction Import form to import timesheet deductions for a payroll.

Note: You must have FULL access to the Time Sheet Deduction Import form to process an import. In addition, worksite managers cannot import any employees whom they cannot access.

To access the Time Sheet Deduction Import form, go to Payroll|Action and select Time Sheet Entry. Select a payroll number in the Time Sheet Entry form, then select Time Sheet Deduction Import on the Actions menu. The Payroll Number that you selected displays.

Note: Note: You can click Download Sample Header File to download a sample Excel data file in .csv format, which can be saved before importing it.

To import timesheet deductions for a payroll:

  1. Go to the Time Sheet Deduction Import form. The current Payroll Number displays. (You cannot update this field.)

  2. Select Upload File.

Note: The uploaded file name cannot contain any spaces and must be in .csv format.

  1. Select Add Files, then select the file that contains timesheet deductions for a payroll. (The file must be in .csv format.)

  2. Select Start Upload. “Upload complete” displays when the file successfully uploads. Click Close. The uploaded filename displays.

  3. Click Start Import. The system validates the uploaded file during the import process to ensure the information is valid.

  4. If there were any errors during the import process, they display in the Error Report.

  5. Click Review to look at the imported data. If there is more than one page, use the Previous Page and Next Page buttons to navigate the imported time sheet data.

  6. If the data is accurate, click Post Data to Time Sheets. The system processes the data and creates the timesheets.

  7. Click OK in the confirmation message.

  8. Click Edit Time Sheets. You return to the Time Sheet Entry form, where you can proceed to the next step of the process.

Using Time Sheet Entry Keyboard Shortcuts

The time sheet allows you to enter information quickly using keyboard shortcuts.

Navigating Summary Time Sheet Entry

Paging

If there are multiple pages, press Page Up and Page Down, or click the

[Image: screenshot]

and

[Image: screenshot]

buttons near the bottom of the form, to navigate to the previous or next pages.

Find/Search

Press Shift+Enter, or click

[Image: screenshot]

, to open the Find dialog. This allows you to search the time sheet for a specific employee; the list filters as you type.

[Image: screenshot]

Moving from Summary to Detail Entry

There are three ways to access the Detail Time Sheet Entry form from the Summary Time Sheet Entry form:

  • Click the name of the employee. The Detail Time Sheet Entry form opens, where you can create a new entry for that employee.

[Image: screenshot]

  • While the cursor is in one of the pay code fields, press Ctrl+Enter. The Detail Time Sheet Entry form opens for that employee and pay code, where you can edit the time sheet entry.

  • While the cursor is in the row of an employee, click a pay code column heading. The Detail Time Sheet Entry form opens for that employee and pay code, where you can edit the time sheet entry.

Navigating Detail Time Sheet Entry

Using the Entry Drop-Down

If there are no entries for the employee, the only option is New Entry. If there are one or more existing entries, you can use the drop-down to select the entry you want to edit. To use it without the mouse, you can use the up and down arrow keys, or simply type the number of the item. For example, you would enter 1 to edit the REG entry, 2 to edit the OT entry, or N to create a new entry.

[Image: screenshot]

Entering Values

[Image: screenshot]

[Image: screenshot]

[Image: screenshot]

Saving in the Detail Time Sheet

Returning to the Summary Time Sheet Form

To return to the summary, press Page Up or click Return. This does not save your work, so be sure to save anything you need before returning to the summary. The Page Up key does not work when the cursor is in the Hours Paid, Amount Paid, Units Paid, or Pay Rate field.

Voiding Payroll Batch or Voucher

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Action/Void_Batch-Voucher.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Action/Void_Batch-Voucher.htm

Voiding Payroll Batch or Voucher

You can void payments in PrismHR, either a single check or a whole batch, using the Void and Reissue Checks form.

During this process, the system voids the original check and issues a new check number that is effective on the date it was processed.

Important! You cannot void and reissue a reconciled or an escheated check. If a check is set to R (reconciled) status or E (escheated) and you try to void and reissue it, an error message displays. For example, the following error message displays if you try to void and reissue a reconciled check, “This check is already reconciled and cannot be reissued.” Also, if you enter a voided check number in this form, an error message displays, “This check is already voided and cannot be reissued.”

To void payments and reissue a check:

  1. Access the Void and Reissue Checks form on the Payroll|Action menu.

  2. Enter or select the original voucher in the Payroll Number field and note the Check Number and Pay Date (for example, check number 8216, and pay date 02/02/2024).

Note: Enter or select the Bank Account associated with the original check number to display other data, including the pay date information.

  1. Click Void and Reissue Checks.

  2. After the system voids and reissues the check, access the Payroll History form on the Payroll|View menu.

  3. Select the Payroll Number where the original check was processed. The Payroll Summary form displays.

  4. Select the Summary icon ( [Image: screenshot] ) next to the Payroll Number. The Payroll Reports form displays.

  5. Locate the voided and reissued payment and select the Open File icon ( [Image: screenshot] ). A browser window opens.

  6. Select Open file to download the file. The reissued check displays a new check number and pay date in the Time Sheet Report.

Note: Note the following:

  • You cannot void and reissue a reconciled check. If a check is set to R (reconciled) status and you try to void and reissue it, the following error message displays, “This check is already reconciled and cannot be reissued.” Also, if you enter a voided check number in this form, an error message displays, “This check is already voided and cannot be reissued.”

  • Employees who are paid using pay on-demand processing have an invoice amount that is debited on the ACH file. However, if you void the pay on-demand voucher, the invoice amount displays as a credit on the ACH file.

Note: Note the following:

  • If you run the pay on-demand process (that is, you generate a file) and then you complete a void, no changes occur in the history file.

  • If you do not generate a file and a void occurs, then the system does not include the voucher in the next file creation.

Add Employees to Payroll

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Change/Add_Employees_to_Payroll.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Change/Add_Employees_to_Payroll.htm

Adding Employees to a Payroll

Use the Add Employees to Payroll form to add employees to the payroll batch. You can only add employees that do not already belong to any of the pay groups scheduled in the payroll; for example, if you want to process a check for an employee in the current batch who belongs to a different pay group. The forms also filters out any employees whose hire date is after the end of the pay period.

Note: Select Quick Load to open the Regular Payroll Control Quick Load form, where you can add multiple employees to a pay group at once. (See Using Regular Payroll Control Quick Load.)

When you add an employee, you must specify the pay group to associate with the employee for the payroll batch. PrismHR uses the pay group to assign the period start date, period end date, deduction period, period number, and optional alternate pay period to the employee.

[Image: screenshot]

To add employees to a payroll:

  1. Click the Actions menu in the Payroll Control form and then select Add Employees to Payroll.

  2. For each employee:

a. Enter the Employee ID. The Employee Name displays.
b. Select the Pay Group, which must be in the payroll.
— —

  1. Click Accept. You return to the Payroll Control form.

  2. Click Save in the Payroll Control form.

When to Use This Feature

Some clients with multiple locations, with pay groups defined for each location, have employees who work for more than one location during the pay period.

For example, during the current pay period, Mark works twenty hours at the Main Street location and twenty hours at the South Street location. The system associates an employee with one primary pay group, and Mark is assigned to the Main Street pay group.

  • Without this feature, Mark would need to be paid for twenty hours within his normally scheduled batch.

  • If you use this feature, you can associate Mark with South Street’s pay group for the purpose of paying him the hours worked at their location.

Benefit and Deduction Considerations

When you add an employee to a batch, the employee’s payroll voucher is treated as a supplemental pay voucher for deductions calculations, regardless of the type of pay found on the voucher. As such, standard deductions are not deducted. However, deductions that normally would be taken from a supplemental pay voucher—a retirement plan, garnishment, or deduction in arrears—will be deducted.

In the example, Mark’s standard benefit deductions would be taken on the payroll voucher paid in his regular pay group batch. If the pay is not sufficient to cover all scheduled benefit deductions, the balance goes into arrears. When the remaining twenty hours are paid in the batch to which Mark was added, PrismHR takes the deduction amounts in arrears on that paycheck.

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Change/Batch_Payments.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Change/Batch_Payments.htm

Entering Multiple Fixed, Pre-calculated Payments

The Batch Payments form allows you to quickly enter multiple fixed, pre-calculated payments to be paid during a specific payroll batch. These payments include bonuses, sales commissions, expense reimbursements, and so on. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Note the following:

  • You can upload batch payment information into the form instead of entering it manually if you have a file in the correct format (see Importing Payments File into a Payroll.

  • You can use the BATCH-PAYMENTS-CHANGE-DEFAULTS (system level) and BATCH-PAYMENTS-CHANGE-DEFAULTS-C (client level) custom feature codes to allocate batch payments (see Using Custom Feature Codes and Specifying Client Custom Feature Codes).

Note: If you do not set these custom feature codes at the system and client levels, the Edit Employee Details column does not display in the Batch Payments form.

To enter multiple fixed, pre-calculated payments into a payroll:

  1. Enter the Payroll Number of the payroll batch within which to pay the additional amounts. This must be an active payroll in the system.

Note: If you enter batch payments after the payroll processor has calculated the batch (INITOK or INITCOMP), the processor must recalculate the payroll to include the payment after you save the batch payment record.

  1. Enable Recalculate Overtime to automatically enable the Recalculate Overtime field on the Payroll Options form. (This field defaults to disabled.)

Note: Note the following:

  • You can access the Payroll Options form by selecting Options on the Actions menu in the Payroll Control form after selecting a Payroll Number.

  • The Recalculate Overtime field does not display for payrolls set to the Regularly Scheduled payroll type on the Payroll Control form.

  1. For each employee:
a. Enter the Employee ID for the line; the employee’s Name displays.

It must be an employee that belongs to a pay group included in the payroll batch; it can be a terminated employee. You can enter more than one line for an individual employee, if needed.

  1. — Enter the Pay Code for this payment. It must have a fixed calculation method. The Description prints on the pay stub or direct deposit advice.
c. Enter the Pay Amount. It can be a negative number, but it cannot be zero.
d. Enter the number of Hours Worked.
— —
  1. — Indicate whether to Suppress Allocation. If you select Yes, the system allocates the line only to the employee’s home data fields, instead of basing it on the employee’s allocations set on the Pay tab in the Employee Details form.

After selecting Yes, you can select the Edit Employee Details (

[Image: screenshot]

) icon to display the Time Sheet Allocation form, where you can assign the Department, Division, Location, Shift, Position, Project, and Phase allocations. After entering the allocation types, click Accept to apply the values to the batch payment.

Note: If you override the home data fields in the Time Sheet Allocation form, a checkmark displays in the Edit Employee Details column in the Batch Payments form.

f. Indicate whether to Add to Retirement, and how.

  • No: Does not take the amount as a retirement deduction.

  • Yes: Takes the pay amount as an extra retirement deduction.

  • Yes - less FICA: Takes the pay amount as an extra retirement deduction, less the FICA percentage.

  1. Click Save.

When the payroll processor calculates the payroll, the payments will be included in the employees’ vouchers. This also increments the employees’ hours by 1; it equates to one unit.

Note: Note: Clicking Delete only deletes the batch payment information for the payroll. It does not delete the payroll batch.

Using the Batch Payments Import File Format

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Change/Batch_Payments_File_Format.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Change/Batch_Payments_File_Format.htm

Using the Batch Payments Import File Format

To use the Batch Payments file import, you must have a tab-delimited text file with the columns shown in Table 128. If you have a row with invalid information (such as a header row), the system automatically ignores it and imports only the payment data.

Column # Field Description Required? Format Description
1 Employee ID Yes N##### Must be the ID of an employee that works for the client and belongs to a pay group included in the payroll batch; it can be a terminated employee. You can enter more than one line for an individual employee, if needed.
2 Employee Name Skipped This column must exist, but the system ignores any value entered. On import, it populates the column with the name that matches the employee ID.
3 Pay Code Yes Must be a valid pay code defined in the system.
4 Pay Code Description Skipped This column must exist, but the system ignores any value entered. On import, it populates the column with the description of the pay code.
5 Pay Amount Yes ###.## Total amount to be paid to the employee.
6 Hours Worked No ##.## Total number of hours the employee worked, if any. If the column is left blank or contains an invalid value, the system defaults the value to 0.00.
7 Suppress Allocation No The system defaults this value to No. If it should be Yes, you must set it manually in the table after the import is complete.
8 Add to Retirement No The system defaults this value to No. If it should be Yes, you must set it manually in the table after the import is complete.

Note: Note: The decimal places in the Pay Amount and Hours Worked columns are optional. If there are more than three decimal places, the system rounds it to two.

The Uploading Batch Payments process window displays. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

  1. When the import is complete, click Close.

The payments in the file populate the table.

  1. Click Save.

When the payroll processor calculates the selected payroll, the payments will be included in the employees’ vouchers. This also increments the employees’ hours by 1; it equates to one unit.

Note: Note: Clicking Delete only deletes the batch payment information for the payroll. It does not delete the payroll batch.

Bankruptcy Order Garnishments

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Change/EE_Garnish_Bankruptcy_Order.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Change/EE_Garnish_Bankruptcy_Order.htm

Bankruptcy Order Garnishments

The following rules apply to bankruptcy order garnishments:

  • Only child support orders will continue to be calculated in conjunction with the bankruptcy order

  • Only one bankruptcy order is allowed

  • Full amount of the bankruptcy order is taken without limits

Employee Garnishment

The Employee Garnishment panel maintains the basic information required for the wage garnishment.

[Image: Employee Garnishment]

  1. Enter the Docket Number assigned by the government agency or court for this wage garnishment.

  2. Select the Category for the type of garnishment being withheld. This determines some of the other panels that display (described below).

  3. Enter the Employee by either entering the name, Social Security Number, or ID to display a pop-up list of matching employee records. You can also click the field label or press Ctrl+Enter with your cursor in this field to open the search window. You cannot change the employee for a existing garnishment.

  4. Enter the Receipt Date on which the wage garnishment notice was received from the issuing authority.

  5. Enter the name of the Issuing Authority that issued this garnishment.

  6. If the state requires you to use an ID other than the docket number, enter it in the State ID# field. This number appears on the checks instead of the docket number.

  7. If you enter a Start Date, the system starts payroll deductions on or after this date.

  8. If you enter a Stop Date, the system stops payroll deductions on or after this date.

  9. Enter the Payee ID to whom amounts withheld for this wage garnishment will be paid. If the payee record is set up to use EFT, the SDU or EFT panel might display.

  10. Enter the Deduction Code used for this garnishment.

  11. Enter an Annotation to print in the Memo field of the check stub. There are two lines available.

Calculation Rules

Enter the calculation rules for the bankruptcy order garnishment.

[Image: screenshot]

  1. Enter the Total Garnishment amount owed by the debtor to be collected under the garnishment order. If no limit is imposed, enter 0.

  2. Specify one of these methods to determine the withholding amount:

  • Enter a Flat Amount to withhold from the employee’s net pay.

  • Enter a Percent and then select whether it should be calculated based on the employee’s Gross Pay, Net Pay (gross pay minus taxes and other garnishments), or Starting Net Pay (gross pay minus taxes).

  1. Enter the Pay Period Limit, which the system uses in conjunction with a Percent calculation to set a dollar limit on the total garnishment amount per pay period.

  2. Enter the Monthly Limit, which is the dollar limit on the total monthly garnishment amount. If there is no limit, leave this field blank.

  3. Enter the Garnishment Fee that is associated with this garnishment, which PrismHR deducts from the employee’s pay each time it processes the garnishment.

Setting Temporary Garnishment Overrides

You can establish temporary garnishment overrides based on specified dates by updating the settings in the Override Rules panel.

[Image: Override Rules panel]

To set temporary garnishment overrides, do the following:

  1. In the Override Rules panel, complete the following fields:

Field — Description

Override Amount — Enter the temporary Override Amount to use during the specified date range.

Override Start Date — Enter the temporary Override Start Date.

Override Stop Date — Enter the temporary Override Stop Date.

Suppress Voucher Types — Select the Suppress Voucher Types, which are the pay types exempt from this garnishment. This setting is not controlled by the override start and stop dates. Instead, it applies to the entire garnishment record.

Suppress From Unscheduled Payrolls — Select Suppress From Unscheduled Payrolls, if the garnishment should not be taken out of unscheduled payrolls.

Override G/L Account — Enter the Override G/L Account that identifies the account number this garnishment credits.

  1. When you have finished entering the information, click Save.

Payments History

The Payments History panel provides a list of garnishments that have been paid to date.

[Image: Payments history panel]

  • The table lists the information for each payment:

  • Voucher Number: Each voucher that has been paid against this garnishment

  • Pay Date: Date on the voucher

  • Amount Due: Amount due as calculated on the voucher

  • Paid On: Date each check was paid

  • Check Number: Number on the check used to pay the garnishment to the payee

  • ACH Reference: Reference for the ACH transaction used to pay the garnishment to the payee

  • EFT/Check$: Amount of each check or transaction

  • Click Adjust to make an adjustment to the table. This does not affect accounting updates or functions, but can cause an adjustment to the employee’s next paycheck.

Updating Employee Garnishment Details

Child Support Garnishments

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Change/EE_Garnish_Child_Support.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Change/EE_Garnish_Child_Support.htm

Child Support Garnishments

The following rules apply to child support garnishments:

  • The system determines the correct maximum percent of disposable income based on employee details

  • Disposable earnings can be tailored to state rules

  • Pro-rata and Equal Share allocations are supported for multiple orders

  • Portion in arrears can be defined

  • Current order amount given priority on arrearage amount when calculating multiple orders

Employee Garnishment

The Employee Garnishment panel maintains the basic information required for the wage garnishment.

[Image: Employee Garnishments]

  1. Enter the Docket Number assigned by the government agency or court for this wage garnishment.

  2. Select the Category for the type of garnishment being withheld. This determines some of the other panels that display (described below).

  3. Enter the Employee by either entering the name, Social Security Number, or ID to display a pop-up list of matching employee records. You can also click the field label or press Ctrl+Enter with your cursor in this field to open the search window. You cannot change the employee for a existing garnishment.

  4. Enter the Receipt Date on which the wage garnishment notice was received from the issuing authority.

  5. Enter the garnishment’s Order Date. This ensures proper garnishment priority ordering in the system. (Only displays if you enabled the TESTGARNEXT and GARNFTLORDER feature codes).

  6. Enter the name of the Issuing Authority that issued this garnishment.

  7. If the state requires you to use an ID other than the docket number, enter it in the State ID# field. This number appears on the checks instead of the docket number.

  8. If you enter a Start Date, the system starts payroll deductions on or after this date.

  9. If you enter a Stop Date, the system stops payroll deductions on or after this date.

  10. Enter the Payee ID to whom amounts withheld for this wage garnishment will be paid. If the payee record is set up to use EFT, the SDU or EFT panel might display.

  11. Enter the Deduction Code used for this garnishment.

  12. Enter an Annotation to print in the Memo field of the check stub. There are two lines available.

Calculation Rules

Enter the calculation rules for the child support garnishment.

[Image: Calculation rules panel]

  1. Enter the Withholding Amount to withhold each pay period for the child support garnishment order. This amount should be the sum of current and past due amounts.

  2. Enter the Portion in Arrears amount to withhold for the child support order to cover the arrearage amount.

  3. Enter the Garnishment Fee that is associated with this garnishment, which PrismHR deducts from the employee’s pay each time it processes the garnishment.

SDU

The system supports the ability to create an ACH file with line items for garnishments. This allows you to submit an ACH file that results in an EFT for all state tax levies.

If a garnishment is for child or spousal support and the payee is a state disbursement unit, you can set up EFT for the garnishment on the SDU panel. The SDU panel establishes the appropriate state information required to process the wage garnishment.

  1. Enter the Case Identifier recognized by the state disbursement unit for child support orders. This field is required if the payee is set to require the case number.

  2. Enter the FIPS Code (Federal Information Process Standard) applicable to the child support entity receiving the transaction. This field will be required if the payee is set up to require the FIPS code and it can require a specific length.

  3. Select Medical Support Indicator if the non-custodial parent has family medical insurance through their employer.

Setting Temporary Garnishment Overrides

You can establish temporary garnishment overrides based on specified dates by updating the settings in the Override Rules panel.

[Image: Override Rules panel]

To set temporary garnishment overrides, do the following:

  1. In the Override Rules panel, complete the following fields:

Field — Description

Override Amount — Enter the temporary Override Amount to use during the specified date range.

Override Start Date — Enter the temporary Override Start Date.

Override Stop Date — Enter the temporary Override Stop Date.

Suppress Voucher Types — Select the Suppress Voucher Types, which are the pay types exempt from this garnishment. This setting is not controlled by the override start and stop dates. Instead, it applies to the entire garnishment record.

Suppress From Unscheduled Payrolls — Select Suppress From Unscheduled Payrolls, if the garnishment should not be taken out of unscheduled payrolls.

Override G/L Account — Enter the Override G/L Account that identifies the account number this garnishment credits.

  1. When you have finished entering the information, click Save.

Payments History

The Payments History panel provides a list of garnishments that have been paid to date.

[Image: Payments history panel]

  • The table lists the information for each payment:

  • Voucher Number: Each voucher that has been paid against this garnishment

  • Pay Date: Date on the voucher

  • Amount Due: Amount due as calculated on the voucher

  • Paid On: Date each check was paid

  • Check Number: Number on the check used to pay the garnishment to the payee

  • ACH Reference: Reference for the ACH transaction used to pay the garnishment to the payee

  • EFT/Check$: Amount of each check or transaction

  • Click Adjust to make an adjustment to the table. This does not affect accounting updates or functions, but can cause an adjustment to the employee’s next paycheck.

Creditor Wage Garnishments

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Change/EE_Garnish_Creditor_Wage_Garnishment.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Change/EE_Garnish_Creditor_Wage_Garnishment.htm

Creditor Wage Garnishments

The following rules apply to creditor wage garnishments:

  • Majority of states follow CCPA limits

  • Tips generally not considered earnings

  • Child support orders take priority

  • In conjunction with child support orders, garnishment can be taken only if the child support percent of earnings is less than 25%

Employee Garnishment

The Employee Garnishment panel maintains the basic information required for the wage garnishment.

[Image: Employee Garnishment]

  1. Enter the Docket Number assigned by the government agency or court for this wage garnishment.

  2. Select the Category for the type of garnishment being withheld. This determines some of the other panels that display (described below).

  3. Enter the Employee by either entering the name, Social Security Number, or ID to display a pop-up list of matching employee records. You can also click the field label or press Ctrl+Enter with your cursor in this field to open the search window. You cannot change the employee for a existing garnishment.

  4. Enter the Receipt Date on which the wage garnishment notice was received from the issuing authority.

  5. Enter the name of the Issuing Authority that issued this garnishment.

  6. If the state requires you to use an ID other than the docket number, enter it in the State ID# field. This number appears on the checks instead of the docket number.

  7. If you enter a Start Date, the system starts payroll deductions on or after this date.

  8. If you enter a Stop Date, the system stops payroll deductions on or after this date.

  9. Enter the Payee ID to whom amounts withheld for this wage garnishment will be paid. If the payee record is set up to use EFT, the SDU or EFT panel might display.

  10. Enter the Deduction Code used for this garnishment.

  11. Enter an Annotation to print in the Memo field of the check stub. There are two lines available.

Calculation Rules

Enter the calculation rules for the creditor wage garnishment.

[Image: screenshot]

  1. Enter the Total Garnishment amount owed by the debtor to be collected under the garnishment order. If no limit is imposed, enter 0.

  2. Specify one of these methods to determine the withholding amount:

  • Enter a Flat Amount to withhold from the employee’s net pay.

  • Enter a Percent and then select whether it should be calculated based on the employee’s Gross Pay, Net Pay (gross pay minus taxes and other garnishments), or Starting Net Pay (gross pay minus taxes).

  1. Enter the Pay Period Limit, which the system uses in conjunction with a Percent calculation to set a dollar limit on the total garnishment amount per pay period.

  2. Enter the Garnishment Fee that is associated with this garnishment, which PrismHR deducts from the employee’s pay each time it processes the garnishment.

  3. Select Non-Consumer Garnishment if this garnishment is a judgment or non-consumer credit garnishment. The system applies the state rules for that type of garnishment.

  4. Select Head of Household if the employee is considered the head of their household for tax purposes. When this is selected, the system takes into account any maximum percentage for garnishments set on the State Garnishment Rules record for the state.

If there is no maximum percentage for heads of household, the system uses the standard maximum percent of disposable or gross pay.

Setting Temporary Garnishment Overrides

You can establish temporary garnishment overrides based on specified dates by updating the settings in the Override Rules panel.

[Image: Override Rules panel]

To set temporary garnishment overrides, do the following:

  1. In the Override Rules panel, complete the following fields:

Field — Description

Override Amount — Enter the temporary Override Amount to use during the specified date range.

Override Start Date — Enter the temporary Override Start Date.

Override Stop Date — Enter the temporary Override Stop Date.

Suppress Voucher Types — Select the Suppress Voucher Types, which are the pay types exempt from this garnishment. This setting is not controlled by the override start and stop dates. Instead, it applies to the entire garnishment record.

Suppress From Unscheduled Payrolls — Select Suppress From Unscheduled Payrolls, if the garnishment should not be taken out of unscheduled payrolls.

Override G/L Account — Enter the Override G/L Account that identifies the account number this garnishment credits.

  1. When you have finished entering the information, click Save.

Payments History

The Payments History panel provides a list of garnishments that have been paid to date.

[Image: Payments history panel]

  • The table lists the information for each payment:

  • Voucher Number: Each voucher that has been paid against this garnishment

  • Pay Date: Date on the voucher

  • Amount Due: Amount due as calculated on the voucher

  • Paid On: Date each check was paid

  • Check Number: Number on the check used to pay the garnishment to the payee

  • ACH Reference: Reference for the ACH transaction used to pay the garnishment to the payee

  • EFT/Check$: Amount of each check or transaction

  • Click Adjust to make an adjustment to the table. This does not affect accounting updates or functions, but can cause an adjustment to the employee’s next paycheck.

Limit Overrides

This section only appears when Creditor Wage Garnishment is selected from the drop-down under the Category field. Use the Limit Overrides panel to override any state-level settings as needed. Note that you can only reduce the maximum for this employee’s wage garnishment; you cannot use these fields to exceed state or federal maximums.

[Image: screenshot]

  1. Enter the Maximum Percent and specify whether that applies to the employee’s disposable or gross Pay.

  2. Enter the Minimum Wage Rate Multiplier, which is the number of hours to multiply by the employee’s minimum wage to calculate the maximum disposable earnings that the creditor can garnish. (This will be overridden if the garnishment maximum is lower.)

For example, if the multiplier is 40, the system multiplies the minimum wage by 40. The resulting amount is the minimum pay that an employee should have after taxes and garnishments. A standard creditor can garnish the amount left after subtracting taxes and the minimum pay amount from an employee’s gross pay.

  1. Select the Minimum Wage Rate Source used to determine the minimum hourly rate for this garnishment.

  2. Select the Hours Calculation Method used to calculate minimum net pay for semi-monthly or monthly pay periods under CCPA rules.

  • Factored: Multiplies the weekly hours by either a factor 2.16 (for semi-monthly) or 4.33 (for monthly). The factor method can be less accurate due to rounding errors, but some states specify its use.

  • Annualized: Multiplies the weekly hours by 52 and then divides by number of pay periods in the year. For example, for semi-monthly, the calculation is ( (30.00 x 52)/24 ).

  1. Enter the Maximum Monthly Fee to collect from the employee for the creditor wage garnishment.

  2. Indicate whether Reduce Limit by Fee Amount should reduce the limit by the administrative processing fee for this state.

  • Yes: The system reduces the limit.

  • No or Select One: The system does not reduce the limit.

  1. Select the Additional Disposable Deductions that are deducted from gross earnings to calculate disposable income for the purpose of calculating this employee’s creditor wage garnishment.

  2. When an Override State Code is selected for an employee, the employee creditor wage garnishment will follow the State Garnishment Rules for the selected Override State on the Employee Garnishments form and not the SUTA state. This field is optional. For example, if an employee is working in NY with NY SUTA and has a creditor garnishment with GA selected for the Override State Code field on the Employee Garnishments form, then creditor garnishment for that employee will be calculated based on State Garnishment Rules for GA instead of NY. The creditor garnishment will now follow the withholding limits based on the State Garnishment Rules form for the state selected in the Override State Code above instead of the employee’s SUTA state.

The following rules apply to Franchise Tax Board garnishments:

  • Can be used for any state

Calculation Rules

Enter the calculation rules for the franchise tax board garnishment.

[Image: screenshot]

  1. Enter the Total Garnishment amount owed by the debtor to be collected under the garnishment order. If no limit is imposed, enter 0.

  2. Specify one of these methods to determine the withholding amount:

  • Enter a Flat Amount to withhold from the employee’s net pay.

  • Enter a Percent of Disposable Earnings.

  1. Enter the Garnishment Fee that is associated with this garnishment, which PrismHR deducts from the employee’s pay each time it processes the garnishment.

EFT

The system supports the ability to create an ACH file with line items for garnishments. This allows you to submit an ACH file that results in an EFT for franchise tax board garnishments and state tax levies if your organization has selected the Consolidated ACH File Processing Used option in System Parameters. The EFT panel allows you to enter the case identifier for the wage garnishment.

Note: Note: This panel displays only for franchise tax board garnishments and state tax levies where the Payee is a garnishing authority with EFT parameters.

Many states permit submission of tax levies by ACH, and some states require it. In addition, the franchise tax board garnishment can be used for any state.

[Image: screenshot]

  • Enter a Percent and then select whether it should be calculated based on the employee’s Gross Pay, Net Pay (gross pay minus taxes and other garnishments), or Starting Net Pay (gross pay minus taxes).

  1. Enter the Portion in Arrears amount to withhold for the spousal support order to cover the arrearage amount.

  2. Enter the Garnishment Fee that is associated with this garnishment, which PrismHR deducts from the employee’s pay each time it processes the garnishment.

SDU

The system supports the ability to create an ACH file with line items for garnishments. This allows you to submit an ACH file that results in an EFT for all state tax levies.

If a garnishment is for child or spousal support and the payee is a state disbursement unit, you can set up EFT for the garnishment on the SDU panel. The SDU panel establishes the appropriate state information required to process the wage garnishment.

  1. Enter the Case Identifier recognized by the state disbursement unit for child support orders. This field is required if the payee is set to require the case number.

  2. Enter the FIPS Code (Federal Information Process Standard) applicable to the child support entity receiving the transaction. This field will be required if the payee is set up to require the FIPS code and it can require a specific length.

  3. Select Medical Support Indicator if the non-custodial parent has family medical insurance through their employer.

Setting Temporary Garnishment Overrides

You can establish temporary garnishment overrides based on specified dates by updating the settings in the Override Rules panel.

[Image: Override Rules panel]

To set temporary garnishment overrides, do the following:

  1. In the Override Rules panel, complete the following fields:

Field — Description

Override Amount — Enter the temporary Override Amount to use during the specified date range.

Override Start Date — Enter the temporary Override Start Date.

Override Stop Date — Enter the temporary Override Stop Date.

Suppress Voucher Types — Select the Suppress Voucher Types, which are the pay types exempt from this garnishment. This setting is not controlled by the override start and stop dates. Instead, it applies to the entire garnishment record.

Suppress From Unscheduled Payrolls — Select Suppress From Unscheduled Payrolls, if the garnishment should not be taken out of unscheduled payrolls.

Override G/L Account — Enter the Override G/L Account that identifies the account number this garnishment credits.

  1. When you have finished entering the information, click Save.

Payments History

The Payments History panel provides a list of garnishments that have been paid to date.

[Image: Payments history panel]

  • The table lists the information for each payment:

  • Voucher Number: Each voucher that has been paid against this garnishment

  • Pay Date: Date on the voucher

  • Amount Due: Amount due as calculated on the voucher

  • Paid On: Date each check was paid

  • Check Number: Number on the check used to pay the garnishment to the payee

  • ACH Reference: Reference for the ACH transaction used to pay the garnishment to the payee

  • EFT/Check$: Amount of each check or transaction

  • Click Adjust to make an adjustment to the table. This does not affect accounting updates or functions, but can cause an adjustment to the employee’s next paycheck.

State Tax Levy Garnishments

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Change/EE_Garnish_State_Tax_Levy.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Change/EE_Garnish_State_Tax_Levy.htm

State Tax Levy Garnishments

The following rules apply to state tax levy garnishments:

  • Calculates similar to a creditor garnishment (See Creditor Wage Garnishments)

  • Not limited to CCPA limits

  • Specified garnishment amount will be taken completely

Employee Garnishment

The Employee Garnishment panel maintains the basic information required for the wage garnishment.

[Image: Employee Garnishment]

  1. Enter the Docket Number assigned by the government agency or court for this wage garnishment.

  2. Select the Category for the type of garnishment being withheld. This determines some of the other panels that display (described below).

  3. Enter the Employee by either entering the name, Social Security Number, or ID to display a pop-up list of matching employee records. You can also click the field label or press Ctrl+Enter with your cursor in this field to open the search window. You cannot change the employee for a existing garnishment.

  4. Enter the Receipt Date on which the wage garnishment notice was received from the issuing authority.

  5. Enter the name of the Issuing Authority that issued this garnishment.

  6. If the state requires you to use an ID other than the docket number, enter it in the State ID# field. This number appears on the checks instead of the docket number.

  7. If you enter a Start Date, the system starts payroll deductions on or after this date.

  8. If you enter a Stop Date, the system stops payroll deductions on or after this date.

  9. Enter the Payee ID to whom amounts withheld for this wage garnishment will be paid. If the payee record is set up to use EFT, the SDU or EFT panel might display.

  10. Enter the Deduction Code used for this garnishment.

  11. Enter an Annotation to print in the Memo field of the check stub. There are two lines available.

Calculation Rules

Enter the calculation rules for the state tax levy.

[Image: screenshot]

  1. Enter the Total Garnishment amount owed by the debtor to be collected under the garnishment order. If no limit is imposed, enter 0.

  2. Specify one of these methods to determine the withholding amount:

  • Enter a Flat Amount to withhold from the employee’s net pay.

  • Enter a Percent and then select whether it should be calculated based on the employee’s:

  • Gross Pay: all taxable wages

  • Net Pay: gross pay minus taxes and preceding garnishments

  • Starting Net Pay: gross pay minus taxes

  • Subsequent Gross Pay: gross pay minus preceding garnishments

  1. Enter the Exempt Amount, which is the amount of wages that are exempt from the state tax levy. The amount levied will be equal to the disposable income, less the exempt amount.

  2. Enter the Garnishment Fee that is associated with this garnishment, which PrismHR deducts from the employee’s pay each time it processes the garnishment.

  3. If you are configuring a State Tax Levy garnishment, you may enter the Federal Poverty Guideline amount for the employee’s pay frequency. This field is optional. This field is only visible if you are configuring a State Tax Levy garnishment. The field accepts numeric values and rounds to two decimal places. When calculating garnishment withholdings for a State Tax Levy during payroll processing, the Federal Poverty Guideline (FPG), if present, is enforced to ensure that the garnishment is not withheld in excess of the employee’s Gross Wage - FPG amount.

EFT

The system supports the ability to create an ACH file with line items for garnishments. This allows you to submit an ACH file that results in an EFT for franchise tax board garnishments and state tax levies if your organization has selected the Consolidated ACH File Processing Used option in System Parameters. The EFT panel allows you to enter the case identifier for the wage garnishment.

Note: Note: This panel displays only for franchise tax board garnishments and state tax levies where the Payee is a garnishing authority with EFT parameters.

Many states permit submission of tax levies by ACH, and some states require it. In addition, the franchise tax board garnishment can be used for any state.

[Image: screenshot]

  1. For state tax levies set up for EFT, enter the Case Identifier. This field will be required if the payee is set up to require the case number.

Setting Temporary Garnishment Overrides

You can establish temporary garnishment overrides based on specified dates by updating the settings in the Override Rules panel.

[Image: Override Rules panel]

To set temporary garnishment overrides, do the following:

  1. In the Override Rules panel, complete the following fields:

Field — Description

Override Amount — Enter the temporary Override Amount to use during the specified date range.

Override Start Date — Enter the temporary Override Start Date.

Override Stop Date — Enter the temporary Override Stop Date.

Suppress Voucher Types — Select the Suppress Voucher Types, which are the pay types exempt from this garnishment. This setting is not controlled by the override start and stop dates. Instead, it applies to the entire garnishment record.

Suppress From Unscheduled Payrolls — Select Suppress From Unscheduled Payrolls, if the garnishment should not be taken out of unscheduled payrolls.

Override G/L Account — Enter the Override G/L Account that identifies the account number this garnishment credits.

  1. When you have finished entering the information, click Save.

Payments History

The Payments History panel provides a list of garnishments that have been paid to date.

[Image: Payments history panel]

  • The table lists the information for each payment:

  • Voucher Number: Each voucher that has been paid against this garnishment

  • Pay Date: Date on the voucher

  • Amount Due: Amount due as calculated on the voucher

  • Paid On: Date each check was paid

  • Check Number: Number on the check used to pay the garnishment to the payee

  • ACH Reference: Reference for the ACH transaction used to pay the garnishment to the payee

  • EFT/Check$: Amount of each check or transaction

  • Click Adjust to make an adjustment to the table. This does not affect accounting updates or functions, but can cause an adjustment to the employee’s next paycheck.

Student Loan Garnishments

The following rules apply to student loan garnishments:

  • Majority of states follow CCPA limits

  • Tips generally not considered earnings

  • Child support orders take priority

  • In conjunction with child support orders, garnishment can be taken only if the child support percent of earnings is less than 25%

Employee Garnishment

The Employee Garnishment panel maintains the basic information required for the wage garnishment.

[Image: Employee Garnishment]

  1. Enter the Docket Number assigned by the government agency or court for this wage garnishment.

  2. Select the Category for the type of garnishment being withheld. This determines some of the other panels that display (described below).

  3. Enter the Employee by either entering the name, Social Security Number, or ID to display a pop-up list of matching employee records. You can also click the field label or press Ctrl+Enter with your cursor in this field to open the search window. You cannot change the employee for a existing garnishment.

  4. Enter the Receipt Date on which the wage garnishment notice was received from the issuing authority.

  5. Enter the name of the Issuing Authority that issued this garnishment.

  6. If the state requires you to use an ID other than the docket number, enter it in the State ID# field. This number appears on the checks instead of the docket number.

  8. If you enter a Stop Date, the system stops payroll deductions on or after this date.

  9. Enter the Payee ID to whom amounts withheld for this wage garnishment will be paid. If the payee record is set up to use EFT, the SDU or EFT panel might display.

  10. Enter the Deduction Code used for this garnishment.

  11. Enter an Annotation to print in the Memo field of the check stub. There are two lines available.

Calculation Rules

Enter the calculation rules for the student loan garnishment.

Note: Note: When Student Loan is selected from the Category drop-down in the Employee Garnishments panel, the Student Loan Type drop-down displays under Calculation Rules.

  1. Select the appropriate Student Loan Type from the drop-down:

  • Apply Federal Limits Minus Medical: Federal standards that respect medical deductions in calculation.

  • Apply State and Federal Limits: This is the default option for student loan garnishments.

  • Apply State and Federal Limits Minus Medical: State and Federal standards that respect medical deductions in calculation.

  1. Enter the Total Garnishment amount owed by the debtor to be collected under the garnishment order. If no limit is imposed, enter 0.

  2. Enter a Percent and then select whether it should be calculated based on the employee’s:

  • Gross Pay: all taxable wages

  • Net Pay: gross pay minus taxes and preceding garnishments

  • Starting Net Pay: gross pay minus taxes

  1. Enter the Pay Period Limit, which the system uses in conjunction with a Percent calculation to set a dollar limit on the total garnishment amount per pay period.

  2. Enter the Garnishment Fee that is associated with this garnishment, which PrismHR deducts from the employee’s pay each time it processes the garnishment. The system will use the calculations set in the state rules for non-consumer garnishments.

Updating Employee Garnishment Details

To access this form, select Garnishment Details from the Actions menu

in the Employee Garnishments form. This information is shared for all garnishments for the employee at the client (for example, it also displays in the Employee Details > Other tab), therefore you must ensure that the information is correct.

Employee Deduction Arrears

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Change/Employee_Deduction_Arrears.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Change/Employee_Deduction_Arrears.htm

Employee Deduction Arrears

Use Employee Deduction Arrears to hold a deduction in arrears whenever an employee’s wages are not enough to cover a benefit deduction. This holds the deduction in arrears until the next pay period when the employee is paid. The system then attempts to take the deduction again. If the wages are still not able to cover the deduction, the deduction amount accumulates as long as it is scheduled to be taken. The benefits billing for that period is also sent to Deduction Arrears. Only benefit deductions are sent to Arrears.

Note: Note: You can only use this form to change existing arrears record information, not create new records. The system creates Employee Deduction Arrears records during payroll batch processing.

An arrears record only exists if a deduction is held in arrears for that employee. You can adjust this record by changing the deduction amount or forgiving a deduction by deleting a line item. It is not possible to add a deduction to this form. Once the deduction from arrears is applied to a paycheck, the arrears record becomes unavailable for viewing.

In addition, you can:

  • Initialize outstanding amounts for employees by creating one or more one-time deduction records.

  • Update an existing record by adjusting the arrears amount on a line or deleting the entire line.

Note: Note: Make sure the benefit deduction is properly reconciled before clicking Delete as the deduction cannot be restored.

To access this form and change employee arrears:

  1. Click Payroll|Payroll Change| Employee Deduction Arrears. The form displays with the Employee field link.

  2. Specify Employee information by:

  • Entering the Employee name, ID, or Social Security number.

  • Clicking the Employee link or pressing Ctrl+Enter in the search field to open the search selector. If the employee has a history of arrears, the system displays this information.

Note: The Next Pay Date field displays informational date value that helps you to quickly identify the next regularly scheduled payroll batch date during the enrollment process.

  1. You have these options:
  • Edit Arrears - Click the Arrears Date link in the table of arrears entries. This opens the Employee Deduction Arrears Detail modal.

You can change:

  • Amount of the arrears

  • Benefit Plan ID

  • Arrears Status - Select Optional or Automatic from the drop-down. The drop-down only appears if arrears on the Group Benefit Plan is set to ‘Suppress All Arrears, Track Optional Arrears Only’. If it is not set, this field is display-only. The Arrears Status field remains hidden until the feature code is entered at the system level.

Click Save to commit your changes and return to the main screen with your changes displayed.

Click Delete to delete an arrears record. Clicking Delete displays a warning message stating, This arrears record will be deleted immediately. Do you want to continue?

  • Click Yes to delete the record and the data for that record will no longer display on the main Employee Deduction Arrears form.

  • Click No to close the warning message and return on the Employee Deduction Arrears Detail modal form with all the previously entered data.

Click Close to close the modal form and return on the main Employee Deduction Arrears form. Any unsaved changes will be lost.

  • Change Status - Changes the status of a record from Optional to Automatic. You can select multiple records to perform a bulk status change on these items. The system displays a message saying the Arrears Status can only be changed from Optional to Automatic, and that changing the automatic status to optional must occur on the Employee Deduction Arrears Detail form. Click OK. You can make a change using the Change Status button to save the change immediately without needing to click Save on the form.

Note: Note: The Change Status button remains hidden until the USEWEEKLYBENEFITS feature code is entered at the system level.

  • Convert to Adjustment - For single records, click the check box next to the arrears entry you want to convert, then click the Convert to Adjustment button. A modal form displays with Benefit Plan and Arrears Balance pre-populated. Additionally, a static text message displays, This action will divide the arrears balance by the number of cycles indicated below to create benefit adjustments. Please note that rounding may cause slight discrepancies and additional adjustments may be needed. The arrears balance will be removed.

On the modal form, enter a date in the Start Date field and provide a value in the Adjustment Cycles field. Click Create. A confirmation pop-up indicating that the system creates an adjustment displays, Your change has caused the system to create billing adjustments. Would you like to review?

  • Click Yes to open the Benefit Adjustments modal form where you can review the newly created benefit adjustment and make changed if necessary.

  • Click No to close the confirmation pop-up window.

  • Delete - For single or multiple records, click the check box next to the arrears entry you want to delete, then click the Delete button at the end of the page. The system asks you to confirm whether you want to delete the selected records. Click Yes to commit the deletion.

Note: Note: The Delete, Change Status, and Convert to Adjustment buttons are disabled until at least one arrears item check box is selected.

  • Cancel - Clears the form at any time.

Employee Deduction Detail

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Change/Employee_Deduction_Detail.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Change/Employee_Deduction_Detail.htm

Entering Employee Deduction Details

Enter any relevant details for recurring deductions in the Employee Deduction Details form, which you can access by clicking Edit Detail on the Recurring Deductions form. (See Working with Recurring Deductions.)

To edit a recurring deduction, do the following:

  1. Enter the Limit amount, which is the most that the system can deduct in a payroll period. This amount overrides any limit defined for this deduction code. If you do not enter a limit here, then any limits defined for this deduction code apply.

  2. Enter the Maximum amount the system can deduct on a monthly, quarterly, yearly, or lifetime basis, as set in the Basis field. Any maximum set here overrides the maximums defined for the deduction code. If you do not enter a maximum here, then any maximums set for the deduction code apply.

Note: When a rehired employee’s lifetime maximum deduction amount is reached as based on their past deductions and their rehired deduction amount, the deduction stops occurring.

  1. Select the Basis to which the Maximum applies: Monthly, Quarterly, Annually, Lifetime, or Pay Period.

Note: Note the following when using the Pay Period option:

  • Selecting Pay Period processes the deduction once per pay period, which can only be used in conjunction with a voluntary deduction type. (If you select a deduction type for a non-voluntary deduction type, then the Pay Period option does not display.) In addition, there is no requirement for a maximum amount when you set the basis by pay period.

  • To allow the system to process arrears, if you select the Pay Period option you cannot add an amount in the Maximum field. (The system disables the Maximum field.)

  • When set to Pay Period in the following scenario for regular, special, or manual payrolls, the system only processes voluntary deductions once per pay period:

  • The voluntary deduction must be configured in the Recurring Deductions form.

  • The deduction type must be Voluntary.

  1. For Voluntary Deductions, you can select Track Arrears. When you select this option, if the deduction amount for this employee cannot be taken due to insufficient earnings, it will go into arrears.

  2. Select Mandatory if this deduction is for goods or services provided to the employee that are a mandatory part of employment.

  3. Enter a Start Date; the system begins processing the deduction on or after this date.

  4. Enter a Stop Date; the system stops processing this deduction on or after this date.

  5. For Voluntary Deductions, you can enter a G/L Override Acct to use rather than the default account number for this deduction.

  6. The Third Party Payee Code to establish a payment to a designated payee.

  7. Enter the Match Method used to calculate the match, either Flat or Percent.

  8. Enter the Match Amount as either a flat amount or a percentage, depending on the Match Method.

  9. Enter a Match Description to print on the Batch Match Code Summary report.

  10. Select the Rate Table.

  11. Select the Rate Tier.

  12. Select one of the ACH Options to associate a deduction with a direct deposit account.

Note: Note the following:

  • You must enable the VOLUNTARYDEDACH custom feature code on the System Parameters form to display the ACH Options field.

  • The ACH Options field only displays for deduction code types that are Voluntary with one of the following Calculation Methods, as configured on the Deduction Codes form:

  • % of Gross Pay

  • % of Gross Earnings

  • Fixed Amount

  1. Click Save to save the detail record and return to the Recurring Deductions form.
