Employee Garnishments

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Change/Employee_Garnishment.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Change/Employee_Garnishment.htm

Submitting Employee Wage Garnishments

You can enter employee wage garnishments using the Employee Garnishments form.

When a company is instructed to garnish employee’s wages, the notice of a garnishment typically includes specific instructions on how to deduct the garnishment. Garnishment checks are printed along with paychecks in a payroll batch to ensure prompt delivery to the payee.

The system includes these garnishment calculation features:

  • State garnishment rules

  • State tax levies that are not limited by CCPA limits

  • Pro rata and Equal Share child support calculations

  • Priority and limit calculation logic when dealing with multiple garnishment types

  • Garnishment fees set up on rule record, but can be overridden for an individual order

  • Monthly garnishment fee maximums handled automatically

  • State garnishment rules determine if child support arrears should be deducted from supplemental pay checks

Note: Note:

  • If under the Override Rules section, there is an Override Amount indicated and an Override Start Date and an Override Stop Date is not mentioned, then this override amount will be used to process payroll regardless of the date.

  • Clicking the fields that display as hyperlinks on this form opens a search criteria form; for example, clicking Payee opens the Select Payee form, where you can select an existing payee.

  • Information for the following fields does not display for deidentified employees:

  • Docket Number

  • Annotation

  • Case Identifier

The options available on the form vary based on the category of garnishment:

  • Child Support Garnishments

  • Spousal Support Garnishments

  • IRS Tax Levy Garnishments

  • State Tax Levy Garnishments

  • Franchise Tax Board Garnishments

  • Bankruptcy Order Garnishments

  • Creditor Wage Garnishments

  • Student Loan Garnishments

Setting Up and Tracking Employee Loans

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Change/Employee_Loans.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Change/Employee_Loans.htm

Setting Up and Tracking Employee Loans

Use the Employee Loans form to establish employee loan information, track the payment of the loan, and view loan payments that were deducted from employee paychecks.

Outside of this form, you can track arrears against the employee loan using one of two methods, which are described in Tracking Arrears.

When you set up a new loan for an employee, PrismHR automatically generates a unique loan identification number. You then enter the amount, date, and reason (optional) for the loan, as well as the employee’s payment deduction amount and frequency.

The Employee Loans panel in the Employee Loans form establishes the information required for the employee loan. Click the Data Import Tool icon (

[Image: screenshot]

) to upload a database file and import data. For more information, see Using the Data Import Tool.

Note: Note the following:

  • Users whose user role is set to DENY for the Employee Loans form cannot import data using the Employee Loans import template and subsequently, the Data Import Tool icon will not display on the Employee Loans form.

  • Users whose user role is set to INQUIRY for the Employee Loans form, but whose user role is also set to DENY for the Data Import Tool cannot view the Import icon on the Employee Loans form.

  • Users whose user role is set to INQUIRY for the Employee Loans form can view the Employee Loans import template, but cannot import data.

Setting Up an Employee Loan

To set up an employee loan, do the following:

  1. Enter an existing Loan Number or click Set up a new loan. PrismHR assigns the loan numbers.

  2. Enter the Employee by either entering the name, Social Security Number, or ID to display a pop-up list of matching employee records. You can also click the field label or press Ctrl+Enter with your cursor in this field to open the search window. This is the employee who is responsible for the loan.

  3. Enter the Loan Date on which this loan was granted.

  4. Enter the Loan Amount granted to the employee. This value must be greater than zero.

  5. Enter the Reason for Loan.

  6. Enter the Loan Payment amount to deduct automatically from each paycheck in order to repay the loan.

  7. Select the Payment Frequency for the payroll deduction; the default is once per pay period.

  8. Enter the Payback Amount required to consider the loan paid in full, which is the amount of this loan plus interest (if any).

  9. Enter the Deduction Start Date on which payroll deductions will begin to pay back the loan.

  10. Enter the Deduction Stop Date on which payroll deductions will cease.

Note: If you do not enter a Stop Date, PrismHR continues to deduct loan payments until the Payback Amount has been satisfied.

  1. Select the Deduction Code used for the employee loan.

  2. Enter the G/L Override Account code to which this deduction is credited. This is used only in the Corporate Edition.

  3. Enter or select the Payee for the employee loan.

Note: Only payees who have the Loans payee type on the Payees form display in the Select Payee list. Also, you can only enter or select a Payee whose Third Party Format for the Processor ID associated with the Payroll Check Account is set to Cachet or –Select– on the ACH Originators form.

  1. The Amount Paid field displays the amount that the employee has paid back on this loan to date. If you are creating a record for a loan where the employee has already made some payments, enter the total paid to date in this field.

  2. Click Save.

Tracking Loan Payments

The Payments panel displays the payment history of the employee loan. It lists the date of payment, the associated voucher, the ACH reference, such as a garnishment, and the payment amount.

Note: The ACH file includes the employee loan deduction amount, the routing and account number, and the client ID and employee ID.

Tracking Arrears

Use one of the following methods to track arrears on an employee loan:

  • Deduction Codes form: Enter or select an Employee Loan Deduction code in the Deduction Code field, then select the To Arrears field. For example:

[Image: Deduction code with the “to arrears” option selected]

  • Control tab on the Client Details form: Enter or select an Employee Loan Deduction code in the Voluntary/Employee Loan Deductions To Arrears field. (Previously, this field was titled Voluntary Deductions To Arrears.) For example:

[Image: Voluntary/Employee Loan Deductions to Arrears grid in the Arrears panel]

Note: Note the following when using the arrears feature:

  • After an employee loan transfers to arrears, it displays on the Employee Deduction Arrears form, which is accessible from the Payroll|Change menu, and on the Deduction Arrears form, which is accessible from the Actions menu [Image: screenshot] on the Employee Details form.

  • An employee loan in arrears displays in the Payroll Deduction in Arrears Report, which is accessible from the Payroll|Report menu. (See the Payroll Reports Guide.)

After you setup the tracking method, here’s what happens with the arrears based on the Payment Frequency selected in the Employee Loans form:

  • Once Each Payroll Period (default): Transfers to arrears and deducted from arrears on each payroll for the employee.

  • Once a Month: Transfers to arrears and deducted from arrears on the next payroll for the employee. After that occurrence, the deduction always occurs on the first payroll of the month.

Recording Partial Arrears Amounts

The system records a partial arrears amount in the To Arrears panel (portion that is placed into arrears) or the From Arrears panel (portion of the arrears amount from previous pay period that displays as being deducted) in the Deductions tab on the Payroll Voucher form, if the employee is only paid enough to deduct some of the loan deduction amount.

The Loan # column in the To Arrears panel or the From Arrears panel displays the loan number from the Employee Loan form that allows loan arrears to display separately based on the loan number, if an employee has more than one employee loan.

Note: Note: If an employee has multiple loans that transfer to arrears or from arrears with the same deduction code on the same date, the system displays multiple rows (one for each loan) in the Loan # column.

Override Rates

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Change/Employee_Override_Rates.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Change/Employee_Override_Rates.htm

Override Rates

In the Employee Override Rates form, you can define a different pay rate for each pay code used to pay the employee. For all other pay codes, the system defaults to the employee’s standard pay rate.

For example, an employee regularly works as a server but occasionally tends bar. Because the hours worked in each position vary from one week to the next, the client should have pay codes for each position. The pay voucher displays the amount earned as a server and as a bartender.

  1. The Employee ID defaults from the Employee Details form.

  2. For each pay code:

a. Enter the Pay Code that represents the pay to override.
  1. — Enter the Pay Rate for that pay code. If you leave this field blank, the system calculates the pay using the employee’s rate in the payroll record. Premium pay rules apply.
  1. Click Save.

Employee Position Rates

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Change/Employee_Position_Rates.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Change/Employee_Position_Rates.htm

Defining Employee Position Rates

You can pay the employee or bill the client at different rates based on the employee pay rates and positions by using the Employee Position Rates form.

Note: Note: For example, if an employee should typically be paid $10.00 per hour when working in the retail position but $15.00 per hour for PTO, enter the employee’s ID, the position code, and 10.00 for the Standard Pay Rate, then enter the PTO Pay Code in the table and 15.00 for the Pay Rate and the appropriate Bill Rate.

To define employee position rates, do the following:

  1. Enter the Employee by either entering the name, Social Security Number, or ID to display a pop-up list of matching employee records. You can also click the field label or press Ctrl+Enter with your cursor in this field to open the search window. If any employees have position rates defined, they display in the list on the right; you can select one to edit or enter a new one.

  2. Enter the Position Code for the position that applies to this position rate.

  3. If you enter a Standard Pay Rate, it overrides the pay rate for this employee for the position.

  4. To pay or bill different rates based on pay code and pay rate:

  1. — Enter the Pay Code for this position. The Pay Description displays. If you enter a code that is not defined for the client, the system displays a warning message to confirm that you want to use that code.
b. Enter the Pay Rate that overrides the Standard Pay Rate. Premium pay rules apply.
  1. — Enter the Bill Rate for this employee performing in this position. If you don’t enter a rate, the system, uses the standard billing rate.
  1. Click Save.

Fringe Benefit Pay Entry

Use the Fringe Benefit Pay Entry form to enter fringe benefit pay adjustments.

WARNING: This function was designed specifically to exclude FICA (Medicare and OASDI) in the tax basis. The Fringe Benefit Pay Entry creates an adjustment voucher for the specified employee that updates the amount of the defined non-cash fringe pay code, defined taxable wages for federal and state income taxes (for the state you specify), and taxable wages for federal unemployment.

[Image: screenshot]

  4. Enter the Employer ID that should be affected by this adjustment.

Importing Tax Register Adjustments

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Change/Import-Tax-Reg-Adjustments.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Change/Import-Tax-Reg-Adjustments.htm

Importing Tax Register Adjustments

Tax registers contain a running total of amounts deducted from employee paychecks or contributed by their employer. You can process tax adjustments when required such as when an employee has an incorrectly assigned withholding tax. Proceed carefully with the tax adjustment process. When you process a tax register adjustment, you are changing the only record of taxes withheld for employees in the system.

Note: Note: This form does not use Client Access Group Security.

This procedure describes how to import an Employee or Payroll Tax Adjustment into PrismHR. Information is also provided to view the appropriate voucher once the tax adjustment import has occurred. The steps involved are:

  • Creating a Spreadsheet

  • Importing the Tax Adjustment

  • Verifying Imported Tax Information

Important! The import process does not currently support billing, so you must leave the Suppress Billing column blank in the import file or use “Y” in that column.

Creating a Spreadsheet

To create this spreadsheet:

  1. Create an Excel Spreadsheet with this tax import information. Remove any commas or headers in your data to avoid tax adjustment import problems.
Column Information
Col A Company ID
Col B Employee ID
Col C Adjustment Date (MM/DD/YYYY)
Col D Employer ID
Col E Adjust Client Tax Register? (Y/N)
Col F Tax Code
Col G Exempt Pay
Col H Sheltered Earnings
Col I Gross Taxable
Col J Over Limit
Col K Tax Amount
Col L Suppress Billing? (Y/N)
Col M School District
Col N Location
Col O Special Options Code
Col P Residential Geocode Override

  1. Save the Excel file as tab-delimited, pipe-delimited, or .csv.

  2. Record the file name and where it was saved.

Importing Tax Adjustments

To import tax adjustment information:

  1. Select Tax Adjustment Import from the Payroll|Change menu. The Tax Adjustment Import form displays.

  2. Set these optional fields to match the contents of your import file:

  • Delimiter: Separates the data fields in the import .txt file. Let the system determine the delimiter (default, Auto) or set the delimiter to the separator type in the import tile (Comma, Tab, Pipe).

  • Qualifier: Used in conjunction with delimiters in fields. Qualifiers are placed around each field to indicate that it’s the same field. The most common qualifier is a double quote. Additional options are Auto (default), None, and Single Quote.

  • First Lines to Skip: Instructs the system to ignore a specific number of lines (column headers) in an import file. The default is zero (0), and up to 10 lines can be skipped.

  1. Click Upload File. A file upload dialog box displays.

  2. Click Choose File and navigate to the file you created.

  3. Highlight the file name and click Open, then click submit. The system displays whether the file uploaded successfully and how long the upload took.

  4. Click Close. The file contents display as a preview.

  5. If there are errors, an error report displays. (Note: These items cannot be imported.) For example:

[Image: screenshot]

  1. Change the Delimiter, Qualifier, or First Lines to Skip selection to clear the errors. The Reload Preview Data button displays.

  2. Click Reload Preview Data to extract the data again using the updated settings without uploading the file again, which might fix the errors. (If errors still display, edit the external file and upload it again to correct the errors.)

  3. If the edited external file displays valid data, a preview report displays. (These are items you can post to create tax adjustments.)

  4. To create tax adjustment vouchers and post them to tax registers, click Create Adjustments. (The posting process runs in the background, so there is a short delay until it finishes.)

  5. When the posting process finishes the report displays associated messages, such as “Done. 3 tax adjustment vouchers were created.”

Note: If the data file contains multiple lines for the same employee, where only the tax codes and amounts are different, the process now combines them onto one voucher instead of creating a separate voucher for each line.

Verifying Tax Adjustment Information

To view the imported tax adjustment information:

  1. Open the Employee Payroll Vouchers screen (found under Payroll|View).
  2. Enter the appropriate Employee ID.
  3. Select the appropriate Year. A list of employee vouchers is generated.
  4. Select the appropriate Voucher Number. The system displays the Payroll Voucher dialog. [Image: screenshot]
  5. Click the Tax tab. [Image: screenshot]
  6. Locate the tax adjustments under the appropriate panels (for example, Employer Tax).
  7. Click Close.========================================================================

Importing Employee Tax Basis from Successor

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Change/Import-Transfer-Tax-Basis.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Change/Import-Transfer-Tax-Basis.htm

Importing Employee Tax Basis from Successor

Use this process to transfer the employee tax basis to PrismHR for a client that has come on midyear to ensure accurate voucher calculations. This could occur for employees that work for a client reporting SUI state (such as Michigan). It could also occur for certified PEOs that import federal taxes from a successor.

If an employee has already reached their tax limit for SUI before being moved to a PEO that uses PrismHR software, then a mechanism is required to import earlier tax data for the employee, or they will start accruing tax again.

Note: Note: This form does not use Client Access Group Security.

To import the tax transfer basis:

  1. Format an Excel spreadsheet using this format. | Column | Information | | — | — | | Col A | Client ID | | Col B | Employee ID | | Col C | Employer ID | | Col D | Tax Year | | Col E | Reason | | Col F | Billing Only? (Use only Y, N or S) Y=Yes, N=No and S=Suppressed for the billing | | Col G | Tax Code | | Col H | Tax Basis | | Col I | Tax Amount |
  2. Save the Excel file as tab-delimited, pipe-delimited, or .csv.
  3. Record the file name and where it was saved.
  4. Click Back Office [Image: screenshot] .
  5. From Operations|Import Processing, click Import Transfer Tax Basis from Successor.
  6. Click Upload File.
  7. Set these optional fields if required:
  • Delimiter- Separates the data fields in the import .txt file. Let the system determine the delimiter (default, Auto) or set the delimiter to the separator type in the import tile (Comma, Tab, Pipe).
  • Qualifier- Used in conjunction with delimiters in fields. Qualifiers are placed around each field to indicate that it’s the same field. The most common qualifier is a double quote. Additional options are Auto (default), None, and Single Quote.
  • First Lines to Skip - Instructs the system to ignore a specific number of lines (column headers) in an import file. The default is 0, and up to 10 lines can be skipped.
  1. Click Upload File. A file upload dialog box displays.
  2. Click Choose File and navigate to the file you created.
  3. Highlight the file name and click Open, then click submit. The system displays a message about whether the file uploaded successfully and how long the upload took.
  4. Click Close. The file contents display as a preview. [Image: screenshot]
  5. Click Import to write values to the appropriate tax registers. [Image: screenshot]

Adjusting Incorrectly Posted Pay and Deduction Amounts

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Change/Pay_Deduction_Register_Adjustments.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Change/Pay_Deduction_Register_Adjustments.htm

Adjusting Incorrectly Posted Pay and Deduction Amounts

Do not use the Pay/Deduction Register Adjustment form unless you completely understand the implications of making adjustments to tax registers. If you are unsure how to use it, contact the System Administrator.

The Pay/Deduction Register Adjustment form is designed for adjusting pay and deduction amounts that have been posted to the incorrect pay or deduction code. When entering pay and deduction amounts, the amounts you enter must balance. For example, if you enter in $100 against pay code REG, you must enter a corresponding -$100 against another like pay code. The net effect of the adjustment must balance to zero. You cannot use this feature to increase or decrease an employee’s overall YTD net paycheck. To do so, you must process a pay event.

Note: This process is intentionally designed to not generate any accounting or tax consequential entries. As such, the amounts you enter must balance within pay classes and deduction types. For example, you cannot enter $100 to REG and -$100 to an expense reimbursement pay code. To do so would have tax and accounting entries.

Similarly, the deduction amounts you enter must balance within deduction types. The deduction type categories are however broader than the total of all system deduction types. The amounts must balance within three categories:

  • Section 125 Benefit Plan Deductions (including Client voluntary that are coded as such)

  • 401(k) Deductions (including Client voluntary that are coded as such)

  • All other deduction types

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Note: This adjustment feature does not generate any accounting entries.

To use this option:

  1. Click New Adjustment.

  2. Enter the Employee ID or click the link to display a list of employees.

  3. For each adjustment:

  1. — Enter the Adjustment Date. The system uses this date to derive the tax year, quarter, and month to be adjusted.

  2. — Enter the Weeks Worked. This is the adjustment to the year-to-date balance of the number of weeks worked.

  3. — Enter the Days Worked. This is the adjustment to the year-to-date balance of the number of days worked.

  4. — Enter the Pay Code or click the link to display a list of pay codes. The Pay Code is the pay to be adjusted.

  5. — Enter the Hours Worked. This is the adjustment to the number of hours worked in association with the code in the Pay Code field.

  6. — Enter the Amount of the adjustment. This is the adjustment amount in association with the code in the Pay Code field. The total of the values in this column must equal zero (0). For example, an employee was originally slated to be paid for 42 hours using the REG pay code. You want to adjust their pay to reflect 2 hours paid using the SHIFT pay code. You type the values REG, -2, and -20.00 in the first line’s Pay Code, Hours Worked, and Amount fields and SHIFT, 2, and 20.00 in the second line.

  7. — Enter the Deduction Code or click the link to display a list of deduction codes. This is the deduction to be adjusted.

  8. — Enter the Amount. This is the amount to be adjusted in association with the code in the Deduction Code field. It works in a similar fashion to the Pay Code and the total of the values in this column must equal zero (0).

  9. — Enter the Reference Number. If the adjustment is an employee or 401(k) loan, enter the loan number. If it is a garnishment, enter the docket number.

  1. Click Post to save the information .

Establishing Pay Groups

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Change/Pay_Groups.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Change/Pay_Groups.htm

Establishing Pay Groups

Use the Pay Groups form to set up a group of employees who are all paid on the same day. You must assign every employee in PrismHR to a pay group.

Use the Actions menu to access other information and setup forms:

  • Audit – see Viewing the Audit Log.

  • Pay Schedule Report – runs the Pay Schedule Report.

  • Pay Schedules – see Establishing Pay Schedules.

  • Show employees – lists employees enrolled in the pay group.

  • Time Sheet Defaults – defines default pay methods and pay codes for this group. When the timesheet is created, the system populates the default hours in the listed default pay code for employees assigned to that pay method. For example, if the pay method is Hourly and the pay code is REG2 in the Time Sheet Defaults panel, then employees with the Hourly pay method will have their default hours populated in the REG2 pay code in the timesheet.

Note: Note the following:

  • The Variable Salary option only displays if the VARSALMETHOD custom feature code is enabled on the System Parameters form.

  • After you enable the VARSALMETHOD custom feature code and select the Variable Salary option, this update takes effect in the next regularly scheduled payroll.

Defining a Pay Group

Define the pay group that represents a group of employees paid on the same day and establish the pay schedule using the Pay Group panel.

To define a pay group:

  1. Select a Payroll.

  2. From Payroll|Change, select Pay Groups.

[Image: screenshot]

  1. Complete these fields in the Pay Groups panel as required:

Field — Description

Pay Group — Enter the pay group code for the client.

Description — Enter a brief pay group description.

Pay Schedule — Enter the pay schedule for the pay group. If you change the pay schedule and employees are assigned to that schedule, the following message displays, “You cannot change the pay schedule of this pay group because there are employees assigned to it. You will need to create a new pay group and assign the employees to it using the Mass Change Pay Group form.”

Work Week Ends On — Select the day of the week that the work week ends on.

Processing Schedule — If needed, enter the processing schedule.

Obsolete — Select to designate that the pay group is no longer in use.

  1. Click Save.

Note: Select the Payroll Control link to access the Payroll Control form, where you can establish essential information for processing payroll in PrismHR.

Entering the Payroll Period in Progress Information

The Payroll Period in Progress panel displays the payroll and pay date information.

[Image: screenshot]

To set up in-progress payroll information:

  1. If this is a new pay group, enter the information for the first payroll period.

  2. Complete the following fields:

Field — Description

Payroll Number — The system automatically assigns the payroll number.

Pay Date — The effective date of the next payroll batch and the date that appears on the payroll check. If there are no payrolls pending for the pay group, enter the first valid pay date. Otherwise, this field is read-only.

Period Start Date — The first date of the payroll period. If you are creating a new pay group, enter the first day of the pay period.

Period End Date — The system calculates this date based on the start date and schedule. The Period Number is based on the number of periods possible to pay a group in one year: a weekly pay group has 52 pay periods, a Bi-weekly group has 26 periods, a semi-monthly pay group has 24 pay periods, and a monthly group has 12 periods.

Period Number — The system populates the period number that corresponds with the pay period.

  1. Click Save.

Entering the Alternate Billing Addresses

Use the Alternate Billing Address panel only if the billing for this pay group should go to a different address than what is listed on the Client Details > Account tab.

Note: Note: This alternate address affects billing only.

[Image: screenshot]

Enter the alternate billing address information (if required).

Performing Pre-ACH Maintenance

Use the Pre-ACH Maintenance panel to test ACH files a specified number of days before running payroll to ensure that all transactions can be completed.

Note: Note: See Pre-ACH Processing

[Image: screenshot]

To set up or maintain Pre-ACH settings for a pay group:

  1. Make sure to specify the appropriate pay group. Its information populates on the form.

  2. If appropriate, select the number of Pre‑ACH Days. The system sends a pre‑ACH file ahead of the regular ACH file by the number of days selected. This number must be less than the cycle length for the feature to work correctly.

If your organization is not using pre‑ACH processing for this pay group, you must set this field to ‑‑Select‑‑.

  1. The system can use either an average or a flat amount for the pre‑ACH:
Pre-ACH Amount Type Details
Average Use the pre‑ACH invoice fields to specify an average for up to five invoices. You can enter any information in the Pre‑ACH Invoice Number and Pre‑ACH Invoice Amount columns, because the system does not verify it. For example, if you are setting up a pre‑ACH prenote on the client for the first time and plan to use five invoices for the average that will typically be around $10,000, you can enter five “starter” invoices using any invoice number (for example, START1, START2, START3, and so on) and enter $10,000 for each. When the system processes a real payroll, it drops the first starter invoice from the list and inserts a real invoice at the end. After the first five payrolls, all the starter invoices are no longer on the list. The system sends pre‑ACH prenotes using the average of the invoices in the list. After five payrolls, the average will be based on actual data. - The system lists each Pre‑ACH Invoice Number in the chain for seeking the current average to pre‑ACH. You can enter different invoice numbers. - The Pre‑ACH Invoice Amount is each invoice’s contribution amount. You can enter a different amount to force a new average. The Current Average displays below the table.
  • The system lists each Pre‑ACH Invoice Number in the chain for seeking the current average to pre‑ACH. You can enter different invoice numbers.
  • The Pre‑ACH Invoice Amount is each invoice’s contribution amount. You can enter a different amount to force a new average. | Flat | Enter the Pre‑ACH Override to use a flat amount rather than the Current Average of invoices and amounts. If you use the flat method, the system always uses that amount for pre‑ACH for the client and this pay group. The system never checks nor averages the invoice amounts. |
  1. If setting up Pre-ACH for the first time, enter the batch number of any completed batch in the Pre‑ACH Batch Number field.

For each pay group, the daily Pre-ACH program compares the in-progress batch number with the batch number entered in this field. If these are identical, the system skips the in-progress batch for Pre-ACH processing. When you enter the ID of a previously completed batch, you indicate that PrismHR needs to process the in-progress batch for Pre-ACH. The system will evaluate the in-progress batch for processing, create the appropriate ACH entries, and automatically update this field with the in-progress batch number. This prevents double entries from occurring.

Note: Note: In the case where Pre-ACH entries were already created for a batch, but this batch was later deleted and re-created (therefore giving it a new batch number), you must manually update this field with the new batch number. For example, assume a Pre‑ACH prenote was sent for batch 202202, but for some reason you decided to delete that batch and create the next regular payroll batch to replace it. If the system assigns number 202205 to the new batch, you must change the value in the Pre-ACH Batch Number field from 202202 to 202205. This ensures that PrismHR does not re-transmit the Pre-ACH entry.

  1. Click Save.

Establishing Information for Processing Payrolls

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Change/Payroll_Control.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Change/Payroll_Control.htm

Establishing Information for Processing Payrolls

You can use the Payroll Control form to establish essential information for processing payroll in PrismHR. There are three types of payrolls that users can process: regularly scheduled, manual, and special/unscheduled batches. You determine the payroll type using the Payroll Type field.

PrismHR uses the parameters defined in the Payroll Control form to automatically schedule the next batch.

  • Regularly Scheduled: Following the successful completion of a payroll, PrismHR automatically creates a new Payroll Control record for the next regularly scheduled payroll. The regularly scheduled payroll includes time sheets for each employee scheduled to be paid in the payroll. Payroll processors can add or delete time sheets as necessary.

Note: Note: When deleting a payroll, Full access users have the option of copying saved entries, which can be applied to a new payroll without having to re-import or re-enter the data. After clicking Yes in the first two confirmation dialogs that display when you click Delete in the Payroll Control form, a third confirmation dialog displays, “Do you want to keep the keyed entries and apply them to the new payroll?” Click Yes to copy all saved entries and charge dates (including entries in the deduction columns) into a new payroll batch. Clicking No produces a blank timesheet. (Previously accepted Pay Rates and Leave Requests remain unchanged.)

In addition, if you try to delete a payroll where a reverse wire transfer journal exists an error displays, “Payroll <XXX> can not be deleted as the ACH journals have already been created.”

  • Special/Unscheduled: Enter a payroll for specific pay groups.

  • Manual: Enter a supplemental or unscheduled payroll for one or more employees.

Note: Note: You can also use the form to view in progress or past payrolls. However, you cannot edit posted payrolls, and you cannot create regularly scheduled payrolls.

You can access other information using the Actions menu:

  • Viewing the Audit Log

  • Setting Special Processing Options

  • Setting Up Pay Group Accruals

  • Processing History

  • Adding Employees to a Payroll

Identifying the Payroll and Type

You can identify the payroll and type in the Payroll Control panel. This panel also displays the current status. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

To identify the payroll and type:

  1. If necessary, select the Calendar Year in which the payroll batch occurs. The default is the current year.

  2. Select an existing payroll or create a new one:

  • Click New Payroll to create the new payroll. The system automatically generates a payroll number.

  • Click Payroll Number and then select the payroll you want to edit. The Payroll Control form populates with the information for that payroll. If the payroll is not finalized, you can make edits as needed.

  1. The Payroll Type indicates the type of payroll.

  • If you are creating a new payroll, select either Manual or Special.

  • If you are editing an existing payroll, you cannot change the type.

  1. If you select Manual as the Payroll Type, select the Reason, so you can track the reason why the client is processing manual payrolls. (This field only displays if you select Manual as the Payroll Type.)

Note: The Reason field is required if the Require Manual Payroll Reason field on the System Parameters form is enabled.

  1. If appropriate, enter a Description that identifies this payroll.

Note: Note the following:

  • When administering payrolls, you cannot enter or select any International Employees (set on the Address tab in the Employee Details form, see Establishing and Maintaining Employee Address Information) in the Employee panel.

  • For completed regular payrolls, you can click View Timesheet to see the time sheet information. (This link is not available for incomplete payrolls.)

  • For payrolls in the Wire Transfer Pending status, you can click the Reset Wire Transfer link to set the payroll back to Payroll Pending Review status. See Processing Payroll: Wire Transfer Pending Status.

  • Select the Pay Group link in the Related Actions section to access the Pay Groups form, where you can set up a group of employees who are all paid on the same day.

Identifying Payroll Processing Information

You can identify the payroll processor and establish the payroll date and time information in the Payroll Processor panel. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

  1. If available, enter the user ID of the Payroll Processor for this payroll. The system defaults to the processor specified in the Account tab of Client Details. See Maintaining Client Contact and Account Assignment Information.

  2. Enter the Pay Date on which to process the payroll. The Quarter End Date, Year End Date, and G/L Period for the payroll display.

Note: When you set a manual payroll to Pay On-Demand on the Payroll Options form and configure that payroll on the Payroll Control form, the system automatically sets the Pay Date to the current date since the employee will be paid today (instant payment).

The following happens:

  • If you try to change that automated Pay Date the system displays a warning, “This is a Pay On-Demand payroll so the Pay Date must be the current date.” (Click OK to continue.)

  • If you enter or select a Pay Date that is not the current date and then select the Pay On-Demand field on the Payroll Options form the system displays a warning, “Pay On-Demand payroll must be paid using the current date. By selecting this option the pay date is updated to today.” (Click OK to continue.)

After you click Accept and return to the Payroll Control form, the system automatically changes the Pay Date to the current date.

  1. Enter the Remote Cutoff Date by which the client must report time data.

Note: The Remote Cutoff Date and Remote Cutoff Time fields only apply if the client enters their own time sheets; this is indicated on the Client Details Control tab.

  1. Enter the Remote Cutoff Time.

  2. Enter the Delivery Date on which the payroll checks should be delivered.

  3. If you are entering a Manual payroll, you can select the Override Pay Period to use as an alternate period to the one defined for the pay group.

Reviewing Shipping Information

Once the posting is complete and the payroll is marked as “Mailed,” the Shipping Information displays. These fields are informational only and cannot be edited. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Identifying Pay Groups or Employees

Use the third panel to identify who is associated with the payroll, either Pay Groups or Employees. For example:

  • Pay Groups: Regularly Scheduled or Special payrolls. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

a. Enter the Pay Group associated with this payroll. The Description displays.

  1. — Enter the Period Start date, which must be the first day of the payroll period for this payroll. The system uses this to select the time sheets to pay; the system selects only time sheets with a charge date within the period entered here.

  2. — Enter the Period End date, which must be the last day of the payroll period for this payroll. The system uses this date to select the time sheets.

  3. — Enter the number of Weeks Worked during the period, which the system uses to produce the Weeks Worked amount on the Quarterly FUTA/SUTA reports.

  4. — Enter the Deduction Period on which the pay date falls. The system uses this during payroll processing to take the appropriate standard payroll deductions for the employees in this pay group. The system takes only the deductions defined for this deduction period.

f. Enter the Pay Period number. The default populates based on the Period Start date.
  1. — Select the Alt Pay Period to use for this pay group. This overrides the period assigned to the pay group; for example, you can use the Annually option to calculate taxes on an annual basis for all wages paid to employees on the payroll, overriding the employee’s regular taxation basis as set by their pay group.
h. If appropriate, enter the Payroll Option Template for the pay group.

If a template was specified, you can click Show Template to see the options specified in that template.

  • Employees: Manual payrolls. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Note the following when using the Pay On-Demand feature:

  • When a manual payroll is set to Pay On-Demand, only employees with an active pay on-demand account display in the list when you select an Employee. (This also applies when selecting employees using the Quick Load option.) If you enter an Employee who does not have an active pay on-demand account an error message displays, “Employee <xxxxx> must have an active Pay On-Demand account to be added to a Pay On-Demand payroll.”

  • When you’re ready to set up a manual payroll as Pay On-Demand, it’s important to note that if you enter employees who do not have a pay on-demand account in their employee record before setting the payroll to Pay On-Demand on the Payroll Options form and click Save, the following error message displays:

[Image: screenshot]

In this situation, make a selection as follows:

  • Yes: Employees without an active pay on-demand account are removed from the payroll, then you can click Save again and the payroll will save.

  • No: Employees without an active pay on-demand account are not removed, but you cannot save the payroll. At this point, you must either disable Pay On-Demand or manually remove these employees from the payroll.

  • If you try to disable the Pay On-Demand field on the Payroll Options form after payroll calculation completes, this field is dimmed and you cannot make this change.

  • To add many employees to the payroll at once:

  1. — You can click Quick Load to open the Payroll Control Quick Load form and easily select the employees to include in the payroll.
  • To enter or edit information for each employee:

  1. — Enter the Employee IDs to include in the manual payroll. You can only add employees who have completed the onboarding process; this ensures that the tax information is complete before they are included in a payroll.

  2. — Enter the Period Start date, which must be the first day of the payroll period for this payroll. The system uses this to select the time sheets to pay; the system selects only time sheets with a charge date within the period entered here.

  3. — Enter the Period End date, which must be the last day of the payroll period for this payroll. The system uses this date to select the time sheets.

  4. — Enter the number of Weeks Worked during the period, which the system uses to produce the Weeks Worked amount on the Quarterly FUTA/SUTA reports.

  5. — Enter the Deduction Period on which the pay date falls. The system uses this during payroll processing to take the appropriate standard payroll deductions for the employee. The system takes only the deductions defined for this deduction period.

g. If appropriate, enter the Payroll Option Template for the employee.

Note: Note the following:

  • If a template was specified, you can click Show Template to see the options specified in that template.

  • If you apply a Payroll Option Template that is set to ACH to a manual Pay On-Demand payroll and click Save, the following error message displays:

[Image: screenshot]

Click OK to continue, then select a non-ACH Payroll Option Template.

Adding a Memo to Payroll Check Stubs

You can use the Memo panel to enter a memo that will display on all payroll check stubs included in this payroll. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

As a service provider user managing client check configuration, you can use substitution variables in client check messages, so that paychecks can display contextual employee and work-assignment information in the check message on a client-by-client basis.

You can enter the following substitution variables either in the Message Text section on the Check Massages form or in the Memo section on the Payroll Control form:

  • Worksite Location - {{HOME.LOCATION}}

  • Position - {{HOME.POSITION}}

  • Division - {{HOME.DIVISION}}

  • Department - {{HOME.DEPARTMENT}}

  • Work Shift - {{HOME.WORK.SHIFT}}

  • Project - {{HOME.PROJECT}}

  • Work Group - {{HOME.WORK.GROUP}}

  • Client Name - {{CLIENT.LEGAL.NAME}}

Note: Note: The Client Name comes from the Client Details form, while the other variables come from the Employee Details form.

  1. Enter up to four Memo lines.

  2. Click Save.

Cloning Previous Payrolls

You can clone a previous payroll using the Clone Last Batch form, accessed from the Payroll Control Actions menu.

  1. Click New Payroll in Payroll Control.

  2. Open the Actions menu and select Clone Last Batch.

The Clone Last Batch form opens.

[Image: screenshot]

  1. Enter the payroll Batch Number that you want to clone. The default is the most recent completed payroll.

  2. Click Accept.

You return to the Payroll Control form, which populates with the information from the cloned payroll. Continue as you would with another payroll.

Setting Special Processing Options

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Change/Payroll_Control_Options.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Change/Payroll_Control_Options.htm

Setting Special Processing Options

You can set special processing options as needed for all employees included in the payroll batch using the Payroll Options form. To access the options, open a payroll in the Payroll Control form and then select Options from the Actions menu. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

To set special processing options:

  1. Select ACH in the Suppress ACH field to prevent the generation of direct deposit transactions. (Employees normally paid by direct deposit will receive paper checks instead.) For example, you might select this option when the client wants to deliver live checks for year-end bonuses.

Note: Note the following:

  • This field applies only to employee ACH processing. It does not suppress electronic billing.

  • If you select Suppress ACH with Pay On-Demand selected, an error message displays stating that they cannot be enabled for the same payroll.

  • If you create a manual payroll with Pay On-Demand selected and then apply a Payroll Option Template with Suppress ACH selected within a timesheet, an error message displays stating that they cannot be enabled for the same payroll and the system does not apply the Payroll Option Template.

  1. Select the ACH Earn Type Limiter to specify the voucher types that will be processed as ACH transactions. Voucher types that you do not specify will be processed as paper checks. This overrides the settings defined in the Employee Details Deposit tab.

  • Blank: All checks (regular, vacation, and supplemental)

  • R: Only regular checks

  • V: Only vacation checks

  • S: Only supplemental checks

  • RV: Only regular and vacation checks

  • RS: Only regular and supplemental checks

  • VS: Only vacation and supplemental checks

  1. Select Suppress Other Earnings from the Suppress Earnings drop-down to prevent payment for other earnings.

  2. From the Suppress Deductions drop-down, select what payroll deductions (other than payroll taxes) to suppress for this payroll batch, if any. For example, you might need to suppress retirement deductions from bonus pay if employees opt not to have it deducted.

Note: Note the following:

  • When you run a supplemental batch, the system ignores voluntary deductions.

  • The system sends benefit deductions to arrears.

  1. Select Suppress Arrears to prevent the deduction of any amounts in arrears.

  2. Select Suppress Garnishments to prevent garnishment deductions.

  3. Select Suppress Benefits Calculation to suppress withholding of any benefits deductions and benefit accruals/arrears calculations. If you suppress benefits for this payroll batch, the system does not calculate benefits for the pay period, and therefore no benefit deductions go to arrears.

  4. Select Suppress Benefits Update to suppress the benefit update step that updates benefit-related deduction amounts on employee standard deduction records.

The system normally updates the benefits on the employees’ standard deduction schedules according to the parameters set at the system level. For example, if you change the amount of the employees’ contributions on the Group Benefit Plan, the system updates the employees’ standard deduction schedule to reflect the change. Use the Suppress Benefits Update option to suppress that update.

  1. Select Suppress Benefit Adjustments to suppress the processing of benefits adjustments.

  2. Select Suppress Client Approval to except the payroll batch from the approval process. The payroll batch processes as if the client company does not use approvals.

  3. Select Suppress Client Bill Pending to suppress client bill pending for this batch.

  4. Select Suppress Loan Payment to suppress the loan payment from calculating and processing in the current payroll.

  5. Select Suppress Manual Checks to prevent a manual check from processing in the next regularly scheduled payroll and instead process it through a separate, special batch. (Note: This functionality is available for Scheduled and Special batches, but does not apply to Manual batches.)

  6. Enable Force Time Off Accruals to override standard time off accrual functionality for payrolls that are not yet initialized and are set to the Manual or Special/Unscheduled payroll type on the Payroll Control form.

Note: Enabling Force Time Off Accruals allows you to select specific time off plans for forced accrual in the Time Off Plans panel.

  1. Select Suppress Payday Notifications to suppress payday notifications at the batch level for regularly scheduled payrolls.

  2. Select Delivery Method Override to enter or select a delivery method in the Select a Delivery Method dialog box that displays. This will display on the payroll’s delivery sheet and delivery fee after payroll completes. Additionally, the system considers the Delivery Method Override field as a true override for the entire batch and when the override is set, no other delivery fees are applied.

  3. Select Delivery Message Override to enter a message in the Special Message field that will display on the payroll’s delivery sheet after payroll completes.

  4. Enter the Federal Tax Rate - Supplemental Pay, which is the rate to use as the federal tax percentage rate for all supplemental pay. This overrides the aggregate method.

  5. You can override the state tax percentage rate for all states, or for specific states.

  • All states: In the field, enter the State Tax Rate - Supplemental Pay, which is the rate to use for all supplemental pay. This overrides the rate for all states.

  • Specific states: In the table, enter the two-character State Code for each state that should use an override state tax rate, as well as the Supplemental Rate to use for each state.

  1. For a manual or special/unscheduled batch, enter the FSA Override Calculation Date that the system should use as the scheduled pay date for FSA calculations.

  2. Select FSA Reimbursement Batch to specify that this is a standalone payroll batch used only to process FSA reimbursements (must be defined in System Parameters).

  3. Enter or select the Benefit Calculation Date to override the actual pay date as the basis for benefit calculations that use an as of date.

  4. Select Force Retirement to Zero to set all retirement deductions to zero for the employees included in the payroll batch.

  5. Use the Show Future Dated Checks On ESS drop-down to indicate whether employees can view paychecks in the payroll that have future dates in Employee Self Service or Employee Portal (EP). This overrides the global setting.

  • Yes: Checks in this payroll batch with dates in the future display.

  • No or Select: Future checks do not display.

  1. Select Recalculate Overtime if the payroll batch should recalculate overtime rates. This option is available only for new payrolls.

Note: Enabling or disabling the Recalculate Overtime field in this form automatically sets the same status in the Recalculate Overtime field on the Batch Payments form.

  1. Select Replaces A Scheduled Batch to run this as an unscheduled payroll batch in place of a regular one.

  2. Select Apply Default T/S Hours to use the employees’ default time sheet hours, if any, in an unscheduled batch. If you do not select this option, all employees show 0.00 hours in the time sheet.

You must select this option when you first create the payroll; the system applies the default hours when it creates the new time sheets. If you save the payroll without selecting this option, and then select it later, the employees’ hours remain zero.

  1. Select Pay On-Demand to pay employees on-demand through a manual payroll, where the system places the funding information in a file format for the pay on-demand vendor.

Note: Note the following:

  • Manual payrolls set to Pay On-Demand do not use the ACH process.

  • A warning displays if you save a manual payroll with Pay On-Demand enabled and then later disable it, “By turning off Pay On-Demand any employees in this payroll may not be paid through the Pay On-Demand accounts which allow for same-day payment.”

  1. Click Accept. You return to the Payroll Control form.

  2. Click Save in the Payroll Control form.

Applying Payroll Option Template in Payroll Control

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Change/Payroll_Control_Payroll_Option_Template.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Change/Payroll_Control_Payroll_Option_Template.htm

Applying Payroll Option Template in Payroll Control

Users can apply a payroll option template as needed to employees in Payroll Control.

To apply a payroll option template:

  1. Use the Payroll Control form to open an existing payroll batch or create a new one; see Establishing Information for Processing Payrolls.

  2. You can apply the template to employees by entering it in the Payroll Option Templates column of the third panel in the form.

  • In Regularly Scheduled and Special payrolls, the template you enter will be applied to all employees in the pay group. You can make changes in the time sheet.

[Image: screenshot]

  • In Manual payrolls, you enter the template for each employee. You can enter them individually in the table, or apply them to the employees selected using the Quick Load option.

[Image: screenshot]

[Image: screenshot]

  1. In the Show Template column of the table in Payroll Control, you can click the icon to open a read-only form to see the selected payroll option template’s settings.

  2. Click Save.

Note: Note: If you change the payroll option template for a payroll where users are editing the time sheet or have initialized the batch, the system will prompt you to confirm that you want to update the batch and reset it to ready for time sheet entry (TS.ENTRY).

Using Payroll Control Quick Load

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Change/Payroll_Control_Quick_Load.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Change/Payroll_Control_Quick_Load.htm

Using Payroll Control Quick Load

Use the Payroll Control Quick Load form to add employees to the manual payroll.

Note: Note the following when using this form:

  • The list includes all employees at the company who are active or whose termination date is within the last 30 days. It does not include new employees who have not completed the onboarding process; this ensures that the tax information is complete before they are included in a payroll.

  • You can sort the list by clicking the header, for example, click Pay Group to sort the list by the pay groups. The first time you click a header, it sorts the list in ascending order (A-Z); the second click changes it to descending order (Z-A).

To access this form:

  1. Go to the Payroll Control form on the Payroll|Change menu.

  2. Select the Calendar Year, Payroll Number, or New Payroll, and the Manual option in the Payroll Type field.

  3. Select Quick Load next to the employee information panel.

To add employees to the manual payroll:

  1. Enter or select the Period Start Date, which must be the first day of the payroll period for this payroll. The system uses this to select the time sheets to pay; the system selects only time sheets with a charge date within the period entered here.

  2. Enter or select the Period End Date, which must be the last day of the payroll period for this payroll. The system uses this date to select the time sheets.

  3. Enter the number of Weeks Worked during the period, which the system uses to produce the Weeks Worked amount on the Quarterly FUTA/SUTA reports.

  4. Enter the Deduct Period on which the pay date falls. The system uses this during payroll processing to take the appropriate standard payroll deductions for the employee. The system takes only the deductions defined for this deduction period.

  5. If appropriate, enter or select the Payroll Option Template to apply to all the employees you select.

  6. Click Find Employees. The message “Please Wait!” displays while the list generates. (In addition, the buttons and input fields are disabled while the list generates.)

  7. To select the employees to include in the payroll:

  • Select the option at the top of the Select Active column to select every employee in the list. Afterwards, you can deselect any employees who should not be included in the payroll.

  • You can select or deselect each individual employee to include by selecting the option next to the Employee ID.

  1. Click Accept. You return to the Payroll Control form, where you enter other information about the payroll.

Maintaining Payroll Notes

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Change/Payroll_Notes.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Change/Payroll_Notes.htm

Maintaining Payroll Notes

You can maintain notes that are specific to a company or an employee within a company’s payroll batch on the Update Payroll Notes form. For example:

[Image: Update Payroll Notes form]

Note: To access the Update Payroll Notes form, select New Note in the Payroll Notes form, which displays on the Client|View menu. (For help using the read-only version of this form, Finalized Payroll Notes, see Working with Finalized Payroll Notes.)

To maintain notes:

  1. The Note Reference # displays the new or existing reference number generated by PrismHR.

  2. The Date, Time, and By fields display the information for when the user created the note.

  3. If this note applies to a specific employee, enter the Employee ID. If you do not enter an employee, the note applies to the client displayed in the top bar of the form.

Note: To quickly search for an employee, start entering the name. After a few keystrokes, the system displays a list of employee names that match.

  1. The Employee Status, Employee Type, Pay Group, and Location of the selected employee display.

  2. Select the Display Mode:

  • One Payroll: Once the payroll processor acknowledges the note, it no longer displays.

  • All Payrolls: The payroll processor must acknowledge the message each processing cycle.

  • Scheduled Payrolls: The note displays only for scheduled payrolls.

  1. Select Mark Urgent if this is an urgent note.

  2. Select Worksite User Viewable to allow worksite managers and worksite trusted advisors to view the note.

Note: The system automatically enables the Worksite User Viewable field after you select an employee. Therefore, you must disable this field to prevent worksite managers and worksite trusted advisors from viewing the note.

  1. Enter the date the note Expires On, if any. The note does not display after this date, even if it is set to display one time and no processor has acknowledged it.

  2. Enter the payroll Notes.

  3. If a user views the payroll note, that information displays in the table at the bottom of the form.

  4. Click Save, or click Complete to close the note and remove it from the current payroll note list on the main Payroll Notes form. You can then review the note history at a later date.

Note: After clicking Complete, you can only review the completed note on the Completed Payroll Notes form. (The information pertaining to who completed the note displays on that form.)

Creating Payroll Reason Codes

You can group and sort payroll reason codes using the Payroll Reason Codes form.

Note: This form is only available for service providers.

To create a new payroll reason code:

  1. Click [Image: screenshot] and select Payroll Reason Codes under System|Change.

  2. Enter or select a Payroll Reason Code (maximum of 10 characters) that represents the payroll’s reason. For example, select CNT (Client) or INT (Internal), which are pre-loaded in the Select Payroll Reason Codes list. The Description displays (maximum of 25 characters).

Note: The Description displays on the Payroll Control form, so users can select it.

  1. Click Save.

To obsolete an existing payroll reason code, click Obsolete Reason Code. (The obsolete payroll reason code will no longer display on the Payroll Control form.)

Reclassify Direct Deposit

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Change/Reclassify_Direct_Deposit.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Change/Reclassify_Direct_Deposit.htm

Reclassifying Direct Deposit

Use the Reclassify Direct Deposit form when a direct deposit cannot occur and you need to create an adjustment voucher. This process reverses the direct deposit and generates an adjustment voucher for the specified amount (this affects ACH processing). For example:

[Image: screenshot]

To create an adjustment voucher:

  1. Enter the Voucher Number. The voucher information displays.

  2. Select Yes from the ACH Send to Check drop-down on each appropriate line.

Note: If there are multiple ACH distribution lines and you do not want to send them all to a check at this time, you can reclassify the other lines later.

  1. Click Save. The system creates an adjustment voucher, which you can retrieve by accessing the Payroll|View|Payroll History form. (See Checks for Adjustments.)

Perform these steps to check that the system created an adjustment voucher:

  1. Check the payroll voucher:
a. Open Employee Payroll Vouchers (found in the Payroll menu under Payroll\ View).
  1. — Enter the Employee by either entering the name, Social Security Number, or ID to display a pop-up list of matching employee records. You can also click the field label or press Ctrl+Enter with your cursor in this field to open the search window.
c. Click the Voucher#. The Payroll Voucher opens.
d. Select the Banking tab and check the information.
— —
e. Click Close.
— —
  1. Make sure the payroll check has been sent to a voucher:
a. Open Reclassify Direct Deposit (found in the Payroll menu under Payroll\ Change).
b. Enter the Voucher Number.
— — —
  1. — Check the line(s) where you indicated that the information should be sent to a check. The Sent to Voucher Number should display.

Recurring Deduction Overrides

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Change/Recurring_Deduction_Overrides.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Change/Recurring_Deduction_Overrides.htm

Temporarily Overriding Deductions

Use the Recurring Deduction Overrides form to temporarily override one or more deductions for a specified employee’s paycheck. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

To temporarily override one or more deductions, do the following:

  1. Enter the Employee by either entering the name, Social Security Number, or ID to display a pop-up list of matching employee records. You can also click the field label or press Ctrl+Enter with your cursor in this field to open the search window.

Note: The Next Pay Date field displays informational date value that helps you to quickly identify the next regularly scheduled payroll batch date during the enrollment process.

  1. Select the Deduction Block Code to use for this override. If you select Block Individual Standard Deduction or Take On Supplemental Pay Voucher, use those panels to designate codes.

  2. Enter the Start Date when this temporary override goes into effect.

  3. Enter the End Date when this temporary override is no longer in effect.

  4. Click Save.

Designating Deduction Codes

Use the Block Individual Standard Deductions or Take Deductions on Supplemental Pay panel to designate which deduction codes to block or which deductions to take, if appropriate. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

To designate deduction codes to block or take, do the following:

  1. Enter the Start Date when this temporary override goes into effect. (Note: The Start Date and End Date are not required.)

  2. Enter the End Date when this temporary override is no longer in effect.

  3. Enter each Deduction Code. The Description displays.

  4. Click Save.

Recurring Deductions

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Change/Recurring_Deductions.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Change/Recurring_Deductions.htm

Working with Recurring Deductions

The Recurring Deductions form lists all payroll deductions, with the exception of payroll taxes. Use this form to enter voluntary deductions for the selected employee. For example:

[Image: Recurring deductions form]

There is no limit to the number of defined deduction codes you can enter for an employee. You cannot enter the same deduction code more than once for the same employee, however, with the exception of loans and garnishments.

Note: Note the following:

  • On the Recurring Deductions form, you can only edit voluntary deductions that are not associated with a plan.

  • If you enter or select a voluntary deduction with an assigned rebate bill code, an error message displays, “A Third Party Payee can only be applied to a Voluntary type deduction code with no Rebate Bill Code assigned. Check the deduction code settings or apply the Third Party Payee to an applicable code.” Click OK to continue.

  • If you enter or select a restricted deduction code (that is, a code not submitted on the Control tab in the Client Details form), a warning displays and you cannot save the record, “Warning - <deduction code> is not a deduction code defined on the <client> Client Detail Control tab.” Click OK to continue.

Note: Service providers can enable the ALLPAYCODESINT custom feature code on the System Parameters form to override the restriction listed above, so the system imports any deduction codes, including the allowed deduction codes that are defined in the Control tab on the Client Details form. (See Using Custom Feature Codes.)

  • When the first payroll for a pay period is processed with a zero ($0.00) amount without enough funds to cover a voluntary recurring deduction, the system takes the deduction on the next payroll for the same pay period, if there are funds available to cover it.

To enter voluntary deductions:

  1. Enter the Employee by either entering the name, Social Security Number, or ID to display a pop-up list of matching employee records. You can also click the field label or press Ctrl+Enter with your cursor in this field to open the search window. The system displays the current deductions.

Note: The Next Pay Date field displays informational date value that helps you to quickly identify the next regularly scheduled payroll batch date during the enrollment process.

  1. You can enter voluntary deductions. For each deduction to take:

  • Enter the Deduction Code. The corresponding Description, Type, Method, Benefit Plan, and Docket#/Loan#/FSA display as appropriate. If you enter a code that is not defined for the client, the system displays a warning message to confirm that you want to use that code.

  • Enter the deduction Amount. This is either a percentage or fixed amount, depending on the calculation method defined for the deduction code.

  • Enter the deduction Periods that determine when this deduction is taken from the employee’s net earnings after payroll taxes.

  • If additional deduction code details are required, click Edit Detail. The Employee Deduction Details form opens. (See Entering Employee Deduction Details.)

  1. Click Save.

Redirecting Direct Deposit Amounts

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Change/Redirect_Direct_Deposit.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Change/Redirect_Direct_Deposit.htm

Redirecting Direct Deposit Amounts

Use the Redirect Direct Deposit form to redirect a direct deposit (DD) to a different DD account after the ACH has already been processed for the voucher’s original direct deposit transaction. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

To redirect a direct deposit:

  1. Enter or select the Voucher Number. The voucher information displays.

  2. Enter or select a Redirect Deposit Date (required) to accurately date Redirect Direct Deposit vouchers and ACH Journals. (Clicking in this field automatically defaults to the current date.)

Note: Note the following:

  • When you update the Send to Account field to initiate a redirect of any existing deposits in the voucher and you save this information, the system uses the date from the Redirect Deposit Date field for creating both the adjustment vouchers and ACH Journal entries.

  • If you enter or select a date that is prior to the current system date an error message displays when you exit the field, “You’ve selected a date <number> days in the past which may cause issues in the bank file, would you like to continue with this date?” Click Yes to continue.

  1. Enter or select an Offset Date (required) for the offset voucher (which reverses the original transaction) that is different from the redirect voucher date (which reissues the payment).

Note: The system uses the Offset Date as the offset voucher’s pay date and the General Ledger (GL) posting date.

  1. Select the active checking or savings account where the direct deposit funds should be redirected in the Send to Account field on each appropriate line. After selecting the Send to Account, the Save button is enabled.

Note: The Send to Account options automatically display an abbreviated account identifier consisting of the last four numbers of the active checking or savings account number for the selected Voucher Number based on the line’s Transit Number and Bank Account Number. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

However, if there is only one currently active checking or savings account and the only currently active checking or savings account has a transit and routing number that matches the transit and account number, then only the –Select– option displays. In this case a warning displays, “There are no valid alternative Direct Deposit Accounts for this voucher.”

  1. Enter a Reason (up to 60 characters) for redirecting the direct deposit.

Note: You can view the reason in the Notes (reason area) on both the offset and redirect adjustment vouchers.

  1. Click Save.

After clicking Save, the system:

  • Creates an adjustment voucher that cancels out the original direct deposit transactions being moved to a new account.

  • Creates an adjustment voucher for the new direct deposit records for the Send to Account options, with a new ACH Journal record written for each new direct deposit on the adjustment voucher.

  • Displays a confirmation message, “New deposit has been submitted. Adjustment voucher <voucher number> posted.” Click OK to continue.

Note: Note the following:

  • If no direct deposit entries exist for the selected Voucher Number a message displays, “There are no direct deposits on this voucher.” After clicking OK in this message, the system clears the Voucher Number field.

  • If open ACH journals exist for the selected Voucher Number a message displays, “There are open ACH Journals for this voucher. Use the ACH Journal Edit/Entry form to update Direct Deposit Information.” After clicking OK in this message, the system clears the Voucher Number field.

Using Regular Payroll Control Quick Load

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Change/Regular_Payroll_Control_Quick_Load.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Change/Regular_Payroll_Control_Quick_Load.htm

Using Regular Payroll Control Quick Load

Use the Regular Payroll Control Quick Load form to add employees to a regular (scheduled) payroll.

Note: Note the following when using this form:

  • The list includes all employees at the company who are active or whose termination date is within the last 30 days. It does not include new employees who have not completed the onboarding process; this ensures that the tax information is complete before they are included in a payroll.

  • You can sort the list by clicking the header, for example, click Pay Group to sort the list by the pay groups. The first time you click a header, it sorts the list in ascending order (A-Z); the second click changes it to descending order (Z-A).

To access this form:

  1. Go to the Payroll Control form on the Payroll|Change menu.

  2. Select a Calendar Year, Payroll Number, or New Payroll.

  3. Select Add Employees to Payroll on the Actions menu.

  4. Select Quick Load. The Regular Payroll Control Quick Load form displays.

To add employees to a regular payroll:

  1. Enter or select the Add to Pay Group option. This field lists all pay groups associated with the Regular Scheduled Payroll. (If there is only one pay group, the system defaults to that selected pay group.)

  2. To select the employees to include in the payroll:

  • Click the checkbox under Select All to select every employee in the list. Afterwards, you can deselect any employees who should not be included in the payroll.

  • You can select or deselect each individual employee to include by selecting the option next to the Employee ID.

  1. Click Accept. You return to the Add Employees to Payroll form, where the employees you selected display.

  2. Click Accept to add the selected employees to the Add Employees to Payroll form with the selected pay group. (After saving the payroll, the system adds these employees to the payroll.)

Scheduled Deductions

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Change/Scheduled_Deductions.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Change/Scheduled_Deductions.htm

Creating Scheduled Deductions

You can establish a one-time or temporary deduction for the employee using the Scheduled Deductions form.

Note: Note the following:

  • You can upload scheduled deductions into the form instead of entering it manually, if you have a file in the correct format (see Importing Employee One-Time Deductions).

  • If you enter or select a restricted deduction code (that is, a code not submitted on the Control tab in the Client Details form), a warning displays and you cannot save the record, “Warning - <deduction code> is not a deduction code defined on the <client> Client Detail Control tab.” Click OK to continue.

Note: Service providers can enable the ALLPAYCODESINT custom feature code on the System Parameters form to override the restriction listed above, so the system imports any deduction codes, including the allowed deduction codes that are defined in the Control tab on the Client Details form. (See Using Custom Feature Codes.)

  • Click the Data Import Tool icon ( [Image: screenshot] ) to import employee one-time deductions using only deduction codes defined at the system level that use the Fixed Amount calculation method. (See the Payroll Administration Guide for more information about using the Employee One-Time Deductions Import Template option to perform this import.)

To create a one-time or temporary deduction for the employee:

  1. Enter the Employee by either entering the name, Social Security Number, or ID to display a pop-up list of matching employee records. You can also click the field label or press Ctrl+Enter with your cursor in this field to open the search window.

Note: The Next Pay Date field displays informational date value that helps you to quickly identify the next regularly scheduled payroll batch date during the enrollment process.

  1. For each deduction:

  1. — Enter or select the Deduction Code. If you select a deduction code that does not use a fixed method for calculation, it could override the standard deduction amount. If you enter a code that is not defined for the client, the system displays a warning message to confirm that you want to use that code.

  2. — You can enter a Check Stub Description to override the default; this appears on the employee’s remittance advice.

c. Select the deduction Status to specify when the deduction occurs.

  • One Time: The system takes the deduction once during the specified pay range and then sets it to Inactive.

  • Active: The system takes the deduction each pay period during the date range.

  • Inactive: The system has stopped taking the deduction.

d. Enter the Amount to deduct from the employee’s net earnings (after taxes).
e. Enter the Start Date; the system begins processing the deduction on or after this date.
— —
f. Enter the Stop Date; the system stops processing this deduction on or after this date.
— —
g. Enter the Third Party Payee Code to establish a payment to a designated payee.
— —
  1. Click Save.
