Scheduled Payments

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Change/Scheduled_Payments.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Change/Scheduled_Payments.htm

Establishing Scheduled Payments

You can establish payments for a specific date in the future or repeat them each pay period during a specified time period using the Scheduled Payments form.

Note: Click the Data Import Tool icon (

[Image: screenshot]

) to import employee scheduled payments. (See the Payroll Administration Guide for more information about using the Employee Scheduled Payments Import Template option to perform this import.)

Assigning the Scheduled Payment

You can assign scheduled payment parameters in the Scheduled Payments panel.

Note: Note: By default, any pay code defined as an earning and not a one-time payment moves to detail lines on the pay voucher.

To assign the scheduled payment, do the following:

  1. Go to the Scheduled Payments panel and complete the following fields for each pay code:
Field Description
Employee Enter the Employee by either entering the name, Social Security Number, or ID to display a pop-up list of matching employee records. You can also click the field label or press Ctrl+Enter with your cursor in this field to open the search window.
Next Pay Date Displays informational value for the Next Pay Date that helps you to quickly identify the next regularly scheduled payroll batch date during the enrollment process.
Pay Code Enter the Pay Code for this payment. Pay codes for scheduled payments must use a fixed calculation method. Note: You cannot enter or select client-restricted pay codes (those codes not assigned to the client in the Pay Code field on the Control tab in the Client Details form). However, if the ALLPAYCODESINT custom feature code is enabled, then internal payroll users can enter or select from all pay codes.
Pay Description The Pay Description displays. If you enter a code that is not defined for the client, the system displays a warning message to confirm that you want to use that code.
Starting Pay Date/Ending Pay Date Enter the Starting Pay Date and Ending Pay Date when the payment is in effect.
Deduction Period Enter the Deduction Period to make this payment on certain periods within the date range. For example, if you enter 2, then PrismHR makes the payment in the second pay period of the month.
Status Select the Status to specify when the scheduled payment occurs: - One Time: The payment is made once during the specified pay range and then set to Inactive. - Active: The payment is made each pay period during the date range. - Inactive: No payment will be made.
  • One Time: The payment is made once during the specified pay range and then set to Inactive.
  • Active: The payment is made each pay period during the date range.
  • Inactive: No payment will be made. | Move To T/S | Select Yes from the Move To T/S drop-down to move this expensed reimbursement or fringe pay code to the detail line on the payroll Voucher Earning Detail form once the payroll initializes. Note: You can only use Move To T/S when the Status is set to Active. (This field does not work with a One Time scheduled payment.) | | Amount | Enter the Amount to pay the employee; the amount can be negative, but it cannot be zero. | | Edit Employee Details | Click this field to open the Time Sheet Allocation form, where you can edit the employee’s department, division, location, and position. (See Editing Employee Details for detailed information.) |
  1. Click Save.

Editing Employee Details

You can edit an employee’s details directly from this form by clicking the Edit Employee Details icon. For example, you can assign independent employee positions and divisions (that is, independent from the employee’s home position and division) to the scheduled payments already set up in this form.

[Image: screenshot]

Note: To display the Edit Employee Details icon on this form, you must enable the SCHEDULED-PAYMENTS-CHANGE-DEFAULTS custom feature code. After accessing the Time Sheet Allocation form the first time, the Edit Employee Details field displays as a regular field instead of an icon in the Scheduled Payments panel (simply click the field to open the Time Sheet Allocation form).

To edit an employee’s details, do the following:

  1. Click the Edit Employee Details icon. The Time Sheet Allocation form displays, where you can edit the employee’s Department, Division, Location, Shift, Position, Project, and Phase.

Note: These fields do not display if they are not set up as a Detail Time Sheet Field on the Time Sheet tab in the Client Details form.

  1. After editing these fields, click Accept.

  2. Click Save.

Defining G/L Account Overrides

You can define the G/L account override information for scheduled payments in the Override G/L Accounts panel.

To define the G/L account override, do the following:

  1. Go to the Override G/L Accounts panel and If a client accounting payment override is required, complete the following fields:

Field — Description

Pay Code — For each Pay Code, enter the G/L Account to charge this payment when the pay voucher is created.

Suppress Allocation — Select Yes from Suppress Allocation if this line allocates strictly to the employee’s home data fields instead of the allocation rules.

Processing Tax Adjustments to Tax Register

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Change/Tax_Adjustment_Entry.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Change/Tax_Adjustment_Entry.htm

Processing Tax Adjustments to Tax Register

Each tax register contains a running total of amounts deducted from an employee’s paycheck. You can process an adjustment to a client’s tax register when necessary using the Tax Adjustment form. For example, you can process an adjustment when an employee is incorrectly assigned a withholding tax or you are starting in the middle of a year.

[Image: screenshot]

Use the tax adjustment process with care. When you process an adjustment to a tax register, be aware that you are making changes to the system’s permanent and only record of taxes withheld for the employee.

Important! Do not use the Tax Adjustment feature unless you completely understand the implications of adjusting tax registers.

To set up a tax adjustment:

  1. Click New Adjustment to create the new entry.

  2. Enter the Employee ID for this adjustment entry.

  3. Enter the Adjustment Date. The system uses this date to derive the tax year, quarter, and month to adjust.

  4. Enter the Employer ID that should be affected by this adjustment.

  5. Select Adjust Client Tax Register if you want the system to update the client’s register for client-based taxes.

  6. Select Suppress Billing if you do not want to bill the client for this adjustment.

  7. Enter the School District ID if you are adjusting a school district tax.

Note: You cannot enter more than one line for a school tax in the same state.

  1. If you do client reporting by location and need to adjust that type of register, enter the worksite Location.

  2. Select a Special Options Code to modify the tax adjustment process.

  • Group-Term Life: adjustment to group-term life

  • Sick Pay Adjustment: adjustment to sick pay

  • Uncollect Tax Adjustment: uncollected Medicare or OASDI tax adjustments

  1. If you are making an adjustment that affects Pennsylvania local taxes, enter the Residential Geocode Override that the system should use to determine the resident PSD code. If you do not enter a value, the system will use the employer’s value.

  2. Enter the information for each tax code in the table.

[Image: screenshot]

  1. — Enter the Tax Code that represents the deduction for the tax you need to adjust. You can only enter a code once in the table. The Tax Description displays, as well as the Pre-Adjust Tax Code Register Entry pane.
b. Enter the Exempt Pay, which is any non-taxable pay.
c. Enter any Sheltered Earnings, such as retirement amounts.
— —
d. If you need to adjust it, enter the amount to adjust the Gross Taxable by.
— —
  1. — Enter the Taxable Over Limit amount, if needed. This has more to do with employer taxes than employee taxes, the amount of pay that has gone over a limit; for example, the value over the FUTA or SUTA limit.
f. The system displays the Net Taxable amount. You cannot edit this value.
  1. — Enter the Tax Amount that was over-withheld as a negative number. The negative amount in this field represents the money to be paid to the employee. You cannot adjust for tax that was under-withheld.
  1. The system displays any quarter or year entries for the selected Tax Codes in the Pre-Adjust Tax Code Register Entry panel.

[Image: screenshot]

  1. Click Save.

If the total tax amount is a negative amount and it is an employee-paid tax, the system automatically attempts to refund the amount to the employee. You can choose whether you want the system to print a check immediately or create a scheduled payment using the tax refund code (defined in System Parameters). If the amount should not be paid to the employee, you can delete the entry in Scheduled Payments.

If the employer is SBEA certified, the tax adjustment updates the Federal Entity Tax Register.

Tax Summary

Click Tax Summary to view a summary of the employee’s taxes before the adjustments.

[Image: screenshot]

Adjusting Third Party Sick Pay Records

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Change/Third_Party_Sick_Pay_Adj.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Change/Third_Party_Sick_Pay_Adj.htm

Adjusting Third Party Sick Pay Records

You can adjust an employee’s year-to-date records to reflect sick pay from a third party. Sometimes referred to as disability pay, the Third-Party Sick Pay Adjustment form allows your organization to enter information that is required for tax purposes. The typical scenario is that the third-party already withheld the taxes and will provide a W-2 to the employee, but your organization would need to collect for the employer taxes. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Employer tax amounts are calculated and billed to the client via the Client Bill Pending feature.

WARNING: Your organization must set up the OASDI and FUTA limits to use the third-party sick pay feature. The system will not let you use the functionality unless these limits are defined in System Parameters.

Note: You can directly access the Third Party Sick Pay Adjustment import template in the Data Import Tool by clicking the

[Image: screenshot]

link.

To adjust an employee’s year-to-date records:

  1. Click New Adjustment to create the new entry.

  2. Enter the Employee by either entering the name, Social Security Number, or ID to display a pop-up list of matching employee records. You can also click the field label or press Ctrl+Enter with your cursor in this field to open the search window.

  3. Enter the Adjustment Date. The system uses this date to derive the tax year, quarter, and month to adjust.

  4. Enter the Bill Date to use for any billing transaction. If you leave this field blank, the system uses the Adjustment Date.

  5. Enter the Employer ID that should be affected by this adjustment.

Note: If the Employer is not assigned to the Client or as an Alternate Employer for the Client an error message displays, Invalid Employer ID,” and you cannot save the information in the form.

  1. Enter the amount of Federal Taxable Sick Pay, which is the total amount paid to the employee by a third-party insurer to cover lost wages during an illness.

  2. Enter the amount of Federal Non-Taxable Sick Pay, which is sick pay that was not taxable because it was attributed to employee contributions to insurance premiums.

  3. Enter the Federal Income Tax Withheld, which is the amount of federal income tax withheld by the third-party insurer.

  4. Enter the FICA Taxable Sick Pay, which is the amount of taxable sick pay paid to the employee by a third-party insurer to cover lost wages during an illness.

  5. Enter the FICA Non-Taxable Sick Pay, which is sick pay that was not taxable because it was attributed to employee contributions to insurance premiums.

  6. Enter the amount of Social Security Tax Withheld by the third-party insurer.

  7. Enter the amount of Medicare Tax Withheld by the third-party insurer.

  8. Select Adjust Client Tax Register if you want the system to update the client’s register for client-based taxes.

  9. For each state to which this adjustment applies (if any):

  1. — Enter the two-character postal code for the state that might have miscellaneous state taxes, such as Hawaii employee disability tax.
b. Select the Tax ID for the state tax withheld from the employee by the third-party insurer.
c. Enter the Taxable Pay applicable to that state.
— —
d. Enter the Tax Withheld by the third-party insurer for that state.
— —

[Image: screenshot]

  1. Click Save.

Importing the Data File

If a client is set to use a time sheet import on the Client Details Time Sheet tab, use Time Sheet Import to import the data file.

To import the data file, do the following:

  1. In the Time Sheet Entry form, click Time Sheet Import [Image: screenshot] . The Time Sheet Import form opens.

  2. Select the Payroll Number. The Pay Groups information displays.

  3. If there is more than one time sheet import definition for the client, select the one you want to use from the Import Definition ID drop-down.

  4. Enable the Use Import for Hours Worked and Employee Default Hours for Hours Paid field to populate the employee’s default hours (not standard hours) on the timesheet.

Note: This field only displays if you enable the TS-LOAD.HRS.WORKED (Global) or TS-LOAD.HRS.WORKED-C (Client) custom feature code on the System Parameters form.

  1. Click Start Import. The Upload File window opens.

  2. Click Choose File. Navigate to the location of the file, select it, and then click Open.

  3. Click Submit. When the file upload completes, a confirmation message appears.

  4. Click Close. You return to the Time Sheet Import form.

  5. If there were any errors, they display in the Error Report. For example, if an employee has hours allocated to a charge date that occurs prior to the employee’s hire date, a warning message displays.

  6. Click Review to look at the imported data. If there is more than one page, use the Previous Page and Next Page buttons to navigate the imported time sheet data.

  7. If the data is accurate, click Post Data to Time Sheets. The system processes the data and creates the time sheets.

  8. Click OK in the confirmation message.

  9. If there were any errors, they display in the Error Report, which you can print.

  10. Click Edit Time Sheets. You return to the Time Sheet Entry form, where you can proceed to the next step of the process.

Transfer Tax Basis Entry

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Change/Transfer_Tax_Basis_Entry.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Change/Transfer_Tax_Basis_Entry.htm

Transfer Tax Basis Entry

You can transfer an employee’s tax basis in the case of a successorship. This allows you to “pick up” where the previous employer “left off” in paying employer-based taxes.

Important! Do not use the Transfer Tax Basis feature unless you completely understand the implications of making adjustments to tax registers.

[Image: screenshot]

  1. Click Create new transfer to create the new entry. The fields are enabled for entry.

  2. Enter the Employee ID for this tax basis transfer entry.

  3. Enter the Employer ID for this tax basis transfer entry.

  4. Enter the Tax Year within which this transfer is being made.

  5. Enter the Reason for the transfer.

  6. From the Billing Only drop-down, select the method for updating the PEO Tax Billing Register.

  • Yes: Update only the PEO Tax Billing Register; the system continues to accrue to the cost side with no regard for these entries.

  • No: The successor wages that you entered impact both the cost and the bill; complete all fields and enter the appropriate tax code.

  • Suppress: Suppress the update of the billing register with successor wages.

Note: Note: When filling in the Tax Basis and Tax Amt fields, be sure to fill in the actual tax amount paid thus far. Otherwise, if you leave the amount as zero, the calculation begins at zero.

  1. For each tax code:
a. Enter the Tax Code. The Tax Description displays.

  1. — Enter the Tax Basis, which is the taxable wage base to transfer from another state (SUTA) or from a successor employer. Enter it as either the limit if the employee has met the threshold or the year-to-date amount if they have not quite met the limit. For example, if the employee has earned $10,000 YTD and the limit on that tax code is $7,000, you would enter $7,000 (not $10,000).

  2. — Enter the Tax Amt, which is the amount of employer-paid tax liability or employee-paid withholding to transfer from another state or successor employer. It is the bill rate multiplied by the wage basis you are entering.

  1. Click Save.

When you post the voucher, this acts as a placeholder for the tax. The entry you made here does not display on any tax reports.

If the employer is SBEA certified, the tax adjustment updates the Federal Entity Tax Register.

Vacation Pay Override

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Change/Vacation_Pay_Override.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Change/Vacation_Pay_Override.htm

Overriding Vacation Pay

In addition to an employee’s regular pay, some clients issue a separate vacation payroll voucher on the pay date prior to the employee’s actual vacation. Because a lump sum total of multiple weeks would prompt a disproportionately higher tax rate than if the tax was determined according to weeks worked, PrismHR allows you to override the vacation vouchers.

To override vacation voucher calculations, perform the following steps before you initialize the batch in which this employee will be paid.

[Image: screenshot]

To override vacation voucher calculations, do the following:

  1. Enter the Employee by either entering the name, Social Security Number, or ID to display a pop-up list of matching employee records. You can also click the field label or press Ctrl+Enter with your cursor in this field to open the search window.

  2. Select the Existing Pay Date for the override, or enter a New Pay Date to create a new override.

  3. You can specify up to ten vacation vouchers:

a. Enter the Start Date of the period paid on this vacation voucher.
b. Enter the Ending Date.
— —

Note: Note: Be sure the Ending Date is correct; PrismHR uses this date to update the Benefits Thru Date field on the Employee Details Work tab. The Benefits Thru Date indicates the last date that benefits were calculated for this employee. During payroll processing, the system refers to the Benefits Thru Date to determine whether a benefit deduction is due. For example, when the system processes a check for an employee whose Benefits Thru Date is in the future, it does not calculate benefits.

  1. — Enter the Deduction Periods (1-5) that correspond to the pay periods paid on the vacation voucher. These override the periods on the Batch Control Record.
  1. Click Save.

Voiding a Garnishment Check

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Change/Void-Garnishment-Check.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Change/Void-Garnishment-Check.htm

Voiding a Garnishment Check

Use Void a Garnishment Check to cancel checks issued for accidental garnishments.

Note: Note: This form does not use Client Access Group Security.

To void a garnishment check:

  1. Click the Payroll menu.

  2. From Payroll|Action, select Void a Garnishment Check to display this form.

  3. Complete these fields:

  • Bank Account Number - Account the check was drawn from. Opens a selector that lists available account numbers.

  • Check Number - Check number that was issued. Opens a selector that filters check numbers by the specified bank account.

  • Reason for Void - Reason for voiding the check.

  • Was Check Sent - Options are Sent to Garnishment Authority or Check Destroyed.

If… Then click… Result
The garnishment check was sent and it will be voided. Sent to Garnishment Authority A zero amount will be displayed in the EFT/Check$ column of the Payment History screen.
The garnishment check was torn up. Check Destroyed A negative amount will be displayed in the EFT/Check$ column of the Payment History screen.

Note: Note: When a check number is selected, the system displays the Pay to Name, Check Date, and Check Amount displayed.

  1. Click Void Check to complete the check cancellation.

Using the Payroll Dashboard

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Dashboard/Payroll_Dashboard.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Dashboard/Payroll_Dashboard.htm

Using the Payroll Dashboard

The Payroll Dashboard (found in the Client menu under Client|Dashboard) provides a summary of payroll information. The dashboard refreshes at regular intervals, ensuring that the information is current.

[Image: screenshot]

  • Payroll Statistics displays the totals. Click a link to open a list of pending or overdue items.

  • Hourly Payroll Processing displays the number of payrolls that have been processed and those to be processed for each hour of the work day.

  • Payroll By Status displays each status, and the percentage of payrolls at those statuses.

  • Payrolls By Processor displays the complete and incomplete payrolls for each payroll processor.

  • Payrolls By Clients displays the percentage of billing, gross, and net amounts that each client company contributes to the total.

  • Payrolls By Cost Centers displays the percentage of billing, gross, and net amounts for each cost center.

  • Payrolls By Service Types displays the percentage of billing, gross, and net amounts for each service type.

========================================================================

Payroll Variance Analysis

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Dashboard/Payroll_Variance_Analysis.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Dashboard/Payroll_Variance_Analysis.htm

Payroll Variance Analysis

The Payroll Variance Analysis dashboard displays information from the most recent payroll and provides a comparison with previously finalized payrolls. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

The Payroll Variance Analysis dashboard displays the following information:

  • Current payrolls in Calculated status display as tabs. Select a tab to view a payroll. The payroll’s Description, Pay Period, and Payroll Type display. In addition, the name of the pay rate displays. This value could be weekly, bi-weekly, semi-monthly, or monthly. (It is based on the names in the system, so some payrolls might have unique names created by training sessions.)
  • Select Compare to Payroll to select a payroll in Finalized status to compare to the current payroll.
  • Note: The payroll number you enter or select in the Compare to Payroll field must meet the following criteria:
  • The comparison Payroll Pay Date is within 180 days of the initialized Payroll.
  • The comparison Payroll Type is Regular or Special.
  • The comparison Payroll Number is a valid payroll.
  • The comparison Payroll is finalized.
  • The comparison Payroll includes the same Pay Group.
  • Select one of the following options in the Payroll Variance Warning field to display the Amounts or Percentages threshold between the current payroll and the comparison payroll:
    • Amounts: Displays threshold amounts. (There is no maximum amount for this option.)
  • Percentages: Displays threshold percentages between 0-100.
  • Note: A text box displays next to the Payroll Variance Warning field where you can change the amount or percentage number. (This number defaults to 10.) If you enter a number for Amounts that is greater than 100 and then select Percentages, the number reverts to 10 (default).
  • The Variance and Variance% values display the statistical dispersion of data compared to the mean values.
  • Select a category in the Breakdown field to view a list of individual employees in that category.
  • While viewing a category, select the Voucher link for an employee to view that employee’s Variance Voucher, which compares the two payrolls for that employee. Select Detail to display a file audit for the payroll change.

In addition, you can do the following:

  • Download the dashboard by selecting Download Variance Detail.

  • Display a warning if the variance equals or exceeds a percentage by entering that percentage in the Payroll Variance Percentage Warning field.

Turnover Dashboard

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Dashboard/Turnover_Report.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Dashboard/Turnover_Report.htm

Turnover Dashboard

Use the Turnover Dashboard to view the company’s turnover information.

  • Total Employees = the number of employees who worked between the start and ends dates of the report, specifically those who started before the report’s end date and were not termed before the report’s start date

  • Termed Employees = the employees who have a terminated status with a date that falls between the report’s start and end dates

[Image: Turnover dashboard example]

To display turnover statistics for employees:

  1. Enter the Beginning Date.

  2. Enter the Ending Date.

  3. Select the Category to display.

  4. Click [Image: screenshot] and the information displays.

  • For each Reason, the system shows the number Terminated during the period and the Percent. The percentage is calculated by dividing the number of termed employees by the total number of employees and then multiplying by 100. In the example illustrated above, the voluntary termed employees count was calculated this way:

[Image: Turnover-Report-Equation]

  • The pie chart displays the termed employees by reason. In the above example, there were eight employees termed during the specified period. Each of the three reasons other than voluntary only had one employee, so those slices are 1/8 of the pie. Voluntary displays as the other 5/8 of the pie.

Amount Did Not Import

Examples of scenarios where you might have an amount that does not import are:

  • All data imports except for expense amounts

  • One pay code will not import

  • Some amounts import and others do not, even with the same pay code

You might see an error that reads, “No hours for employee N#####, paycode NNNN on line #.”

Typically this is caused when the file includes $ or , in the amount fields. In the example below, the Bonus amounts will not import because they each include one or both of those characters. The Regular pay will import correctly.

Tab-Delimited File with $ or , in the Amounts

[Image: tab-delimited file example with dollar amounts entered incorrectly, including commas and dollar signs]

Edit the import file to remove any dollar signs or commas, save the file, and re-import it. All of the amounts shown below will import correctly.

Tab-Delimited File with Correctly Formatted Amounts

[Image: correctly entered dollar amounts using only periods]

Client Status Does Not Allow Finalizing a Payroll

Client status does not allow for finalizing a payroll.

The client’s status is currently of a class Pending, Inactive, or Client Cancelling (Pre-Termination). The system requires that the class of the status be Active to finalize the payroll.

After determining that this is the appropriate action to take, a user must set the client status back to one that indicates they are Active to post the payroll.

To resolve this error:

  1. Open Client Status Change (found in the Client menu under Client|Action).

  2. From the New Status drop-down, select a status that indicates the client is Active.

  3. Enter the Effective Date for the change in status.

  4. Click Save.

Comp Code Does Not Have Rate on Template

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Error_Messages/Comp_Code_Does_Not_Have_Rate.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Error_Messages/Comp_Code_Does_Not_Have_Rate.htm

Comp Code Does Not Have Rate on Template

Client ### Employee: ### Voucher ### Error: The Comp Code NN.#### does not have a rate on the bundled sheet NNNN. Processing cannot continue. The processing for this employee will stop.

The bundled billing template assigned to the client uses default rates and does not have a rate for the W/C code specified in the error message. You need to enter a rate for that code, or a default rate.

Note: Note: If the Default Rate is greater than zero, the system uses it for any Workers’ Compensation code not listed in the table. If there is a value in this field and no value in the W/C Code field, there may be billing errors; use the Default Rate with care. If you leave the Default Rate blank, users entering data for clients with this billing template see messages that the listed Workers’ Compensation code does not have a billing amount. The system continues to display this message until you update the bill template for the code or enter a default amount.

To resolve this error:

  1. Open Billing Templates (found in the Back Office menu under System|Change).

  2. Enter the Template ID indicated in the error message.

  3. Go to the Bundled Rate Maintenance panel and do one of the following:

Enter the rate information for the W/C Code from the error message:

  • Enter the W/C Code.

  • Enter the Min Admin Fee amount to use. This overrides any amount entered on the client record, except for special rates. The system discounts the minimum fee by the special discount rate.

  • Enter the WC Def Bill Rate, which is the default billing rate for the W/C Code.

Enter the Default Rate to apply to all W/C codes not defined in the table. This is useful for “one-price-fits-all” clients. Please read the note above before using the Default Rate field.

  1. In the Coverage Details panel, enter the correct Existing Effective Date.

  2. Click Save.

Federal Entity ID Missing

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Error_Messages/Federal_Entity_ID_Missing.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Error_Messages/Federal_Entity_ID_Missing.htm

Federal Entity ID Missing

Federal Entity ID is missing for this client. It is required because this client is assigned to a certified PEO.

Your organization has enabled the SBEA feature set and the employer associated with the client is set as a certified PEO. This is done in Employer Details.

If the client federal entity does not yet exist, you first need to create the record. Use the following procedure to create one for the client; if you have not set up federal entities for most of your clients, see Creating Client Federal Entities. (If the entity exists, go to step 6.)

To resolve this error:

  1. Open the Client Federal Entities form (found in the Back Office menu under Employer|Change.

  2. Enter the numeric Entity ID (recommended: try entering the same number as the client ID).

  3. Enter the nine-digit Federal EIN (employer identification number) assigned to the employer by the IRS in the format ##-#######.

  4. Complete the other fields as desired; see Creating Client Federal Entities for details.

  5. Click Save.

  1. Open Payroll Import Definition (found in the Back Office menu under System|Change).

Mixed Mapping

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Error_Messages/Pay_Code_Mixed_Mapping.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Error_Messages/Pay_Code_Mixed_Mapping.htm

Mixed Mapping

There is a conflict between the mapping methods in the file and import definition.

There are three basic methods for importing:

  • Mapping

  • Matching

  • Matching for more than 10 codes

Mapping

This method works directly with your file and the import definition. You match the column numbers directly to fields.

Mapping Columns to Fields

[Image: Illustration where import columns are mapped to rows in the field definitions grid.]

Matching

This method not only looks at your file and uses the import definition, but it also needs to look at the Client Details to know what to match for pay codes.

For example, if your import file looks like the one shown below:

Matching File Example

[Image: Example of a matching import file]

The Import Field Definitions match the values in columns 4, 5, and 6 to the values from the Client Details Time Sheet tab for Pay Code 1, Pay Code 2, and Pay Code 6.

Matching Import Definition Example

[Image: Example of matching import grid rows to Pay Codes 1, 2, and 6]

Matching for more than 10 Codes

This method is an extension of the basic matching example above. It uses the matching example for what is available on the Client Details Time Sheet tab, and then uses the translation table to import an eleventh code.

For example, if your import file looks like the one below:

Matching File Example for more than 10 codes

[Image: Matching file example for more than 10 codes]

The Import Field Definitions match the values in columns 4, 5, 6, 7, and 8 to the values from the Client Details Time Sheet tab for Pay Code 1, Pay Code 2, Pay Code 6, Pay Code 7, and Pay Code 8. It then assigns matches the value in column 9 to the pay code specified in the Import Translation Table.

Matching Import Definition Example for more than 10 codes

[Image: Matching example for more than ten codes, where the remaining are mapped to a foreign code in the translation table]

Positive Pay

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Front_Matter/About_Positive_Pay.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Front_Matter/About_Positive_Pay.htm

Positive Pay

Positive pay is an automated fraud detection tool offered by the cash management department of most financial institutions. In its simplest form, it is a service that matches the account number, check number, and dollar amount of each check presented for payment against a list of checks previously authorized and issued by the company. All three components of the check must match exactly or the bank will not honor the check.

The main tasks related to positive pay are:

  • Setting up positive pay on each bank account, which is maintained in the backend system for PrismHR.

  • Creating a positive pay file; see Create Positive Pay Files.

  • Recreating positive pay files as needed: see Recreate Positive Pay Files.

  • Producing a positive pay report: see Positive Pay File Report.

Deduction Sequencing

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Front_Matter/Deduction_Sequencing.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Front_Matter/Deduction_Sequencing.htm

Deduction Sequencing

The order in which deductions are calculated during initialization is simply based on the order in which the deductions appear on the employee’s Recurring Deductions. That order is determined by the order in which benefits—such as 401(k) plans, FSA plans, group benefit plans, garnishments, and loans—are entered into the system. Since group benefit plans are automatically calculated by the system on a periodic basis, they are usually the deduction codes that appear at the bottom of the list in Recurring Deductions.

At the beginning of batch initialization, the system adds all scheduled deductions to the employee’s pay voucher regardless of the cash pay available to support the deduction amounts. After all pay and deductions have been added to an employee’s paycheck and the initial tax calculation is complete, the system searches for any vouchers where the sum of the calculated taxes and payroll deductions exceeds the amount of cash pay. In such cases, the system removes or reduces the deductions to the point where the net cash pay calculated on the voucher is equal to or slightly greater than zero.

The system performs the following process until the net pay is equal to or slightly greater than zero:

  1. Removes or reduces deductions that are currently in arrears and were added to the pay voucher.

  2. Removes or reduces employee loan deductions.

  3. Removes or reduces other scheduled deductions, beginning with one-time deductions.

  4. Removes or reduces deductions that are the result of a benefit billing adjustment.

  5. Removes or reduces deductions that contribute to the cost of a group benefit plan, and puts any amount not deducted into arrears.

  6. Removes or reduces any voluntary deductions that are set up to go into arrears, and puts any amount not deducted into arrears.

  7. Removes or reduces any voluntary deductions that are not set up to go into arrears.

  8. Removes or reduces any retirement contribution deductions.

  9. Removes or reduces any FSA contribution deductions.

If the net pay is still not adjusted, it is probably the result of a manual override made to a tax calculation. In such cases, the payroll processor must manually remove the override and recalculate the batch.

Payroll Option Templates Overview

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Front_Matter/Payroll_Option_Templates_Overview.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Front_Matter/Payroll_Option_Templates_Overview.htm

Payroll Option Templates Overview

Payroll option templates (also known as calculation templates) allow your organization to change the processing options for one or more employees within a particular payroll batch.

Note: Note: This is different from the Payroll Options in Payroll Control, which applies the settings to all employees in a batch.

  1. Maintain the templates that your organization uses: see Managing Payroll Option Templates.

  2. Your organization might specify templates at the client level:

  • If your organization has not chosen to always use payroll option templates at the global level, you must assign templates to each client that will use them; see Client Setup for Payroll Option Templates.

  • If your organization has opted to use payroll option templates at the global level, then you need to set a custom feature code; see Global Management of Payroll Option Templates. If a client does not have any templates specified in Client Details, users can select any template for employees in that client’s payroll batches.

  1. Users can apply templates to employees in Payroll Control; see Applying Payroll Option Template in Payroll Control.

  2. Users can also apply templates to employees in Summary Time Sheet Entry; see Applying Payroll Option Template in the Time Sheet.

  3. After the payroll is processed, users can see which template was used by looking at the employee’s voucher; see Payroll Option Template in Employee Voucher.

Tracking Voluntary Deductions To Arrears

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Front_Matter/PR_UG_Chapter_Track_Voluntary_Dedns_To_Arrears.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Front_Matter/PR_UG_Chapter_Track_Voluntary_Dedns_To_Arrears.htm

Tracking Voluntary Deductions To Arrears

You can track arrearage on voluntary deductions using the fields in various forms that support and enable this feature.

During payroll calculation, the system looks to determine if a particular voluntary deduction should go into arrears. It checks the records in this order:

  1. Employee Details

  2. Client Details

  3. Deduction Codes

You can set up the arrears-tracking features at the levels required by your organization:

  • One or more employees

  • One or more clients

  • The entire system

  • A combination of these options for any deduction codes

Processing Third Party Checks

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Front_Matter/PR_UG_Cutback_Check_Processing.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Front_Matter/PR_UG_Cutback_Check_Processing.htm

Processing Third Party Checks

Third party check processing connects employee voluntary deductions and garnishments with designated payees. PrismHR deducts the designated pay amounts from the employee and creates a check made payable to the designated payee through third party check batch processing or when your organization processes a payroll.

Note: Note: In addition to setting up the payees and deduction codes for each client, Third Party Check Printing Mode must be set in System Parameters.

Important! The legacy system did not require a system parameter selection because the automatic processing of garnishment checks with payroll did not function as intended. With the improvement to the process in PrismHR, it is now necessary to define whether processing will be done by Batch Mode or Real Time. This setting must be enabled in system parameters before processing payrolls with third party deductions/garnishments.

To process third party checks, see the following:

  • Maintaining Third Party Payees Vendor Information

  • Defining Voluntary Third Party Deductions

  • Setting Up Third Party Check Printing Mode

  • Generating Third Party Check Information

Deduction Methods

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Reference/Deduction_Methods.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Reference/Deduction_Methods.htm

Deduction Methods

In some forms, deduction methods display as abbreviations.

  • F - Fixed

  • R - (Rate) x (Hours Worked)

  • L - Tax Levy Reverse Calculation

  • G - Garnishment

  • K - Retirement Plan

  • PG - Percent of Gross Earnings: includes all payments, which are expense reimbursements, fringe benefits, and earnings

  • PE - Percent of Gross Earnings: includes pay codes with Earning disburse type

  • PS - Percent of Straight Time: includes pay codes with Straight rate class

  • U - Union

The calculation method determines how the system calculates the deduction amount, or where it obtains the calculation method.

Settings in Employee Details

Each employee record contains personal information for the employee.

Users with the appropriate permissions can access Employee Details through the HR menu under HR|Change. Refer to the online help or the Human Resources User Guide to learn about using this form.

Name tab: These fields are read-only; use other features to make changes.

  • Status Date

  • Type Date

  • Position

  • Employer

  • Employer Start Date

  • Last Hire Date

  • Original Hire Date

Address tab: This tab contains the employee’s personal address information.

  • Deliver Check Home

Work tab: Some fields can be adjusted on this tab, and others require you to use other features to change the values.

  • Benefits Thru Date

  • Term Reason

Pay tab: This tab contains the employee’s compensation data, including Compensation and Allocations.

Tax tab: Use this tab to maintain the employee’s present tax filing status. If you need the tax filing status at the time a voucher was produced, you can find the information on the payroll voucher. This tab also includes the Employment Verification data.

Deposit tab: All or part of an employee’s net payment can be deposited directly, and even include a balance amount on the paycheck.

Other tab: Various additional employee settings.

Field Description
Check Type Select one of the following options: - Garnishment: Retrieves employee garnishment information. - Third Party: Retrieves employee third party check information.

The Negative Pay Report, available from the Payroll|Report menu, allows you to generate a report that lists all employees whose gross pay is less than zero or have negative hours. (This might occur as an adjustment mechanism for the client.)

The report only displays those employees who have negative hours or a negative gross pay entry, sorted by the net ascending hours. For example:

[Image: Negative Pay Report example]

Note: Note the following about this report:

  • You can run this report after doing the timesheet entry.

  • The shaded lines display the sub-total net hours for each employee, but these sub-totals cannot be exported to Excel output.

  • Employees with net positive hours might display in this report.

The report columns are:

Column — Description

Emp ID — The ID associated with the employee.

Name — The employee name associated with the negative gross pay.

Pay Code — The pay code associated with the employee.

Location — The location associated with the employee.

Project — The project associated with the employee.

Date — The pay date associated with the employee.

Pay Amt — The negative pay amount associated with the employee. (Note: This could also be a positive pay amount, if an employee has both negative and positive pay entries.)

Hours — The negative hours associated with the employee. (Note: This could also be positive hours, if an employee has both negative and positive pay entries.)

Batch Register Report

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Reports/Batch_Register_Report.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Reports/Batch_Register_Report.htm

Batch Register Report

This report displays detailed information per employee for a payroll.

[Image: Batch Register report parameters]

To run the Batch Register report:

  1. Enter the Payroll Number.

  2. Click Run.

[Image: Batch Register report output]

The report columns are:

  • Employee Name: Employee name displays as last name first.

  • Address: The employee’s residential address.

  • Title: The employee’s position title.

  • Status: The employee’s employment status (for example, Active or On Leave).

  • Type: The employee’s employment type (for example, Full-Time or Part-Time).

  • EEO: The employee’s position EEO class.

  • Employee ID: Employee ID

  • Dept: The employee’s assigned department.

  • W/C: The employee’s assigned workers compensation class code.

  • FLSA: The employee’s FLSA type (for example, Standard, Highly Compensated or Exempt).

  • PayGrd: The employee’s pay grade based on their position title.

  • Salary: The employee’s compensation amount based on the pay group.

  • Hire: The employee’s last hire date.

  • Term: The reason for employee’s termination.

  • Review: Date of employee’s last review.

  • Employee Number: Employee Number

  • Gender: Employee Gender

  • DOB: The employee’s date of birth.

  • Tax Filing Info:

  • Type: Type of tax filing (for example, Federal, AR, AZ and so on).

  • Status: The status of tax filing.

  • Add’L: Additional codes associated with that tax type.

  • Direct Deposit:

  • Account No: Employee Bank Account Number

  • Tran/ABA: Employee Bank Transaction Number

  • CHK/SAV: The employee’s (C) checking or (S) saving account where the pay amount is deposited.

  • $/%: The amount or percentage that is deposited. Balance displays when it is the last deposit or only deposit.

  • Earnings:

  • Type: Pay Code and Description

  • Current: The pay amount for this pay period.

  • MTD: Month to date pay

  • QTD: Quarter to date pay

  • YTD: Year to date pay

  • Deductions:

  • Type: Deduction Description

  • Current: The deduction amount for this type during this pay period.

  • MTD: Month to date deduction

  • QTD: Quarter to date deduction

  • YTD: Year to date deduction

  • Disbursements:

  • Voucher No: Voucher Number

  • Check No: Check Number

  • Check Amount: The amount on this check.

  • Direct Deposit Amount: The amount that is direct deposited for this check / voucher.

  • Paid Time Off:

  • Description: The paid time off description.

  • CarryFWD: The amount of paid time off carried forward.

  • Accrued: The amount of paid time off accrued in this pay period.

  • Used: The amount of paid time off used in this pay period.

  • Balance: The amount of paid time off available after this paid period.

  • Grand Total: The total for all employees.

  • Total Employee Count: The number of the employees included in the report.

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Reports/Benefit_Adjustment_Report.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Reports/Benefit_Adjustment_Report.htm

Benefit Adjustment Report

This report will display employees with adjustments to their benefit and details of the adjustment.

  1. Enter the Selection Parameters to determine what displays on the report. If left blank, all employees display:

  • Enter the Employee by either entering the name, Social Security Number, or ID to display a pop-up list of matching employee records. You can also click the field label or press Ctrl+Enter with your cursor in this field to open the search window. This will display results for only that employee, OR

  • Enter the Start Date and the End Date to run this report for a date range.

Under the Other Parameters section, click USE ‘XLS’ Format if you want to

  1. Click Run to generate the Benefit Adjustments Report for the selected employee or for the selected date range.

  2. Click Close to close this form at any time.

The report columns are:

  • Employee ID: Employee ID

  • Employee Name: Employee name displays as last name first.

  • Benefit Plan: The plan ID.

  • Period: The year and month.

  • Start Date: The benefit start date.

  • Bill Amount: The amount billed to the client from the benefit company.

  • Employee Contribution: The amount paid by the employee.

  • Insurance Cost: The amount of the premium that has already been accrued.

  • Net Inv Effect: The Bill Amount - employee contribution

  • Cycles: The number of cycles to bill.

  • Cycles billed: The number of cycles already billed.

  • B/R Adjustment: The benefit reconciliation adjustment to apply to the benefits reconciliation process of this adjustment.

  • Retro Enroll: Whether the adjustment applies to a retroactive enrollment. Pre-tax contributions cannot fund any part of the premium for retroactive enrollments. Y for Yes and N for No.

  • Ref. Number: The plan reference number.

  • Comment: Descriptive comments about this adjustment, typically something that would help someone understand the benefit adjustment.

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Reports/Certified_Payroll_Report.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Reports/Certified_Payroll_Report.htm

Certified Payroll Report

Use the Certified Payroll Report form to run the on-demand version of the Certified Payroll Report. This report displays information about wages and payroll for all employees.

Note: Note: This report currently supports only the federal government version; additional state versions will be added at a later date.

[Image: Certified payroll report parameters]

Note: If an employee has a fringe rate, a second number displays in the RATE OF PAY column in the report output, separated from the first number using a slash (/). For example, 50.00/4.21.

To run this report:

  1. Select or enter the Week Ending Date for the report.

  2. Select Process Initialized Vouchers Instead of Posted to set the calculation to allocate by project total. When unchecked, the allocation is based on gross pay.

  3. Select Allocate Deductions/Taxes by Project to calculate deductions and taxes. Checking the box sets the calculation to allocate by project total. When unchecked, the allocation is based on gross pay.

  4. Select Report Type.

a. Select PDF to generate the report in a PDF format.
b. Select CSV to generate this report in an excel format.
— —

  1. Enter Project Codes for the payrolls that you want to include in the report. The Payroll Number displays.

  2. Click Run.

Setting Client Allocation Formats

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Reports/Client-Allocation-Formats.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Reports/Client-Allocation-Formats.htm

Setting Client Allocation Formats

You can use the Client Allocation Formats form to set the presentation of each column in the Client Allocation Report (see Client Allocation Report). Formatting options include:

  • Selects the applicable client bill format if tied to a client bill or another format describing the allocation columns.

  • Specifies whether to include an employee totals column.

  • Adds, inserts, and deletes columns and shows them as tabs in the header area.

  • Adds text for up to two header lines for each column.

  • Creates and deletes allocation codes and descriptions.

Note: Note: If you try to delete an existing client allocation report format, a warning displays and prompts for confirmation. If your user role has Inquiry access to the form, all options except for Summary Report and Cancel are disabled. However, you can still select a format code and click a header to show the various allocations associated with it.

Formatting a Report

To access this form and format a report:

  1. Click Back Office [Image: screenshot] .

  2. From System|Change, click Client Allocation Formats.

  3. Set a Format Code in either of the following ways:

  • Enter a value in the text box.

  • Click the Format Code link to open the Select Allocation Format selector. Then type a code to search or select an existing code from the list.

  1. Enable Include Employee Total Column to add a column titled Employee Total as the last column in the report. The value is the total of all appropriate columns for each employee.

  2. From the Report Columns panel, click + Add Column. Column Header fields and an Allocation Code grid appear. Generally, up to 10 columns can fit in a page in Landscape orientation. Additional columns appear in the exported report but may not be visible in a print-out. When a column is first added, its tab is associated with a number, such as Column 1, Column 2, and so forth. You are directed to the new column once it’s created. [Image: Example report column setup]

  3. Enter a column name in Column Header Line 1 and use Column Header Line 2 if needed.

  4. Click + to add an allocation code to this column. You can enter a new code and description, or select an existing code by clicking the Allocation Code link and searching or selecting a code from the Select Allocation Code selector. You can only select one code at a time.

Note: You cannot enter a duplicate Allocation Code in a client allocation format in any of the columns. (An error message displays if you enter a duplicate code.)

The following allocation codes are available:

Allocation Code Description
401K Allocates 401K match amount.
401KMatch Sums the 401k Match amounts held in the following fields of the Employee Payroll Voucher: - Field 192 Matching Contribution - Field 195 PEO Matching Contribution - Field 255 Safe Harbor Type One Match - Field 256 Safe Harbor Type Two Match This amount is allocated based on the sort information entered for the report. Note: The amounts summed for this code differ from the amounts shown for the existing Allocation code 401K.

  • Field 195 PEO Matching Contribution
  • Field 255 Safe Harbor Type One Match
  • Field 256 Safe Harbor Type Two Match | ACCR-insurance class code | Entering ACCR- followed by a valid insurance class code collects all accrued amounts for any Benefit Plan assigned that insurance class code. For example, medical and dental accrued amounts could be summed in one column of the report, and long and short term disability accrued amounts could be summed in another column. You can enter the following insurance codes: - MED: Medical - DEN: Dental - VIS: Vision - LIFE: Life - LTD: Long Term Disability - STD: Short Term Disability - EPLI: Bond/EPLI - OTHBEN: Other |

Multiple lines can be entered for the column using any pay codes needed to sum a particular type of hours in this column of the report. For example, all regular type hours worked could be summed in one column of the report, and all overtime type hours in another column. Note: For the hours worked to be summed, the pay code CANNOT be set up for Units of Service. | | HRSWKD- | Entering HRSWKD- followed by an asterisk () collects all hours worked against any cash/hours pay codes NOT entered under a separate pay code as described above. (This allows a column in the report for all other pay.) | | HRSWKD-TOTAL | Entering HRSWKD-TOTAL creates a column in the report with the sum of all the columns using HRSWKD-, as described above. | | JRBCODE | Displays the Job Rate Billing pay codes that have been allocated. | | JRBHRS | Displays the Job Rate Billing hours associated with each of the pay codes. | | JRBAMT | Displays the Job Rate Billing amounts associated with each of the pay codes. | | JRBRATE | Displays the Job Rate Billing pay rate for each of the associated pay codes. | | LIFE | Allocates Life. | | LTD | Allocates Long Term Disability. | | MED | Allocates Medical. | | MULT-X | Multiplies the specified column (MULT-X) against the other columns. For example, if MULT-2 and MULT-3 are placed in column 6, then column 6 contains the product of columns 2 and 3. | | MULT/100-X | Divides the specified column by 100 (MULT/100-X), then multiplies that value against other columns. For example, if MULT/100-6 and MULT/100- 7 are placed in column 8, then the values in column 6 and column 7 are each divided by 100, and the resulting values are multiplied together. | | NETPAY | Net Pay Amount from voucher. Net Pay amount is posted against the first level of allocation on voucher. Any other allocation levels have zero (0) for Net Pay. | | NETPAYAL | Net Pay Amount from voucher. Net Pay is allocated for all levels of allocation using standard allocation logic. | | OASDI | Allocates Federal Insurance Contributions Act/Old Age, Survivors and Disability Insurance (FICA/OASDI). | | OTHBEN | Allocates other benefit. | | OTHTAX | Allocates all other taxes. | | OTHTAX2 | NOT USED | | OTHTAX3 | NOT USED | | PAYAMT- | Entering PAYAMT- followed by an asterisk () collects all amounts paid against any cash pay codes NOT entered under a separate pay code as described above. This allows a column in the report for all other pay. | | PAYAMT-pay code | Entering PAYAMT- followed by a valid cash pay code collects all amounts paid against that pay code in this column of the report at run time. Multiple lines can be entered for the column using any pay codes needed to sum a particular type of pay in this column of the report. For example, all regular type pay could be summed in one column of the report, and all bonus type pay in another column. | | PAYAMT-TOTAL | Entering PAYAMT-TOTAL creates a column in the report with the sum of all the columns using PAYAMT-, as described above, for amounts paid. | | PAYDATE | Allocates pay date (forces to detail). | | REBATE | Allocates deduction rebate billing. | | SALESTAX | Allocates sales tax amount. | | STD | Allocates Short Term Disability. | | SUTA | Allocates State Unemployment Tax Act (SUTA). | | SUBTOTAL- | Entering SUBTOTAL creates a sub-total column within the report. Enter the code with another column number from the template after SUBTOTAL-. Multiple lines can be entered for the column, and all columns entered are sub-totaled with in the column using this code. For example, if SUBTOTAL-5 and SUBTOTAL-7 are entered as Allocation Codes within column 8, column 8 within the report displays the sum of columns 5 and 7. | | TERMDATE | Allocates employee termination date. | | TEXT- | The text entered after this code displays in the column of the report. This column of text is the same for all records and can ONLY be displayed in download versions (not printed) of the report. | | TIPCR | Collects and allocates amounts for Pay Codes that have a Pay Class of RT (Reported Tips) and a Cash/Non-Cash of N (Non-Cash). | | TIPCRINCL | Collects and allocates amounts for Pay Codes that have a Pay Class of RT (Reported Tips) and a Cash/Non-Cash of N (Non-Cash) included in the employee total. | | VIS | Allocates vision. | | W/C | Allocates Workers’ Compensation. | | WCCOST | Allocates Workers’ Compensation cost. | | WCCP | Allocates Workers’ Compensation client premium. | | WCCREDITBACK | Allocates Workers’ Compensation credit back for tips. | | WCDISC | Allocates Workers’ Compensation discount. | | WCTRIA | Allocates Workers’ Compensation Terrorism Risk Insurance Act (TRIA). | Note: You can only use these allocation codes with the mvQuery version of the Client Allocation Report*.

  1. Click Insert Column Before to create a new tab to the left of the currently selected tab or click Delete Column to remove the currently selected column and move remaining columns one column to the left.

  2. Click Summary Report if you want to generate a summary report in PDF format. See Viewing the Job Control Status Report

  3. When the process is complete, click Close to generate a summary report in PDF format.

  4. Click Save to commit the changes.

The following example shows part of a summary report.

[Image: Allocation Format report output]

Note: Note: See Setting Client Allocation Report Parametersfor more information.

Copying an Existing Format Code

You can duplicate an existing format code and its formatting using the Copy feature.

Note: The Copy button is disabled until you enter or select a Format Code.

To copy an existing format code:

  1. Enter or select a Format Code.

  2. Click Copy. The Copy Client Allocation Format form displays.

  3. Enter a new format code in the Enter a code for the new format field.

Note: If you enter an existing format code an error message displays, “Format code already exists. Please choose a different code.”

  1. Click Save. The Client Allocation Formats form re-displays. The new format code displays with the copied formatting.

  2. If appropriate, update the new format code’s information, then click Save.

Client Allocation Report

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Reports/Client_Allocation_Report.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Reports/Client_Allocation_Report.htm

Client Allocation Report

This report provides a listing of client allocations based on the allocation format selected.

Parameters and defaults:

  • If there is a company level Client Allocation Parameters record saved, this will determine the default values in the form for this report.

  • If there is not a company level Client Allocation Parameters record saved, the default values will be global level parameters if a Global level record has been saved in Client Allocation Report Parameters.

  • If there is no company or global level Client Allocation Parameters record, the system defaults are as shown.

To access this form, clickReports menu. Under Payroll|Report, click Client Allocation Report.

Note: You can also access the Client Allocation Report for a selected payroll in the Approval Payroll Reports form. To do this, select Approval Payroll Reports in the View Report/Analytic field on the Payroll Approval form, then select Client Allocation Report in the Report Title column.

To run the Client Allocation Report:

  1. Enter Selection Parameters to determine what displays on the report (required).
  • Enter the Payroll Number to run this report for a specific payroll or select Enter a Pay Date Range and enter a Start Date and End Date to run the report for a date range.
  1. Enter Report Parameters to determine how you want the report to display.

  • Select the Allocation Format from the drop-down (required). (Allocation formats are managed in the Client Allocation Formats form.) The Allocation Format controls what data will be in each column of the report. When a format is selected, the number of columns defined display.

  • Select the Report Type:

  • Detail Report: This option displays the amounts allocated for each employee and miscellaneous charges at each allocation level, sub-totals for each allocation level, and the report total.

  • Summary Report: This option displays sub-totals for each allocation level and the report total.

  • Select Suppress EE Info in Report to suppress the line in the Detail Report displaying additional employee information, allowing more employees to fit per page in the report.

  • Select Suppress Employee ID to suppress the Employee ID column in the Client Allocation Report.

  • Select Suppress Subtotals to suppress the subtotals from the Detail Report.

Note: Using these two options together (along with the allocation and sort parameter Field Type Employee), allows the report to display employee amounts only.

  1. From the Field Type Column Display drop-down, select one of the following options:- Both Code and Description: This option includes a column in the report for the Field Type Code and the Field Type Description. This is the default.

  • Code Only: This option adds a column in the report for the Field Type Code.

  • Description Only: This option adds a column in the report for the Field Type Description.

  • Do Not Display: This option suppresses both the Field Type Code and Field Type Description in the report. If this option is not saved on the Client Allocation Report Parameters form, the default is Do Not Display.

  1. From the Field Type Column Display Order drop-down, select one of the following options:

  • Before EE Info: This option adds the Field Type columns to the report, before the columns with employee information.

  • After EE Info: This option displays the Field Type columns to the report, after the columns with employee information. If this option is not saved on the Client Allocation Report Parameters form, the default is After EE Info.

  1. Select Other Parameters as appropriate.

  • Select Sort by Field Type Description to sort by the Field Type description instead of the Field Type Code.

  • Select Suppress Page Break on Primary Sort (Detail Report) to suppress additional page breaks in the primary allocation in the Detail Report.

  • Select Include Page Break on Primary Sort (Summary Report) to add a page break to the primary allocation in the Summary Report.

  • Select Print Detail Line if Zero to include all allocated employees and miscellaneous charges, even when the amounts set up for the Allocation Format is zero (or null) for the employee or miscellaneous charge.

  • Select Suppress Miscellaneous Billing to suppress miscellaneous charges from the report.

  1. Enter Header Options. These options determine what information that appears in the report header when running the report for a Payroll Number. If the report is run for a date range, only the date range appears in the header.

  • Enter the Header Code.

  • Payroll Number: Displays the Payroll Number in the report header.

  • Invoice Number: Displays the Invoice Number in the report header.

  • Both: Displays both the Payroll Number and Invoice Number in the report header.

  • Select Include Pay Group in Header to include all pay groups included in the payroll, along with the period start and end dates.

  1. Enter Output File (XLS) options to determine the content exported to Excel via XLS:

  • Suppress Company Name suppresses this column when exporting as an Excel report.

  • Suppress Report Title suppresses this column when exporting as an Excel report.

  • Suppress Select Criteria suppresses this column when exporting as an Excel report.

  1. Enter the Allocation and Sort Parameters in the table, in display order. The criteria entered in this table control how the amounts included in the report are allocated.

  • Select the Field Type. This field controls the sortand how the amounts will be allocated for each employee and miscellaneous charge. If an employee or miscellaneous charge has time split across multiple items entered in the Field Type (for example, multiple departments), the amounts will be allocated across all departments. At least one field type is required. There is no limit to the number of fields you can enter.

  • You can enter custom Field Labels to go with the Field Type. This option allows the label for the Field Type entered to be customized, if desired. For example, if allocating the Field Type DEPARTMENT the label in the report will display DEPARTMENT unless the Field Labels is entered as Dept, then the report will display Dept.

  • Select either Sort By or Detail Only from the Sort/Detail drop-down. The first Field Type must be a Sort By field. Both Sort By and Detail Only Field Types can be used for allocations within the report, but Detail Only will not be sorted or subtotaled.

  • Indicate whether to include a Sub Total for the field.

  • If you selected Sort By, the options are Yes or No.

  • If you selected Detail Only, the only option is No.

  • The first Field Type in the table must be set to Yes.

  • Field types with Sub Total set to Yes will have a subtotal within the report.

  1. Click Run.

Note: Note: If you want convert the report to a printable PDF, the report must not include more than 14 columns of data; If you selected the Suppress EE Info in Reports parameter, this maximum is 10. Reports that include more columns of data can be converted to Excel.

Client Bill Rate Report

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Reports/Client_Bill_Rate_Report.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Reports/Client_Bill_Rate_Report.htm

Client Bill Rate Report

Use this form to generate a report to display a listing of client bill rates for a selected payroll number or an invoice number for the client.

Note: Note:

  • Worksite Managers, Worksite Trusted Advisors, and Service Providers can access the form.

  • Client Access Group Security and Data Entity security is enabled on this form.

To access the form, click Reports. Under Payroll|Report, click Client Bill Rate Report.

To generate the Client Bill Rate Report:

  1. Complete one of the following:

Field Name — Description

Payroll Number — Enter the payroll number for which you want to run this report or click the Payroll Number link and select it from the Select Payroll Batches dialog box, OR

Invoice — Enter the invoice number for which you want to run this report or click the Invoice link and select it from the Select Client Invoices dialog box.

  1. Click Run to generate the report. The report shows up on screen.

  2. Click Clear to clear the form at any time.

  3. Click Close to close this form.

This report shows the following columns:

  • Dept Code: The employee’s department code.

  • W/C Class: The workers’ compensation ID.

  • Employee Name: Employee name displays as last name first.

  • Wages: The employee’s wages for that payroll.

  • Bill Rate: The rate in which the bill is paid.

  • Bill Charge: The amount charged for each bill rate.

  • Gross Bill: The total of wages and bill charges.

  • Benefits: The amount of benefits paid.

  • Credits: The amount of credits applied.

  • Misc: Miscellaneous amounts applied.

  • Total Bill: The total of all columns.

Client Check Register Report

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Reports/Client_Check_Register_Report.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Reports/Client_Check_Register_Report.htm

Client Check Register Report

This report provides check information from the Payroll Check Register. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

To run the Client Check Register report:

  1. Enter a Starting Pay Date and an Ending Pay Date to run this report for a date range.

  2. Select the Check Type to display.

  3. Select the Check Status to display.

Note: If you select Reconciled, the Include Stale-dated Checks field displays. Enabling this field includes stale-dated checks when you run a reconciled check report.

  1. Select Sort By to determine how the report is sorted.

  2. Click Run. The report output displays. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

The report columns are:

  • Check Number: The number of the check

  • Type: The type of check (for example, Payroll, Garnishment, or Third Party)

  • Check Date: The date the check was issued

  • Status: The check status (for example, Escheated, Open, Reconciled, Stale-dated, or Voided)

  • Paid To: The employee’s name to whom the check is written

  • Amount Paid: The amount on the check

Deduction Code Detail Report

This report displays employee’s deduction information.

To run the Deduction Code Detail report:

  1. Enter the Selection Parameters to determine what displays on the report. If left blank, all employees display:

  • Enter the Pay Date On Or After and the Pay Date On Or Before to run this report for a date range.

  • Enter the report filters to display on the report:

  • Enter the field type. The field label displays. For example, if you enter a Location, the Location Name displays. The report displays records for that Location.

  1. Filter any Deduction Codes or Deduction types in the Detail Filters panel.

  2. Click Run.

The report columns are:

  • Ded’n Code: The deduction code used to identify the deductions from employee’s pay.

  • Deduction Description: The deduction description used to identify the deductions from employee’s pay.

  • Employee ID: Employee ID

  • Employee Name: Employee name displays as last name first.

  • Pay Date: The date the employee was paid.

  • Check #: The number on the check for that pay period.

  • Voucher #: The number of the voucher for that pay period.

  • Amount: The amount of the deduction.

Sort on Sort Parameters Description — By Default this is unchecked. Check this option to use the sort parameters descriptions instead of the codes for the options entered in Primary Sort, Secondary Sort and Tertiary Sort.

Suppress Pay Group in Header — By Default this is unchecked. Check this option to exclude the Pay Group, Pay Period Start, and End Dates in the report header.

Suppress Zero Deductions — By Default this is unchecked. Check this option to exclude zero deductions. The default is to show all deductions, even zero balance ones.

Benefits Only — By Default this is unchecked. Check this option to show only deductions that are associated with a Benefit Plan.

Include Return and Retain Amounts — By Default this is unchecked. Check this option to give Service Providers the ability to include the Retained Amount and Returned Amount columns on the report.

Only Show deductions that are Returned to the Client — By Default this is unchecked. Check this option to give Service Providers the ability to show deductions that are returned to the client.

e. Under the Report Filters section:

Field Name — Description

Division — If you want to run this report for specific divisions, enter the divisions here or click the Division link and select them from the window. The corresponding Division Names will populate automatically.

Department — If you want to run this report for specific departments, enter the departments here or click the Department link and select them from the window. The corresponding Department Names will populate automatically.

Location — If you want to run this report for specific locations, enter the locations here or click the Location link and select them from the window. The corresponding Location Names will populate automatically.

Project — If you want to run this report for specific projects, enter the projects here or click the Project link and select them from the window. The corresponding Project Description will populate automatically.

Shift — If you want to run this report for specific shifts, enter the shifts here or click the Shift link and select them from the Select Employee window. The corresponding Shift Description will populate automatically.

Employee ID — If you want to run this report for specific employees, enter their employee IDs here or click the Employee ID link and select them from the Select Employee window. The corresponding Employee Names will populate automatically. Leave this field blank to select all employees associated with the users selected client.

Field Name Description
Employer ID Enter the employer ID for whom you want to run this report or click the Employer ID link and select it from the Select Employer dialog box.
Starting Date Enter the starting date of the reporting period. This date must be the first date of the month.
Ending Date Enter the ending date of the reporting period. This date must be the last date of the month.
Pay Period This field will display if you have selected an employer above. Select the pay period from the following options: - Weekly (PayDay 1-7) 1=Monday - 7=Sunday - Biweekly (PayDay 1-7) - Semi-monthly (PayDay {1-28}, {1,28}{EOM} - Monthly (PayDay {1-28}{EOM}
  • Weekly (PayDay 1-7) 1=Monday - 7=Sunday
  • Biweekly (PayDay 1-7)
  • Semi-monthly (PayDay {1-28}, {1,28}{EOM}

Enter the commission pay codes to include in the Commissions column or click the Commission Pay Code link and select them from the Select Pay Code dialog box. The Pay Code Description will populate automatically for the selected pay codes. | | Earning Pay Code | This field is optional. Enter the earning pay codes to exclude from the Payroll column or click the Earning Pay Code and select them from the Select Pay Code dialog box. The Pay Code Description will populate automatically for the selected pay codes. | | State | This field is optional. If you want to restrict this report for certain states, enter them here. Leave this field blank for this report to show all applicable states. |
  1. Click Run and the Department of Labor Employment Statistics Report will display on screen.

Eligible Time Off Hours Report

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Reports/Eligible_PTO_Hours_Report.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Reports/Eligible_PTO_Hours_Report.htm

Eligible Time Off Hours Report

This report provides a listing of employees’ hours worked and employment dates to determine time off eligibility.

To run the Eligible Time Off Hours Report:

  1. Enter the Selection Parameters to determine what displays on the report. If left blank, all employees display:

  • Enable Less Than 52 Weeks to display employees that have worked less than 52 weeks.

  • Enable Hide employees with no hours to suppress the display of employees with no hours worked or no time off hours used.

  • Enter the report filters to display on the report:

  • Enter the field type. The field label displays. For example, if you enter a Location, the Location Name displays. The report displays records for that Location.

  • Select Primary Sort and Secondary Sort to sort by.

  1. Click Run. The report displays in XLS format. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

The report columns are:

  • Employee: Employee ID.

  • Employee Name: Employee name displays as last name first.

  • Last Anniversary: The employee’s last anniversary date.

  • Status: The employee’s status. (For example, FT - Full-Time or PT - Part Time.)

  • P/E Date: The period end date.

  • Hours: The hours the employee worked.

  • Weeks: The number of weeks the employee worked.

  • Calc Hours: The weekly average of the hours the employee worked.

  • Eligible Hours: The amount of hours available for paid time off.

  • Hours Used: The hours used by the employee for paid time off.

  • Balance: Subtracts the hours used from the eligibility hours.

  • Hire Dare: The employee’s last hire date.

  • 5+: Indicates if the employee was hired more than five years ago.
