Employee Check Register Report

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Reports/Employee%20Check%20Register%20Report.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Reports/Employee Check Register Report.htm

Employee Check Register Report

Use this form to generate the Employee Check Register report which shows basic information about the employees’ pay check including gross pay, deductions, net pay, check number, and department for a payroll or a pay date range for a client.

To access the form, click Reports. Under Payroll|Report, click Employee Check Register Report.

Note: Note:

  • Worksite Managers, Worksite Trusted Advisors, and Service Providers can access the form.

  • Client Access Group Security and Data Entity security is enabled on this form.

To generate the Employee Check Register Report:

  1. Complete the Report Period using one of the following:

Field Name — Description

Payroll Number — Enter the payroll number of click the Payroll Number link and select one from the Select Payroll Batches dialog box for which you want to run this report OR

Pay Date Range — Start Date - Enter the starting pay date for which you want to run this report. End Date - Enter the ending pay date for which you want to run this report.

  1. Click Run to generate the report. The report shows up on screen. Click XLS to download the report.

This report shows the following columns:

  • Employee ID - The employee ID.

  • Employee Name - The name of the employee.

  • Home Department - The Home Department code.

  • Gross Pay - The gross pay earned by the employee on this check number.

  • Deductions - The deductions withheld for the employee on this check number.

  • Net Pay - The net pay received by the employee on this check number.

  • Check Number - The check number by which this payment was made.

  • Federal Income Tax - Federal Income Tax amount withheld on this check number.

  • EE FICA Medicare - Employee paid FICA Medicare Tax amount withheld on this check number.

  • EE FICA Social Security - Employee paid FICA Social Security Tax amount withheld on this check number.

  • ER FICA Owed - Employer contribution to FICA Tax amount withheld on this check number.

Employee Time Off Summary Report

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Reports/Employee-PTO-Summary.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Reports/Employee-PTO-Summary.htm

Employee Time Off Summary Report

The Employee Time Off Summary Report summarizes various types of time off for an employee.

To run this report:

  1. Click the Reports menu.

  2. From Payroll|Report, select Employee Time Off Summary to open the form.

  3. Select a Time Off Plan (such as Floating Holiday) to filter the report results, or leave blank to run the report for all Time Off plans.

  4. Click Run to run the report.

  5. Click Report to display the report output. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

The report columns are:

  • Employee Name: The name of the employee for which time off is being reported.

  • Employee ID: ID of the employee for which time off is being reported.

  • Accrued Thru: Date through which the time off plan is accrued.

  • Year End: Year end date for the current plan year.

  • Plan Name: The Time Off plan being reported, such as Sick Time.

  • Accrual Rate: The employee’s pay period rate of accrual calculated as of the year end date.

  • Carry Over: The number of hours carried over from the previous benefit year.

  • Accrued: The year to date hours accrued.

  • Used: The year to date hours used.

  • Balance: Current balance of time off remaining ((Carryover + Accrued) - Used).

  1. Click Print to print the report, or Open as Spreadsheet to view the results as a spreadsheet.

a. Under the Selection Parameters section

Field Name — Description

Payroll Number — This is the default option. Enter the payroll batch number you want to run this report for or click the Payroll Number link and select the payroll batch from the Select Payroll Batches window.

b. Under the Parameters section
Field Name Description
— —
Deposit Types Specify for which Deposit Types you want to run this report from the following options: - Include Both Direct Deposit and Prenotes - Include Active Direct Deposit - Include Prenotes - shows all employees with Prenotes for ACH Processing. > Note: Note: Prenotes are a way to setup an employee’s bank account in the system, and the ACH file will contain the bank account and routing information to confirm the bank account is a valid bank account before transmitting net check amounts on subsequent payrolls.

Obtaining Time Off Carryover Loss for Employees

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Reports/Employee_Carryover_Loss.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Reports/Employee_Carryover_Loss.htm

Obtaining Time Off Carryover Loss for Employees

You can use the Employee Carryover Loss form to produce a report that displays time off carryover lost for each employee from the previous year. For example, if employees can carryover up to 40 hours of time off and an employee has 60 hours available at the end of the year, the report would display 20 hours of lost time off carryover.

Note: The report that the Employee Carryover Loss form produces does not apply to global time off.

To obtain time off carryover lost for each employee:

  1. On the Reports menu, select Employee Loss Carryover under Payroll|Reports.

  2. Select the Accrual Schedule.

  3. Select the Time Off Plan.

  4. Enter or select the As Of Date.

  5. Click Run. The Time Off Carryover Loss Report displays. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

The report columns are:

  • Employee ID: Employee ID.

  • Employee Name: Employee name.

  • Accrual Schedule: The Time Off accrual schedule.

  • Time Off Plan: The Time Off plan.

  • Carryover Lost: Amount of employee’s time off carryover lost since As Of Date.

Employee Scheduled Payments Report

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Reports/Employee_Scheduled_Payments_Report.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Reports/Employee_Scheduled_Payments_Report.htm

Employee Scheduled Payments Report

The Employee Scheduled Payments Report displays, for each applicable employee:

  • Payments scheduled for a specific future date.

  • Payments that are repeated each pay period during a specified time period, as entered on the Scheduled Payments form.

Procedure

To run the report:

  1. Select a Detail Sort to specify the way information displays and sorts on the report: you can sort by Employee Name, Employee ID, Pay Code, or Pay Description.

  2. Enter the Scheduled Payments Selection filters to filter the report down to a specific Payment Status or set of Scheduled Pay Codes.

  3. Enter some Report Filters to further refine the data that displays on the report. For example, if you enter a Location, the Location Name displays, and the report displays data for that location.

  4. Click Run.

[Image: screenshot]

Report Output

[Image: screenshot]

The report columns are:

  • Emp ID: Employee ID.

  • Employee Name: Employee name.

  • Pay Code: The paid code entered.

  • Pay Description: The pay description used to identify the pay type.

  • Start Date: The pay period start date.

  • End Date: The pay period end date.

  • Deduction Period: The deduction period specifies a particular time during the pay period when the deduction occurred.

  • Payment Status: The status specifies when the scheduled payment occurred.

  • Amount: The amount paid to the employee.

  • Add to 401K: The value that displays specifies whether the payment was a 401(k) contribution.

  • Move to T/S: The value that displays specifies whether a reimbursement or fringe pay code was moved to the detail line on the payroll Voucher Earning Detail form when the payroll initialized.

Note: Note: The values in these columns are typically the employee “home” assignments, unless the SCHEDULED-PAYMENTS-CHANGE-DEFAULTS feature code is enabled in System Parameters. In this case, these columns may also display modifications to “home” assignments that are specific to the time sheet entry for that payment. For more information about editing scheduled payment assignments, see Establishing Scheduled Payments.

  • Dept: Department code associated with the payment.

  • Loc: Worksite location code associated with the payment.

  • Div: Division code associated with the payment.

  • Proj: Project code associated with the payment.

  • Phase: Phase code associated with the payment.

Fax Back Report

The Fax Back Report displays employee payroll information formatted and including header and memo information for fax transmissions. Use the Fax Back Report form to determine what information prints in the report and in what order.

[Image: screenshot]

To run the Fax Back Report:

  1. Enter the Payroll Number to run this report.

  2. Enter the number of Extra lines on breaks to include on the report, if any.

  3. Indicate the Pay Rate Display default for the report. Multiple pay rates print for clients that have multiple pay rates on the Employee Position Rate form or the Pay tab of the Employee Details form.

Note: Employees assigned the Variable Salary option in the Pay Method field on the Employee Details form displays as “VSalary” in the on-screen and .xls report output. In addition, if you select Do not show anything except hourly/salary or Show Pay Rates as hourly or salary, based on EE as the Pay Rate Display, the system treats this pay method as “Salary” for the purposes of this report. (The Variable Salary option only displays if the VARSALMETHOD custom feature code is enabled on the System Parameters form.)

  1. Specify how the report should sort:

  • Select the field to Sort By. These are entities used by the client.

  • From the Sort Field By drop-down, indicate whether the system should use the code or the description to sort the items.

  1. Enter Fax Back Header Notes that should print in the report’s header as needed. You can enter more than one line. You can also enter the substitution variables and to include the Remote Cutoff Date and Remote Cutoff Time from the payroll control record in the report.

  2. Enter a Fax Back Memo that should print on the report, if any. You can enter more than one line.

  3. Click Run. The report displays.

To include employee deductions in the report, you must enter the Custom Feature Code FAXBACKDEDN in System Parameters; see Maintaining System Parameters.

When this custom feature code is in place, you can suppress employee deductions for individual clients by selecting Suppress Deductions on Faxback in the Report Print Options form, accessed from the Actions menu

[Image: screenshot]

in Client Details; see Using Report Print Options.

FLSA Classification Analysis Report

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Reports/FLSA_Classification_Analysis_Report.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Reports/FLSA_Classification_Analysis_Report.htm

FLSA Classification Analysis Report

Your organization would use this report to determine whether employees are classified correctly.

FLSA types are intended only to indicate which FLSA test employees in this position are subject to. This is for the purpose of reporting and, in the future, warning purposes. An FLSA type of “exempt” indicates that there is no compensation test for this position. In other words, any employee with such a position satisfies the FLSA compensation tests regardless of their compensated. This selection does not replace or alter the FLSA Exempt field functionality.

[Image: screenshot]

  1. Enter the Selection Parameters to determine what displays on the report. If left blank, all employees display:

  • Enter each Position Classification in the order you want them to display on the report. The Description displays.

  • Select each FLSA Type in the order you want them to display on the report.

  • Standard: The position satisfies standard duties test, or is exempt from duties test but still subject to standard salary test.

  • Highly Compensated: The position satisfies the highly compensated duties test only.

  • Exempt: The position is exempt from the duties and salary tests (such as teachers, doctors, and lawyers). FLSA Exempt must be selected on Position Classification.

  • Select a Pay Group. The Description displays.

  • Select Yes for FLSA Exempt to show employees that are FLSA exempt. If you have not selected FLSA exempt and an FLSA type on Position Classification, the report applies Standard type.

  • Select Yes for Salaried to show employees whose pay method is Salary or Variable Salary.

Note: The Variable Salary pay method option only displays if the VARSALMETHOD custom feature code is enabled on the System Parameters form. (See Establishing and Maintaining Employee Pay Information.)

  • Click the Payroll Number field to select posted (COMP) payrolls. The Show only employees with zero pay field displays after selecting a payroll number. Click this field to ensure the report only displays employees who had zero pay for the selected payroll number.

  1. If you want to treat commissioned employees like salaried employees on the report, select Treat Commissioned as Salaried.

  2. Click Run.

The following report example displays all employees associated with a position classification:

[Image: screenshot]

The following report example displays all employees associated with a payroll number:

[Image: screenshot]

The report columns are:

  • Employee Name: Employee name displays as last name first.

  • ID: Employee ID

  • Position Classification: The employee’s classification for reporting purposes

  • Salaried (Y/N): Pay method is salary

  • Pay Group: The employee’s payment sequence.

  • FLSA Type:

  • S = Standard: The position satisfies the standard duties test, or is exempt from the duties test but is still subject to standard salary test.

  • H = Highly Compensated: The position satisfies the highly compensated duties test only

  • E = Exempt: The position is exempt from the duties and salary tests (such as teachers, doctors, and lawyers)

  • FLSA Exempt: FLSA Exempt must be selected on Position Classification

  • Annual Pay: Total pay for the year

  • FLSA Threshold: The annual compensation amount necessary, per FLSA type, to qualify as an exempt employee

  • Difference: Annual Pay subtracted from FLSA Threshold when Annual Pay is less then FLSA Threshold

  • Pct% Difference: Percent difference between FLSA Threshold and Annual Pay

  • Misclassified: Displays Y for employees who might be misclassified, N for employees who are classified correctly, or B if the FLSA standard can only be met if the employee is also compensated with non-discretionary bonus or incentive pay in addition to their base salary in the system. Displays O (Over Threshold) if the position earns enough to be flagged as FLSA exempt, but is not. This may or may not be an error, depending on your system setup.

FLSA Exempt Compensation Report

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Reports/FLSA_Exempt_Compensation_Report.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Reports/FLSA_Exempt_Compensation_Report.htm

FLSA Exempt Compensation Report

As of December 1, 2016, the Department of Labor has increased the compensation thresholds necessary for FLSA exemption. For employees subject to the standard compensation test, these regulations allow employers to make up as much as 10% of the FLSA exemption requirement in any quarter with non-discretionary bonus, incentives, or commission pay within the quarter or first pay period thereafter.

This report tests whether an FLSA exempt employee was sufficiently compensated or if additional compensation is necessary to meet the respective FLSA standard. You can use it for single pay periods, quarterly, or yearly analysis.

The report applies either the standard compensation or highly compensated employee test. The standard test applies to any employee with a job / position classification without an FLSA exemption test type set (“FLSA Type”), as well as those set to standard.

[Image: screenshot]

  1. Enter the Selection Parameters to determine what displays on the report:

Enter either the Pay Periods Ending Date range, a Quarter, or a Payroll Number. It is critical to capture scheduled pay periods in a quarter to know how much the employee should have been compensated.

  • Enter a Pay Periods Ending On or After date for the pay periods start date you want to review. Enter a Pay Periods Ending On or Before date for the pay periods end date you want to review.

  • Select a Quarter for the pay periods you want to review.

  • Click the Payroll Number field to select posted (COMP) payrolls. The Show only employees with zero pay field displays after selecting a payroll number. Click this field to ensure the report only displays employees who had zero pay for the selected payroll number.

  1. Select an FLSA Type, either Standard or Highly Compensated.

  2. State - Select the Work State of the employee/s from the drop-down for the Pay Period, Quarter or the Payroll Number. Leave this field blank if you want to display employees from all states for the Pay Period, Quarter or the Payroll Number.

  3. Minimum Standard Salary - For Standard FLSA Type, enter the minimum salary here.

  4. Minimum Highly Compensated Salary - For Highly Compensated FLSA Type, enter the minimum salary here.

Note: Note: Depending on whether the employee is paid weekly, biweekly, semi-monthly or monthly, PrismHR will divide this Minimum Salary by 52 or 26 or 24 or 12 to get the Period Minimum. The Period Minimum multiplied by Pay Per Date Range (5 for a 5 day work week) will provide the Total Compensation Expected on the FLSA Exempt Compensation Report. The difference between the Total Compensation Expected and the Actual Total Compensation is the Deficiency on the FLSA Exempt Compensation Report.

  1. Select a Pay Group. (The Description displays after making this selection.)

  2. Click Run to display the report on-screen.

  3. Click Close to close this form at any time.

The report columns are:

  • Employee Name: Employee name displays as last name first.

  • ID: Employee ID

  • Hire Date: The date the employee was hired.

  • Status: Employee status; the report lists any employee who was active for any portion of the date range.

  • Position Code: The employee’s job.

  • Work State: The state where the employee works.

  • Pay Group: The employee’s payment sequence.

  • FLSA Type: Either S (standard) or H (highly compensated)

  • FLSA Exemption Category: If an employee’s Position is marked as FLSA Exempt on the Employee Details form and has an associated FLSA Exemption Category indicated therein, it will now reflect in this report.

  • Pay Period: The employee’s pay cycle, whether that is weekly, biweekly, semimonthly, or monthly.

  • Period Salary: The employee’s annualized salary, as entered in PrismHR, per the appropriate pay cycle.

  • Period Minimum: The amount of compensation required each pay cycle for an employee to retain exemption.

  • Pay Per in Date Range: The number of scheduled, regular pay periods, that the employee was included in, with a period end date falling in the date range selected.

  • Total Compensation Expected: The period minimum multiplied by the number of pay periods in the date range.

  • Actual Total Compensation: Gross pay amount from all vouchers multiplied by the number of pay periods in the date range.

  • Deficiency: The total compensation expected minus actual total compensation; any employee that is at or over the FLSA threshold will have a 0 in this column.

Important notes about this report:

  • When run over multiple pay periods, this report will not indicate if an employee was appropriately compensated in a specific pay period.

  • The report does not validate when a payment is made. The non-discretionary bonus or incentive pay should be paid in a timely manner (for standard employees that would be by the first payroll after the end of the quarter).

In order for “makeup compensation” to reflect accurately in this report, it must be issued in a separate payroll batch with a period end date in the quarter to which payment is attributed. If it is paid in a subsequent scheduled payroll batch after quarter end, it will not display in this report.

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Reports/Gross-To-Net_Register_Report.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Reports/Gross-To-Net_Register_Report.htm

Gross-To-Net Register Report

This report provides a summary of the employee voucher, including all pay and deductions.

[Image: screenshot]

To run the report:

  1. Enter the Selection Parameters to determine what displays on the report:
  • Enter the Payroll Number to run this report for a specific payroll. To run the report for a date range, enable the Enter a Pay Date Range option and then a Start Date and End Date.
  1. Select the Sort Parameters:

  • Set the Primary, Secondary, and Tertiary Sort By categories.

  • Select the Detail Sort to specify the way information displays and sorts.

  • Detail w/Break Totals: This option is the default. The report will include a break and sub-total for each of the sort options entered as well as a report total.

Figure 108: Gross-To-Net Register Report

[Image: screenshot]

The report information that displays in the columns of the report:

  • Employee ID

  • Last Name, First Name, and Middle (middle initial)

  • Code: The code applied (for example, pay, tax, or benefit).

  • Pay Description: The description of the code.

  • Type: Pay (P-number) or Deduction (D-number). The number indicates how many of each Type (Pay or Deduction) were on the voucher.

  • Hours: Hours paid for the pay period.

  • Units: Units paid for the pay period.

  • Rate: The employee unit rate.

  • Hours Paid: Total amount paid for hours worked prior to deductions.

  • Unit Paid: Total amount paid for units worked prior to deductions.

Under the Employee ID and Last Name:

  • Division: Employee’s division.

  • Department: Employee’s department.

  • Location: Employee’s location.

  • Project: The project the employee is assigned to.

  • Position: The employee’s position.

At the bottom of the report:

  • Summary for Voucher: The voucher number for the payroll.

  • Pay Date: The date the employee is paid.

  • Gross Pay: Total amount paid to the employee prior to deductions.

  • Expenses: Employee’s expenses for the voucher.

  • Gross Earnings: The employee’s earnings once Expenses have been subtracted from Gross Pay.

  • Deductions: Employee deductions for the voucher.

  • Taxes: Employee taxes for the voucher.

  • Net Pay: Employee pay once Deductions and Taxes have been subtracted from Gross Pay.

Invoice Variance Report

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Reports/Invoice_Variance_Report.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Reports/Invoice_Variance_Report.htm

Invoice Variance Report

This report compares the amounts allocated in one client’s invoice to the amounts allocated in another invoice for the same client, displaying the amounts for each by Invoice Line Item and Bill Code, the differences between the invoices, and the difference (in percentage) between each amount.

Note: Note: The Invoice Line Items and Bill Codes that display in the report are based on the client’s current Bill Format, which is set on the Billing tab on the Client Details form.

Invoice Variance Report Form

[Image: screenshot]

Report Parameters Panel

The Report Parameters panel consists of the following fields:

Field Description
Zero Line Suppress This field consists of the following options: - Use Client’s Billing Format (default): The Invoice Line Items that have zero amounts will display or be suppressed based on the Billing Format setup. - Show All Detail Lines: Displays all Detail Lines, including zero amounts, regardless of the Billing Format setup. - Suppress All Zero Amount Lines: Suppresses all zero amount Detail Lines regardless of the Billing Format setup.
  • Use Client’s Billing Format (default): The Invoice Line Items that have zero amounts will display or be suppressed based on the Billing Format setup.
  • Show All Detail Lines: Displays all Detail Lines, including zero amounts, regardless of the Billing Format setup.
  • Suppress All Zero Amount Lines: Suppresses all zero amount Detail Lines regardless of the Billing Format setup. | Show Bill Code Details | Allows you to display additional lines in the report as follows: - If you select this checkbox, an additional line displays in the report for each Bill Code associated with each Invoice Line Item. (This field is checked by default.) - If unchecked, only the Invoice Detail Lines display. |
  • If you select this checkbox, an additional line displays in the report for each Bill Code associated with each Invoice Line Item. (This field is checked by default.)
  • If unchecked, only the Invoice Detail Lines display. | Show Sub-Totals | This field is only available if the Invoices being compared contain Sort Items. If Invoice One has Sort Items, the option will be available, and the default will be checked. When you run the report, in addition to the comparison at the Invoice Total level, each level of Sort Item displays a Sub-Total. If unchecked, only the Invoice Total displays in the report. (Note: To include Sub-Totals, both Invoices must contain the same Sort Items.) | | Page Break on xxx | This field is only available if Invoice One contains an Invoice Break and the Break Item is one of the Sort Items. The description that displays reflects the Break Item that triggers the page break. (The default is unchecked, which does not create any extra page breaks.) If you check this option, the report creates a page break after each Sub-Total for the Break Item in Invoice One. | ## Invoice Panels

The following Invoice panels display in the Invoice Variance Report form:

  • Invoice One: The controllinginvoice in this process. (The sub-totals and page breaks are based on the settings in this invoice.)

  • Invoice Two: The variance invoice.

Note: Note: Sub-Totals and Page Breaking are controlled by the data in Invoice One and cannot be included in the report if Invoice Two has different Invoice Sort Items.

Both panels consist of the following fields:

Field Description
Payroll Number Payroll Number associated with the invoice to be used in the report. The payroll must be successfully initialized for an invoice to be available for comparison. (The default is the client’s current payroll.) The Payroll Number has an associated Search/Lookup. The Lookup displays all payrolls for the client that have an associated invoice. Clicking the Payroll Number field displays the Payroll Search dialog, which contains the following information: - Payroll Number - Pay Date - Payroll Type - Description - Payroll Status You can refine the search using the following options: - Pay Date - Payroll Type - Description (Note: For Scheduled Payrolls, the Pay Group is included in the Description.) - Payroll Status
  • Payroll Number
  • Pay Date
  • Payroll Type
  • Description
  • Payroll Status
  • Pay Date
  • Payroll Type
  • Description (Note: For Scheduled Payrolls, the Pay Group is included in the Description.)
  • Payroll Status | Invoice | The invoice(s) associated with the payroll: - If there is no invoice available, an error displays after entering/selecting the Payroll Number. - If there is only one invoice available, the field defaults to that invoice. - If there are multiple invoices available, select the invoice from the drop-down list. |
  • If there is no invoice available, an error displays after entering/selecting the Payroll Number.
  • If there is only one invoice available, the field defaults to that invoice.
  • If there are multiple invoices available, select the invoice from the drop-down list. ## Running the Invoice Variance Report

Note: Note: This report is only available for Service Providers.; however, you can enable this report for Worksite Managers and Trusted Advisors by setting the WSMWTAINVVARRPT custom feature code at the system level. (See Using Custom Feature Codes.)

To run this report, do the following in the Invoice Variance Report form:

  1. Select the options in the Report Parameters panel.

  2. Enter or select the Payroll Number for Invoice One, then select it for Invoice Two. The following information displays:

  • Description (Note: This is the description for the payroll from Payroll Control.)

  • Pay Date

  • Payroll Type

  • Payroll Status

  1. A grid displays the Period Start and End Date data. If the Payroll Type is Manual, the grid displays:

  • Employee ID

  • Employee Name

  • Period Start

  • Period End

For all other Payroll Types, the grid displays:

  • Pay Group

  • Pay Group Description

  • Period Start

  • Period End

  1. In the Invoice field, accept the invoice associated with the payroll or select another invoice for Invoice One and Invoice Two. The following information displays:

  • Invoice Status: An invoice can be Initialized or Posted. (Note: Initialized Invoices are associated with a payroll still being processed. If changes are made to the payroll, these changes can have an effect on the invoice.)

  • Invoice Date: The date of the invoice.

  • Billing Template: The template used to determine how the billing for the invoice was created.

  • Invoice Total: The total amount of the invoice.

  • Invoice Break: The break item used in the invoice for page breaking. The following conditions have an effect on page breaking in the report:

  • The Invoice Break on Invoice One affects the Page Break option in the report; for example, if Invoice One has Invoice Break set to Department, then the Page Break on Department option will be available or, if Invoice One does not have an Invoice Break, then the Page Break option will not be available (or display).

  • If the Invoice Break for Invoice One is not one of the Invoice Sorts in Invoice One, the Page Break option will not be available (or display).

  • If Invoice One and Invoice Two have different items set for Invoice Break, the item on Invoice One will be the break item used in the report and displayed as the Page Break option.

  • Invoice Sort(s): A list of the Sort Items being used on the invoice for allocating amounts. The Sort Item(s) have the following effects on the sub-totaling and page breaking:

  • If there is no Sort Item(s) on Invoice One, there can be no sub-totaling or page breaking and neither option, (Show Sub-Totals and Page On), will display.

  • If the Break Item for Invoice One is not one of the Sort Item(s), there can be no page breaking and the Page Break option will not display.

  • If the Sort Item(s) are not the same on both invoices, there can be no sub-totaling or page breaking. The options will display, but if selected, a warning message displays after running the report and both options are ignored.

  • Bill Client: The Bill Client Company Number and Name associated with the invoice.

Note: Note: Long client names are truncated to 40 characters.

  • Employer: The Employer Number and Name associated with the invoice.
  1. Click Run. A new window opens, which displays the report results.

Invoice Variance Report Results

[Image: screenshot]

The report provides the following data:

Data Description
Line Items and Bill Codes Based on the client’s current Bill Format (set on the Billing tab in the Client Details form)
Invoice Amounts Amounts allocated to each line item display for both invoices (Invoice One and Invoice Two). Note the following: - Negative amounts are represented by a negative number. - Zero amounts are represented by a dash.
  • Negative amounts are represented by a negative number.
  • Zero amounts are represented by a dash. | Variance Amount | Difference between Invoice One and Invoice Two. Note the following: - Negative amounts are represented by a negative number. - Zero amounts are represented by a dash. |
  • Negative amounts are represented by a negative number.
  • Zero amounts are represented by a dash. | Variance Percentage | Percentage of the difference between the invoices. Note the following: - Negative amounts are represented by a negative number. - Zero amounts are represented by a dash. |
  • Negative amounts are represented by a negative number.
  • Zero amounts are represented by a dash. | Count Items | Five count lines display after the Invoice Detail Lines for the Invoice Totals: - Employee Voucher Count: Total number of employee payroll vouchers billed. - Employees Paid: Number of employees paid. - Checks Printed: Number of employee checks created. - Garnishment Checks: Number of garnishment checks created. - Direct Deposits: Number of employees paid via direct deposit instead of a printed check. Note: These count items only display in the Invoice Total section of the report, not in any of the Sub-total sections. |
  • Employee Voucher Count: Total number of employee payroll vouchers billed.
  • Employees Paid: Number of employees paid.
  • Checks Printed: Number of employee checks created.
  • Garnishment Checks: Number of garnishment checks created.
  • Direct Deposits: Number of employees paid via direct deposit instead of a printed check. | Suppressed Zero Lines | For a Line Item to be suppressed, both Invoice Amounts must be zero. If either invoice has an amount for the detail line, the line will be included in the report. Note the following: - If Zero Line Suppression is based on Use Client’s Billing Format, the zero lines that are suppressed will be based on the Print if Zero setting on the Billing Format. - If Zero Line Suppression is set to Show All Detail Lines, all line items from the Billing Format will be displayed, regardless of the Print if Zero setting. - If Zero Line Suppression is set to Suppress All Zero Amount Lines, only line items from the Billing Format that have an amount for at least one of the invoices will display, regardless of the Print if Zero setting. |
  • If Zero Line Suppression is based on Use Client’s Billing Format, the zero lines that are suppressed will be based on the Print if Zero setting on the Billing Format.
  • If Zero Line Suppression is set to Show All Detail Lines, all line items from the Billing Format will be displayed, regardless of the Print if Zero setting.
  • If Zero Line Suppression is set to Suppress All Zero Amount Lines, only line items from the Billing Format that have an amount for at least one of the invoices will display, regardless of the Print if Zero setting. | Show Bill Code Details option | - If this box is checked, a detail line will be included in the report (under each Invoice Line Item) for each of the Bill Codes defined for that line in the Billing Format. The rules for Suppressed Zero Lines apply to each of the Bill Codes defined for each line item on the invoice. - If this box is unchecked, only Line Items will display and individual Bill Code detail will be suppressed. |
  • If this box is checked, a detail line will be included in the report (under each Invoice Line Item) for each of the Bill Codes defined for that line in the Billing Format. The rules for Suppressed Zero Lines apply to each of the Bill Codes defined for each line item on the invoice.
  • If this box is unchecked, only Line Items will display and individual Bill Code detail will be suppressed. | Show Sub-Totals | - If this option is checked, in addition to the Invoice Total details, the report displays a Sub-Total section for each Sort Item associated with the invoices. - Each detail line in each sub-total section follows the Suppress Zero Lines and Show Bill Code Details options, as described above. |
  • If this option is checked, in addition to the Invoice Total details, the report displays a Sub-Total section for each Sort Item associated with the invoices.
  • Each detail line in each sub-total section follows the Suppress Zero Lines and Show Bill Code Details options, as described above. | Page Breaks | If this option is checked, a page break is triggered for each change to the item controlling the Invoice Break from Invoice One. | ========================================================================

Identifying Employees with Pay On-Demand Accounts

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Reports/Pay_On_Demand_Account_Report.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Reports/Pay_On_Demand_Account_Report.htm

Identifying Employees with Pay On-Demand Accounts

The Pay On-Demand Account Report, available from the Operations Payroll|Report menu, allows you to generate a report that lists all employees who have pay on-demand accounts and which of those accounts are active or inactive.

Note: Note the following:

  • This form uses Client Access Group security.

  • Service providers and worksite managers can only view employees who they are allowed to access.

  • The Pay On-Demand Account Report link does not display for users whose roles are set to INQUIRY or DENY for the Pay On-Demand Account Report form.

  • If you view the Pay On-Demand Account Report before clicking Generate File but after selecting a Vendor Type in the Pay On-Demand Processing form the file generation fails and the following error message displays, “There were no Pay On-Demand vouchers to be processed for <vendor>,” even if there are vouchers available to process.

  • If you re-select the Vendor Type and generate the file again without viewing the Pay On-Demand Account Report, the system completes the process.

To run this report:

  1. Select Pay On-Demand Account Report in theReports menu under Operations Payroll|Report.

  2. Enter or select the Client ID.

  3. Select the Account Status. (Note: The default is All.)

  4. Click Run. During a short delay, the system builds the data. (Note: If you enter or select a Client ID and no pay on-demand accounts are found, a confirmation message displays, “No items to print on this report.”)

The report only displays those employees who have pay on-demand accounts that are active or inactive. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Note: Click XLS to download the report.

The report columns are:

Column — Description

Client ID — The ID associated with the client.

Employee ID — The ID associated with the employee.

Employee Name — The name of the employee associated with the pay on-demand account.

Transit Number — The transit number associated with the pay on-demand account.

Account Number — The account number associated with the pay on-demand account. (Note: This number is masked on the report.)

Vendor — The vendor associated with the pay on-demand account.

Status — Identifies whether the pay on-demand account is active or inactive.

Pay Period Time Off Report

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Reports/Pay_Period_PTO_Report.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Reports/Pay_Period_PTO_Report.htm

Pay Period Time Off Report

This report provides a listing of employees’ time off by payroll and year-to-date. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: A warning message displays when you access this form, “The most recent Payroll must be posted for this report to display accurate data.” Click OK to continue, then run the most recent payroll to ensure the system posts accurate data in this report.

To obtain a listing of employees’ time off:

  1. Enter the Selection Parameters to determine what displays on the report:

  • Enter the Payroll Number to run this report for a specific payroll.

  • Select Department to display.

  • Select Division to display.

  • Select Location to display.

  • Select Project to display.

  • Select Shift to display.

  • Select Totals Only to display only the grand total.

  1. Click Run. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

The report columns are:

  • Employee Name: Employee name displays as last name first.

  • Accrued Thru: The date when the employee stops earning time off.

  • Year Ending: The date the year ends.

  • Plan Description: The description of the paid time off plan.

  • Accrual Rate: The rate at which the employee earns time off.

  • Carry Over: The hours the employee carrier over from last year’s earnings.

  • Pay Period Accrued: The hours accrued in a pay period.

  • Pay Period Used: The hours used in a pay period.

  • Year-to-Date Accrued: The hours that were accrued year-to-date.

  • Year-to-Date Used: The hours used year-to-date.

  • Balance: The remaining hours that can be used.

To generate the Payroll Tax Report:

  1. Complete the following:
Field Name Description
Tax Type Specify whether to view Both Employer & Employee, Employer Only, or Employee Only tax types in the report output: - Both Employer & Employee: Includes all tax codes regardless of the option selected in the Paid By field on the Tax Deductions form. - Employer Only: Only includes tax codes when the Paid By field on the Tax Deductions form is set to Employer. - Employee Only: Only includes tax codes when the Paid By field on the Tax Deductions form is set to Employee.
  • Both Employer & Employee: Includes all tax codes regardless of the option selected in the Paid By field on the Tax Deductions form.
  • Employer Only: Only includes tax codes when the Paid By field on the Tax Deductions form is set to Employer.
  • Employee Only: Only includes tax codes when the Paid By field on the Tax Deductions form is set to Employee. | Payroll Number | Enter the payroll number for which you want to run this report or click the Payroll Number link to select it from the Select Payroll Batches window. |
  1. Click Run. The report output displays. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Payroll Status Report

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Reports/Payroll%20Status%20Report.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Reports/Payroll Status Report.htm

Payroll Status Report

Use this form to generate a report to show the statuses of the various payrolls based upon a user-defined cut-off date or pay date range for all the clients.

Note: Note: Client Access Group Security is enabled on this form.

To access the form, click Reports. Under Operations Payroll|Report, click Payroll Status Report.

To generate the Payroll Status Report:

  1. Complete the following:
Field Name Description
Run By Enable one of the following options: - Cutoff Date: Enter or select an end date by which the hours need to be entered into the system. (Leave this field blank to include all dates.) - Pay Date Range: Enter or select a pay date range. (Leave these fields blank to include all dates.) Note: The values must be entered in date format. In addition, the start date cannot occur after the end date and the end date cannot occur before the start date.
  • Cutoff Date: Enter or select an end date by which the hours need to be entered into the system. (Leave this field blank to include all dates.)
  • Pay Date Range: Enter or select a pay date range. (Leave these fields blank to include all dates.) | Payroll Step | Select specific payroll steps. (Leave this field blank to include all payroll steps.) Note: Selected steps do not display in the report header. |

  1. Click Generate Report. The report displays.

  2. Click XLS to download the report.

  3. Click Close to close the report.

The on-screen/downloadable report includes the following columns:

  • Client ID: The client ID.

  • Name (Client Name): The name of the client for the corresponding payroll number.

  • Payroll Number: This is the batch ID or the batch number.

  • Cutoff Date: The date by which the hours need to be entered into the system.

  • Cutoff Time: Time by which the hours need to be entered into the system.

  • Cutoff Complete: Whether or not the hours have been submitted.

  • Pay Date: The date the payroll was paid.

  • Ship Date: The date the payroll is sent out by the PEO to the clients.

  • Deliver Date: The date the payroll is received by the clients.

  • Payroll Status: The last step that was performed on that payroll batch as on the Cutoff Date.

  • Step Date: The date on which the last step was performed.

  • Step By: The user name who performed the last step.

Payroll Audit Report

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Reports/Payroll_Audit_Report.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Reports/Payroll_Audit_Report.htm

Payroll Audit Report

You can use the Payroll Audit Report to review a payroll before it is finalized and posted.

After payroll has been initialized/calculated, the report compares the current payroll against the prior payroll and displays changes, outliers, and potential issues that warrant review.

The Payroll Audit Report helps reduce the amount of time spent on manual payroll review and also helps payroll processors quickly identify what may have changed since the last pay period.

Important! The output recorded in the Payroll Audit Report is generated using artificial intelligence (AI), so ensure you review all output for accuracy, completeness, and appropriateness before using it.

Accessing the Payroll Audit Report

You can access the Payroll Audit Report on two forms after a payroll has been initialized/calculated:

  • SuperBatch: The report displays with the other reports in the SuperBatch review workflow. (Click [Image: screenshot] in the batch row. Payroll Audit is the first item in the payroll review menu that displays.)

  • Process Payroll: In the Selected Payroll panel, select Payroll Audit Report. (This button displays when the selected payroll status is INITCOMP, INITOK, or INITWARN.)

Generating the Payroll Audit Report

To generate the Payroll Audit Report:

  1. Go to the Payroll Audit Report.

  2. The information for the selected Payroll Number displays. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

  1. The following information displays in the Payroll Audit Report for the selected payroll:
Section Description
Payroll Header The top of the report displays summary information about the payroll: - Pay Date - Cycle Status: Payroll type, which is regularly scheduled, manual, or special - Pay Period - Pay Group - Period Number - Deduct Period - Weeks Worked: Number of work weeks - Employees: Number of employees included in the payroll Below the Payroll Header, a quick summary displays the Total Gross, Taxes, Deductions, and Estimated Net for the payroll.
  • Pay Date
  • Cycle Status: Payroll type, which is regularly scheduled, manual, or special
  • Pay Period
  • Pay Group
  • Period Number
  • Deduct Period
  • Weeks Worked: Number of work weeks
  • Employees: Number of employees included in the payroll | Records | Select Records to display an Overview of issues the system has identified that may need attention, such as Pay Issue, DD Change, DD Reversal, and Zero Earnings. You can select each item and navigate directly to the relevant section of the report. | | Earnings Snapshot | Displays an earnings snapshot, which compares the prior payroll to the current payroll. This snapshot includes the Employee Count, Total Earnings, Cash Earnings, Total Hours, Net Pay, Total Deductions, and percent changes between the two periods. | | Employee Analysis | Displays the following information: - Earnings Outliers: Employees with significant pay changes, such as a 100% drop in pay. - Statistical Outliers: Employees with zero earnings and employees with the largest dollar changes from the prior payroll. |
  • Earnings Outliers: Employees with significant pay changes, such as a 100% drop in pay.
  • Statistical Outliers: Employees with zero earnings and employees with the largest dollar changes from the prior payroll. | Compensation Details | Provides the following information: - Earnings by Code: A breakdown of all pay codes used in the payroll. New pay codes that were not present in the prior payroll are flagged for review. - Tax Withholding: A breakdown of taxes with percent changes from the prior payroll. - Shift-Coded Earnings: Any shift differentials employees have, with percent changes. - Hours & Rate Flags: Identifies employees whose hours differ significantly from the prior payroll. |
  • Earnings by Code: A breakdown of all pay codes used in the payroll. New pay codes that were not present in the prior payroll are flagged for review.
  • Tax Withholding: A breakdown of taxes with percent changes from the prior payroll.
  • Shift-Coded Earnings: Any shift differentials employees have, with percent changes.
  • Hours & Rate Flags: Identifies employees whose hours differ significantly from the prior payroll. | Deductions & Benefits | Displays deduction and benefit changes that meet a configured percentage threshold. (Only employees with changes exceeding the threshold display in this section.) | | Banking & Payments | Displays payment and fraud review information: - No Net Pay: Lists employees who have no net pay in the current payroll. - Direct Deposit Changes: Flags direct deposit banking changes made during the pay period, which helps identify potential fraud, such as multiple employees changing direct deposit information on the same day. - Payment Method Breakdown: Displays how employees in the payroll will be paid, whether by check, direct deposit, or other method. - Top Earners: A breakdown of the highest-paid employees in the payroll, with any percentage changes in their pay flagged for review. |
  • No Net Pay: Lists employees who have no net pay in the current payroll.
  • Direct Deposit Changes: Flags direct deposit banking changes made during the pay period, which helps identify potential fraud, such as multiple employees changing direct deposit information on the same day.
  • Payment Method Breakdown: Displays how employees in the payroll will be paid, whether by check, direct deposit, or other method.
  • Top Earners: A breakdown of the highest-paid employees in the payroll, with any percentage changes in their pay flagged for review. | Billing & Invoice | Details billing items relevant to PEO clients, including workers comp billing, admin fees, workers comp changes, and miscellaneous billing, such as pending client bills. An Invoice Comparison at the bottom of the report allows processors to verify the billing totals before finalizing payroll. | | Audit Log | Select Audit Log to display all data changes made for the client during the pay period. | | Warnings & Errors | Select Warnings & Errors to list payroll errors and warnings, consolidating the information that also displays in the SuperBatch form into one place. | | Actions | Select Actions to display a selectable list of items flagged for attention, similar to the Overview section but focused on items most likely to require follow-up. | ========================================================================

Payroll Cash Requirement Report

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Reports/Payroll_Cash_Requirement_Report.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Reports/Payroll_Cash_Requirement_Report.htm

Payroll Cash Requirement Report

The Payroll Cash Requirement Report provides a listing for all cash requirements for a specified payroll.

Note: You can run this report for all payrolls, those that are posted and those that are initialized but not yet posted.

[Image: screenshot]

To run this report, do the following:

  1. Enter the Payroll Number you want to run for this report.

  2. Select Switch to Bundled/Unbundled format, if needed.

  3. Click Run.

[Image: screenshot]

This report displays the following information:

  • Pay Date: Date the payroll associated with this report was processed.

  • Period Start and End Date: Start and end dates for this payroll. If there are multiple start and end dates, then the earliest Period Start date and the latest Period End date displays.

  • Report columns: The Item Description, Total Cash Requirement, the amount Invoiced by Service Provider, and the amount Retained by Client for Future Funding display the following information:

Field Description
Net Pay The net amount for the payroll.
Deductions The deductions taken in the payroll.
Taxes Withheld The taxes withheld from the payroll.
Employer Contribution Employer contributions for benefits included in the payroll.
Provider Fees Provider fees deducted from the payroll.
Grand Total The totals for all amounts in the report.

Payroll Check Journal Report

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Reports/Payroll_Check_Journal_Report.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Reports/Payroll_Check_Journal_Report.htm

Payroll Check Journal Report

This report provides employee payroll check details, including the pay method, check/deposit, check date, start/stop period, workers compensation class, employee ID, and net pay. (This report is part of the Payroll Initialization reports.)

To access the form, clickReports menu. Under Payroll|Report, click Payroll Check Journal Report.

Note: You can also access the Payroll Check Journal Report for a selected payroll in the Approval Payroll Reports form. To do this, select Approval Payroll Reports in the View Report/Analytic field on the Payroll Approval form, then select Payroll Check Journal in the Report Title column.

To set up the parameters for this report:

  1. Enter the Selection Parameters to determine what displays on the report:
  • Enter the Payroll Number to run this report for a specific payroll or select Enter a Pay Date Range to enter a Start Date and an End Date to run this report for a date range.
  1. Set the Sort Parameters:

  • Select the Primary Sort for the report.

  • You can select a Secondary Sort and Tertiary Sort.

  • Select the Detail Sort (Employee Name, Employee ID).

  1. Select the Report Parameters as needed:
Field Description
Report Type Select the Report Type: - Detail with Break Totals: Includes a break and a sub-total for each of the sort options entered (except employee name), as well as a grand total for all employees. - Detail only: Includes the detail information without sub-totals, only a grand total for all employees. - Summary only: Does not include details, but only sub-totals for each of the sort options entered (except employee name) as well as a grand total for all employees.
  • Detail with Break Totals: Includes a break and a sub-total for each of the sort options entered (except employee name), as well as a grand total for all employees.
  • Detail only: Includes the detail information without sub-totals, only a grand total for all employees.
  • Summary only: Does not include details, but only sub-totals for each of the sort options entered (except employee name) as well as a grand total for all employees. | Report Format | Select the Report Format (Standard, With Summarized Fees and Taxes, With Bundled Billing). | | Sort on Codes instead of Descriptions | Select to sort by pay code rather than pay description. | | Page Break on Primary Sort | Select to start a new page for a new Primary Sort. | | Suppress Pay Group in Header | Select to exclude the Pay Group, Pay Period Start, and End Dates in the report header. |
  1. Select the Other Parameters as appropriate:
Field Description
Employee Unique ID Select the Employee Unique ID to use in the report (Employee ID, Employee Number).
Display Pay Codes Using Timesheet Detail Format Select to display the same detail as the time sheet and voucher.
Include Expense Reimbursements Select to include expense reimbursement pay codes.
Include Non-Cash Pay Codes Select to include non-cash as well as cash pay codes.
Include ‘Employee Total Expense’ on Report Select to include the Employee Total Expense, which is the sum of all pay and contributions.
Employee Unique Clock Number Select which “clock number” to use in the report: - Employee Number: The report obtains the employee number from the payroll voucher. - Employee Clock Number: The report obtains the clock number from the employee details.
  • Employee Number: The report obtains the employee number from the payroll voucher.
  • Employee Clock Number: The report obtains the clock number from the employee details. | Suppress Employee Names on the Report | Select to exclude employee sort names from the report. | | Consolidate Report Totals by Pay Code Only | Select to display the totals by pay code, rather than detail lines. | | Exclude Check Detail Information | Select to exclude detailed check information (check number, check date, and period start and end dates). | | Split Hours and Units Columns | Select to display columns for Paid Hours and Paid Units. Paid Hours specifies pay codes with pay reason set to hours and Paid Units specifies pay codes set. |
  1. Enter the Report Filters to display on the report:
  • Enter the field type. The field label displays. For example, if you enter a Location, the Location Name displays. The report displays records for that Location.
  1. Click Run. The Payroll Check Journal Report displays. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Listed are samples of the report columns, based on selections in the form:

  • Sort-By Criteria: The field selected in the Primary Sort.

  • Employee Name: Employee name displays as last name first.

  • Pay Method: The method in which the employee is paid.

Note: Employees assigned the Variable Salary option in the Pay Method field on the Employee Details form displays as “Salaried” in the on-screen and .xls report output. (The Variable Salary option only displays if the VARSALMETHOD custom feature code is enabled on the System Parameters form.)

  • Chk/Deposit: How the check was issued to the employee.

  • Check Number: The number on the check.

  • Check Date: The date the check was issued.

  • Period Start: The date the pay period started.

  • Period End: The date the pay period ended.

  • WkComp Class: The employees Workers’ Compensation Class.

  • Employee ID: Employee ID

  • Net Pay: The net pay on the check.

  • Pay Description: The pay code description.

  • Hours/Units: The number of hours or units for the pay period.

  • Pay Rate: The employee’s rate of pay.

  • Amount: The employee’s amount of pay for the selected date range or payroll batch.

  • Deduction Description: The deduction code description.

  • Amount: The amount of the deduction for the selected date range or payroll batch.

  • Contribution Description: The contribution code description.

  • Amount: The contribution amount for the selected date range or payroll batch.

  • Summary Only: Does not include details, but only sub-totals for each of the sort options entered (except employee name) as well as a grand total for all employees.

  1. Set the Other Parameters:

  • Select Sort on Sort Parameters Descriptions to sort the report by the descriptions instead of the codes selected as the Sort Parameters.

  • Select Page Break on Primary Sort to start a new page for the selected Primary Sort items.

  • Select Suppress Zero Deductions to exclude deductions with a value of zero from the report.

  • Select Suppress Zero Vouchers to exclude payroll vouchers with a total of zero from the report.

  1. Set the Compact Format Parameters (if this is a Compact report format):

  • Select Include YTD Amounts to include the year-to-date amounts for pay, deductions, and taxes on the report.

  • Select Include Employer Contributions to include the employer’s contribution amounts for deductions on the report.

  • Select Add employee arrears to employer amount to include employee arrears as part of employer contribution amounts on the report.

  • Select Sort Pay by Pay Code Descriptions to sort the pay by the code descriptions instead of the pay codes.

  • Indicate the order in which to Sort Deductions by:

  • Deduction Code: Sorts deductions by Deduction Code.

  • Deduction Description: Sorts by Deduction Code Descriptions.

  • Benefit Plan, Deduction Code: Sorts by the Benefit Plan ID associated with the deduction, if any, then the Deduction Code.

  • Benefit Plan, Deduction Description: Sorts by the Benefit Plan ID associated with the deduction, if any, and then by the Deduction Code Description.

  • Select Use LANDSCAPE Format and one or both of its associated parameters, Include YTD Amounts and Include Employer Contributions, to control landscape output form selection.

Note: If you do not select one of these parameters, the system uses the standard report size, even if the Use LANDSCAPE Format field is selected. In addition, you cannot use this parameter with the Suppress Rate Column parameter.

  • Select Suppress Rate Column and Include YTD Amounts to suppress the Rate column in the report output, which provides enough display room to accommodate larger YTD amounts and their commas. (This parameter is only available in Portrait format. If you enable the Use LANDSCAPE Format parameter and the Suppress Rate Column parameter a warning displays, “Cannot select Landscape with Suppress Rate Column option.”)

Note: The Include Employer Contributions parameter is not available with the Suppress Rate Column parameter. If you enable the Includes YTD Amounts and the Suppress Rate Column parameters with that parameter a warning displays, “Cannot select Include Employer Contributions with Suppress Rate Column option.”

  • Select Suppress Non-Cash Fringe Pay Codes to exclude non-cash fringe pay codes, which helps differentiate between what is actual pay and what is non-cash fringe pay.
  1. Set the Header Options:

  • Select Include Client ID to include the client’s ID in the report’s header

  • Select Include Client Legal Name to include the client’s legal name in the report’s header

[Image: screenshot]

  1. Enter the Report Filters to display on the report:
  • Enter the field type. The field label displays. For example, if you enter a Location, the Location Name displays. The report displays records for that Location.

[Image: screenshot]

Listed are samples of the report columns, based on Standard format:

  • Employee Name: Employee name displays as last name first.

  • Employee ID: The Employee ID displays when the report is run in compact format.

  • Address: Employee Residential Address

  • Title: Employee Position Title

  • Status: The employee’s employment status (for example, Active or On Leave).

  • Type: The employee’s employment type (for example, Full-Time or Part-Time).

  • EEO: The employee’s position EEO class.

  • Employee ID: Employee ID

  • Dept: The employee’s assigned department.

  • W/C: The employee’s assigned workers’ compensation class code.

  • FLSA: The employee’s FLSA type (for example, Standard, Highly Compensated, or Exempt).

  • PayGrd: The employee’s pay grade based on their position title.

  • Salary: The employee’s compensation amount based on the pay group.

  • Hire: The employee’s last hire date.

  • Term: The employee’s termination date, if any.

  • Review: Date of employee’s last review.

  • Employee No: Employee Number

  • Gender: Employee Gender

  • DOB: Employee date of birth

  • Tax Filing Info:

  • Type: Type of tax filing (for example, Federal, AR, AZ).

  • Status: Status of tax filing

  • Add’L: Additional codes associated with that tax type.

  • Direct Deposit:

  • Account No: Employee Bank Account Number

  • Tran/ABA: Employee Bank Transaction Number

  • CHK/SAV: The employees (C) checking or (S) saving account where the pay amount is deposited

  • $/%: The amount or percentage that is deposited. Balance displays when it is the last deposit or only deposit.

  • Earnings:

  • Type: Pay Code and Description

  • Current: the pay amount for this pay period.

  • MTD: Month-to-date pay

  • QTD: Quarter-to-date pay

  • YTD: Year-to-date pay

  • Deductions:

  • Type: Deduction Description

  • Current: The deduction amount for this type during this pay period.

  • MTD: Month-to-date deduction

  • QTD: Quarter-to-date deduction

  • YTD: Year-to-date deduction

  • Disbursements:

  • Voucher No: Voucher Number

  • Check No: Check Number

  • Check Amount: The amount of this check

  • Direct Deposit Amount: The amount that is direct deposited for this check/voucher.

  • Paid Time Off:

  • Description: Paid Time Off Description

  • CarryFWD: The amount of paid time off carried forward.

  • Accrued: The amount of paid time off accrued in this pay period.

  • Used: The amount of paid time off used in this pay period.

  • Balance: The amount of paid time off available after this paid period.

  • Grand Total: Total for all employees.

  • Total Employee Count: The number of the employees included in the report.

[Image: screenshot]

Listed are a sample of the report columns, based on Compact format:

  • Employee Name: Employee name displays as last name first.

  • Emp ID: Employee ID

  • Dept: Employee department

  • Net Amt: Net pay amount for this pay period.

  • DD Amt: Direct deposit amount

  • Check Amt: Check amount

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Reports/Payroll_Retirement_Contributions_Report.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Reports/Payroll_Retirement_Contributions_Report.htm

Payroll Retirement Contributions Report

Use the Payroll Retirement Contributions Report form to run a report on contributions made to employee retirement accounts. This report can be run using calculated payrolls that are either initialized or posted.

Note: Note:

  • Service Provider Only.

  • Does not use Client Access Group security.

To access the form, clickReports menu. Under Payroll|Report, click Pay Retirement Contribution Report.

Show me an example of the Payroll Retirement Contributions Report form:

Figure 129: Payroll Retirement Contributions Report

[Image: screenshot]

  1. Enter the Selection Parameters to determine what displays on the report:

  • Enter the Payroll Number to run this report for a specific payroll or click the select

  • Enter a Start Date and an End Date to run this report for a date range.

  1. Set the Sort Parameters:

  • Select the Primary Sort, Secondary Sort, and Tertiary Sort categories.

  • Select the Detail Sort to specify the way information displays and sorts on the report (Employee Name, Employee Unique ID).

  1. Set the Report Parameters:

  • Select the Report Type:

  • Detail w/Break Totals: Includes a break and a sub-total for each of the sort options entered (except employee name), as well as a grand total for all employees.

  • Detail Only: Includes the detail information without sub-totals, only a grand total for all employees.

  • Summary Only: Does not include details, but only sub-totals for each of the sort options entered (except employee name) as well as a grand total for all employees.

  • Select Sort on Sort Parameters Descriptions to sort the report by the descriptions instead of the codes selected as the Sort Parameters.

  • Select Page Break on Primary Sort to start a new page for the selected Primary Sort items.

  • Select Suppress Pay Group in Header if needed.

  1. Select Other Parameters as appropriate:
  • Select the Employee Unique ID from the drop-down (Employee ID, Employee Number).
  1. Enter the Report Filters to display on the report:

  • Select the Type Class you want to include in the report from the drop-down.

  • Enter the field type. The field label displays. For example, if you enter a Location, the Location Name displays. The report displays records for that Location.

  • Employee Elective Contributions: The employee’s contributions.

  • Employee Catch Up: Employee catch up amounts paid.

Generating the Payroll Validation Report

This report provides a listing of validation errors for the selected payroll number. In addition, you can download the error messages to an Excel file in .csv format.

Note: You can also generate the Payroll Validation Report from the Selected Payroll panel on the Process Payroll form. See the Payroll Processing Guide for more information.

To generate the Payroll Validation Report:

  1. Select Payroll Validation Report on the Payroll|Report menu. The Payroll Validation Report form displays.

  2. Select a Payroll Number.

  3. Click Generate Report. The validation errors, if any, display on-screen. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

  1. Click Download Report. In the window that displays, click the downloaded report link in the lower left side of the window. The report displays in Excel where you can save it in .csv format.

Payroll Voucher Report

You can use the Payroll Voucher Report form to generate the Payroll Voucher Report for a selected client or pay date, so you can review voucher details before posting and reconciling against source data. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: This report is available for initialized and posted payrolls with the INITOK, INITCOMP, POSTCOMP, or COMP status.

To generate the Payroll Voucher Report:

  1. Go to the Payroll Voucher Report form on the Payroll|Report menu. The current Client ID displays.

Positive Pay File Report

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Payroll/Reports/Positive_Pay_File_Report.htm Path: PD/Payroll/Reports/Positive_Pay_File_Report.htm

Positive Pay File Report

This report displays positive pay per checking account, file stub code, or date range.

  1. Enter the Selection Parameters to determine what positive pay files are included in the report:

  • Enter the Checking Account to list positive pay files for just one checking account; if left blank, the report displays the file information for all checking accounts.

  • Enter the File Stub to list positive pay files for just one file stub code; if left blank, the report displays the file information for all file stub codes.

  • Enter the Date Created to list positive pay files for just that date; if left blank, the report displays the file information for all dates.

  1. Click Run.

The report columns:

  • Checking Account / File Stub: The account ID (or file stub) and name for the checking account.

  • Output File Name: The file name output from the system.

  • Date Created: The date the file was created.

  • Time Created: The time the file was created.

Note: Note: All dates and times in PrismHR are Central Time.

  • Number of Checks: The number of checks in the file.

  • Number of Voids: The number of voids in the file.

  • File Type: Value specifies whether the file is an Original or Recreated file.

  • Original File Name: If the file is recreated, the original name for the file displays.

  • Total Amount: The total dollar amount of the checks in the file.

  • Total Voids: The total dollar amount of the voids in the file.

Field Name Description
Starting Date Enter the starting date of the reporting period. This date must be the first date of the month.
Ending Date Enter the ending date of the reporting period. This date must be the last date of the month.
Employer ID This field is optional. Leave this field blank to report for all employers. If you want to run this report for specific employers, enter the employer IDs for whom you want to run this report here or click the Employer link and select them from the Select Employer dialog box.
Include Corporate Clients By default, this field is set to Yes. - Select Yes to include clients with the service type field set to Corporate or Staffing. - Otherwise, select No.
  • Select Yes to include clients with the service type field set to Corporate or Staffing.
  • Otherwise, select No. | Tax Authority | This field is optional. Leave this field blank to report for all tax authorities. This could either be a state, county or city tax authority. If you want to run this report for specific tax authorities, enter the codes for the tax authority IDs for whom you want to run this report here or click the Tax Authority link and select them from the Select Tax Authority ID dialog box. | | Tax Identifier | This field is optional. Leave this field blank to report for all tax identifiers. Leave this field blank- to run this report for all clients. If you want to run this report for a specific client, enter the client ID for whom you want to run this report here or click the Client ID link and select it from the Select Client dialog box. | | Client Category | This field is optional. Leave this field blank to run this report for all Client Categories. If you want to run this report for a specific client category, enter the category code here or click the Client Category link and select it from the Select Categories dialog box. | | Cost Center | This field is optional. Leave this field blank to run this report for all cost centers. If you want to run this report for a specific cost center, enter the cost center code here or click the Cost Center link and select it from the Select Cost Centers dialog box. | | Separate Resident/Work-Based City Taxes? | This field is optional. By default this option is unchecked. To use this option, you must use tax identifier 31 to change the format of the report. > Note: Note: If Separate Resident/Work-Based City Taxes? field is checked and Tax ID is not set to 31, an error will display. To run the report you must either uncheck theSeparate Resident/Work-Based City Taxes? field or enter Tax ID 31. | | Report Only Employees with Taxable Wages Less than or Equal to zero | This field is optional. By default this field is unchecked. Check this field if you want to show only employees with negative or zero pay. Else leave this field blank. | | Include Resident Location Geo/Description and Work Location Geo/Description | This field is optional. By default this field is unchecked. Check this field is you want to add resident and work geocode and descriptions to the report. Else this field blank. | | Conversion Vouchers | Select from the following options: - All Vouchers - This is the default option. This will generate the report based on all vouchers. - Only Conversion - This will generate the report based only on conversion vouchers. - Only Non-Conversion - This will generate the report based only on non-conversion vouchers. |
  • All Vouchers - This is the default option. This will generate the report based on all vouchers.
  • Only Conversion - This will generate the report based only on conversion vouchers.
  • Only Non-Conversion - This will generate the report based only on non-conversion vouchers. | Show if Tax Auth Equals | This field is optional. Leave this field blank to report for all tax authorities. This could either be a state, county or city tax authority. If you want to run this report for specific tax authorities, enter the codes for the tax authority IDs for whom you want to run this report here or click the Show if Tax Auth Equals link and select them from the Select Tax Authority ID dialog box. > Note: Note: This field will be used as an additional tax parameter to further help filter for specific values. As an example, you can enter a tax authority of 00 and a tax code of 15, but then use this attribute to only show vouchers that both include 00-15 and the authority you enter on this field. | | And Other Tax ID = | This field is optional. Leave this field blank to report for all tax identifiers. If you want to run this report for specific tax identifiers, enter the tax identifiers for the type of taxes to be reported or click the And Other Tax ID link and select them from the Select Tax Identifier ID dialog box. > Note: Note: This field will be used as an additional tax parameter to further help filter for specific values. As an example, you can enter a tax authority of 00 and a tax code of 15, but then use this attribute to only show vouchers that both include 00-15 and the tax identifier you enter on this field. | | Include Corporate Clients | This field will display only if the EXCLCORPTX custom feature code is activated on the System Parameters form. (By default Yes is selected.) - Select Yes to include clients with the service type field set to Corporate or Staffing. - Otherwise, select No. |

This will generate the report based on all vouchers. - Only Conversion - This will generate the report based only on conversion vouchers. - Only Non-Conversion - This will generate the report based only on non-conversion vouchers. |
  • All Vouchers - This is the default option. This will generate the report based on all vouchers.
  • Only Conversion - This will generate the report based only on conversion vouchers.
  • Only Non-Conversion - This will generate the report based only on non-conversion vouchers. | Show if Tax Auth Equals | This field is optional. Leave this field blank to report for all tax authorities. This could either be a state, county or city tax authority. If you want to run this report for specific tax authorities, enter the codes for the tax authority IDs for whom you want to run this report here or click the Show if Tax Auth Equals link and select them from the Select Tax Authority ID dialog box. > Note: Note: This field will be used as an additional tax parameter to further help filter for specific values. As an example, you can enter a tax authority of 00 and a tax code of 15, but then use this attribute to only show vouchers that both include 00-15 and the authority you enter on this field. | | And Other Tax ID = | This field is optional. Leave this field blank to report for all tax identifiers. If you want to run this report for specific tax identifiers, enter the tax identifiers for the type of taxes to be reported or click the And Other Tax ID link and select them from the Select Tax Identifier ID dialog box. > Note: Note: This field will be used as an additional tax parameter to further help filter for specific values. As an example, you can enter a tax authority of 00 and a tax code of 15, but then use this attribute to only show vouchers that both include 00-15 and the tax identifier you enter on this field. |

Third Party Sick Pay is an amount provided to an employee by a third party (for example Aflac Insurance Company). Field — Description

Adjustment Date Above or Equal To — Enter the start date to be used for this adjustment. This will be used to derive the tax year, quarter and month to be adjusted.

Adjustment Date below or Equal To — Enter the end date to be used for this adjustment. This will be used to derive the tax year, quarter and month to be adjusted.

Employer ID — Enter the Employer ID affected by this adjustment.
